Over 1 600 instances: **169 complete answers (159 OPT, 10 UNSAT), every one with a proof VERIFIED by
veripb 3.0.2 and none REJECTED**; 501 incumbents; **543 REFUSED**, of which 388 the width wall
(D-0028, an `objective` or a counter declared over 10⁴ to 2·10⁹ values), 145 the 8 GiB heap budget
(M7-T8), 9 a repeated variable in `fzn_global_cardinality` (gcc.ml, community-detection in 2017,
2021 and 2026), 1 an unbounded `var int`; 14 more died of memory past the width warning, and 25 did
not flatten (MiniZinc 2.10 on 2015–2024 models, or over 1200 s). Baguette is last in 13 editions and next to last in 3 (2012,
2016, 2026), always above the one entrant that was itself the year's tail. The years it did best
(2016, 2024, 2012) are the years with the fewest refusals, not the years with easier instances.

**What the calibration says.** Our Chuffed's status agrees with the official Chuffed on 90 to 99
instances per edition (78 in 2013, where the official flatten failed 20 times); the node is 1.6 to
2.3x faster than the Challenge machine from 2021 on and about equal or slower before (2013–2017,
2019–2020). So the ranks from 2021 are, if anything, flattering on time splits; baguette's rank never
turns on them (the smallest gap to the entrant above is 5 points in 2019, every other gap is 15 to
260 points of quality).

**Reading, and what it points at.** Three quarters of the lost ground is decided before search
starts: the order encoding over the declared objective width, and the heap that encoding costs. A
bounded objective (`objective` views, or a lazily grown ladder, the M7 width discussions) and a
heap budget that scales with the box would turn 533 of the 543 refusals into attempts; what those
attempts would score is the next measurement, not this one. The free category (`-f`) was not run.

## D-0122  M7-T26, what the 1 600 Challenge instances ask for, against what baguette propagates natively; and a word on the comparison itself

**Status**: **MEASUREMENT**, recorded 2026-11-02 (agent-mznc), by `tools/compare/challenge_globals.py
~/mznc-archive bench/challenge <runs>` over the sixteen runs of D-0105 to D-0121.

**The comparison is not like for like, and D-0121 should be read with that in mind.** Every
Challenge entrant runs without proof logging; baguette has no such mode (D-0046) and every row of
D-0105 to D-0121 was produced writing a VeriPB 3.0 proof. The order encoding that makes the proof
possible is also what the width wall (388 refusals) and the heap budget (145) are made of. So the
ranks measure "baguette with its proof against solvers without one", which is the standing the
project wants to know, but a gap to the entrant above is not a gap in search alone.

**Vocabulary, because it was misread once.** A harness `REFUSED` is the FRONT END refusing the
FlatZinc before any search (exit 2 or 3: a declared width over the cap, the heap budget, a
`fzn_global_cardinality` with a repeated variable, a `var int` with no inferable bound). It is not a
proof refused by the checker, which would be `check_verdict REJECTED`; across the 169 complete
answers of the sixteen editions that count is 0.

**The census** (instances using the global, out of 1 600; outcome of baguette on them; `complete%`
is OPT+UNSAT over the instances attempted, i.e. not refused and flattened):

| global | instances | native | REFUSED | OPT+UNSAT | incumbent | TIMEOUT, no solution | complete % |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| natives only, or none | 614 | | 181 | 58 | 233 | 120 | 14 |
| cumulative | 241 | yes | 125 | 20 | 43 | 34 | 20 |
| alldifferent / all_different | 299 | yes | 89 | 15 | 86 | 90 | 8 |
| count family | 192 | no (D-0097 withdrawn) | 91 | 13 | 69 | 18 | 13 |
| diffn | 140 | no | 68 | 17 | 22 | 26 | 26 |
| table | 135 | no | 61 | 9 | 28 | 29 | 13 |
| **regular** | 110 | no | 16 | **0** | 24 | **70** | **0** |
| circuit | 95 | no | 31 | 6 | 18 | 32 | 11 |
| value_precede(_chain) | 105 | no | 54 | 2 | 32 | 1 | 5 |
| **inverse** | 70 | no | 20 | 4 | 1 | **44** | 8 |
| **bin_packing_load** | 65 | no | 48 | **0** | 17 | 0 | 0 |
| global_cardinality(_low_up) | 110 | yes | 40 | 5 | 36 | 29 | 7 |
| **global_cardinality_closed** | 30 | **no** (gcc + a domain restriction) | 0 | 1 | 3 | **26** | 3 |
| member | 40 | no | 19 | 1 | 0 | 20 | 5 |
| nvalue | 40 | no | 14 | 15 | 8 | 3 | 58 |
| lex_less / lex_lesseq / lex_greatereq | 95 | no | 5 | 17 | 56 | 17 | 19 |
| var set of | 35 | no | 17 | 1 | 7 | 8 | 6 |

**Reading.** On the instances that reach search, the baseline (natives only) completes 14 %, and
the decomposed globals sort into three groups. Those that are plainly killing the search: `regular`
(0 of 94 attempted, 70 of them time out without a single solution), `inverse` (44 of 50 attempted
time out empty), `member` and `global_cardinality_closed` (46 of 51 empty), `bin_packing_load` (0
complete). Those that do about as well as the baseline through the standard decomposition: `table`,
`circuit`, `diffn`, `count`, the lex family. And those that are better than the baseline, so not a
priority: `nvalue`, `at_most`/`at_least`, `network_flow_cost`, `maximum`. Two of the first group
are cheap: `global_cardinality_closed` and `_low_up_closed` are gcc over a closed value set, one
mznlib line each onto gcc.ml plus the domain restriction; `member` is a disjunction of equalities
over a `View`. `regular` and `inverse` are propagators to design, with their proof stories
(`regular` unfolds to a layered graph whose arcs are clauses over order literals, the natural
object for a `rup`-based justification; `inverse` is element both ways). `circuit` and `table`
stay where M4-T6 left them: decomposition is competitive here, so a native one is a speed row,
not a reach row.

The same join over the 543 refusals changes nothing in D-0121's conclusion: 181 of them are on
models with no decomposed global at all, and they are width and heap wherever they fall.

## D-0123  M7-T27, the wall is memory, in three places, and the objective's width is not one of them

**Status**: **MEASUREMENT**, recorded 2026-11-02 (solo-m7t27). Reproduce with
`python3 -I tools/compare/refusal_causes.py /scratch/arthur/m7t26 --widths` on `fataepyc-06`,
over the sixteen run directories of D-0105 to D-0121. **Rewrites the premise of the M7-T27
roadmap row**; decides nothing about the encoding, and says why that decision comes last.

### The recount

D-0121's "388 width, 145 heap" came from the `detail` column of `results.tsv`, which keeps the
first 180 characters of stderr. The width WARNING (M7-T1) is printed first, so every later death
inherited the word "width". The Challenge runs passed **no** `--max-order-width` (D-0065's default
is unlimited; `scripts/compare_run.sh` passes `--max-heap-mb` only), so a refusal by declared width
was not possible. Reading the whole stderr:

| what ended the run | instances |
|---|---|
| exit 5, `--max-heap-mb` exhausted (8 GiB, M7-T8) | **520** |
| exit 3, `fzn_global_cardinality` with a repeated variable (M7-T29) | 19 |
| exit 2, OCaml `Out of memory` before the guard | 3 |
| exit 2, `var int` with no inferable bound (M7-T29) | 1 |

### The 520 heap deaths, split by the guard's own message

The heap message says how many ladder clauses were minted and, when the synchronous check inside
`declare_int` fired, which variable was being declared; the asynchronous `Gc` alarm names none.

| family | n | where the heap went | evidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| **A** 0 clauses minted | 14 | the front end, before the first `declare_int` | `.fzn` of 360–850 MB; 26–48 s |
| **B** after the encoding, no variable named | **347** | rows, propagator set-up, or the SEARCH | 45 s to 1 196 s of wall; 114 had minted under 10⁶ clauses, which cannot cost 8 GiB |
| **C** inside a ladder loop | 159 | the ladders themselves | p50 25.7 M clauses at death ≈ **300 bytes of heap per rung**; the named variable is an `X_INTRODUCED` in 106 cases, never `objective` |

**The objective is never the variable being declared at death (0 of 159).** Over the 495 refused
models with an objective: it is the single widest variable in 324, but its share of the SUMMED
declared width is ≥ ½ in only **84** and ≥ 0.9 in 71. An objective-only remedy (a view over a
narrow carrier, a bounded ladder for it) reaches at most those 84 and none of family B.

### Four instances re-run under a 60 GB budget (fataepyc-06, `--stats`, `--time-limit 300`)

| instance | summed width | what happened |
|---|---|---|
| 2012 pattern-set-mining-k1_mushroom (28 MB `.fzn`) | 8 122 | encoding alone: **1.0 GB, 44 s**; then **≈1.2 GB per search node**, 8.9 GB at 300 s, 77 nodes, 1 solution |
| 2018 team-assignment_data1_6_24 | 532 134 | 3 solutions, a 307 MB `.pbp` at 300 s |
| 2015 mapping_mesh3x3_mpeg_2 | 4.3 M | encoding complete (4.29 M clauses, 18 warned variables), then **dead at 60 GB in search**, 0 solutions |
| 2022 wordpress_Wordpress11_Offers500 | 26.3 M | a **3.0 GB `.opb`**; killed at 600 s **still propagating the root** (0 decisions), 45 GB RSS |

pattern-set-mining **without `--proof`** uses the same memory (5.8 GB after 4 nodes, 65 615
propagator runs, against 5.9 GB with the proof), so the growth is in `lib/core`, not in the
writer. That model has exactly one long row, the sum of 8 124 Booleans that defines its
objective. A `Linear` pruning's reason is one fact per OTHER term of the row, snapshotted
eagerly because I-X6 forbids reading live state (`linear.ml`, "per-term snapshot"), so a row
that prunes k of its n terms in one fixpoint retains k·n snapshots: **quadratic in row length,
per node**. `docs/GCS-COMPARISON.md` named this shape ("GCS's pre-refactor `ReasonFunction`")
and expected the cost; this is its first measurement at Challenge scale.

### What this changes

1. **M7-T27 is three rows, in this order of payoff**, not one design question about the
   objective. (a) The explanation memory of family B: one snapshot per row per fixpoint instead
   of one per pruning, or a counting reason for unit-coefficient Boolean sums, without touching
   I-X6, with a decision record because the reason shape is a contract. (b) The encoding memory
   of family C: `Encoding.rev_constraints` holds every `.opb` row as OCaml data until the file
   is written, and `consistency` is a per-value `Hashtbl` although rung ids are consecutive;
   stream the file and compute the ids, `.opb` byte-identical, no decision needed. (c) Only
   then the width itself: the Θ(w) rows and justifications D-0028 accepted, which is what is
   left on wordpress-shaped instances once (a) and (b) are done, and which D-0031 (no lazy
   ladder after the first trace line) and the comparison's refusal of a bits carrier
   constrain. (d) Family A, the front end at 15× the file size and 44 s per 28 MB, separately.
2. **More memory is not a remedy**: 7.5× the budget turned none of the four into an answer.
3. `--time-limit` is checked between nodes only, so a root propagation that never finishes
   (wordpress) ends in the harness's `timeout`, as `killed`, with no stats. Worth a line.

### What it does not decide

Which of the two reason shapes in (a) is right, and whether (c) needs a new carrier at all once
(a) and (b) have moved families B and C into attempts. Both are measurements to take after,
not before.

## D-0124  M7-T27 (a): a `Linear` pruning's reason is materialised LATER, from the trail's history, not snapshotted per term at the push

**Status**: DECIDED and implemented, 2026-11-02 (agent-reason, branch `wave40-reason`). Follows
D-0123 (sub-row (a)). Amends one sentence of D-0026; narrows nothing in I-X6, I-X9 or D-0035.
Reproduce on `fataepyc-06`: `/scratch/arthur/m7t27a/` holds both binaries and the eight runs.

### Step 1, the measurement that chose the shape

Instance `2012_pattern-set-mining-k1_mushroom` (28 MB `.fzn`), `--time-limit 60 --max-heap-mb
60000 --stats`, `OCAMLRUNPARAM=v=0x400`, binary at `9b1a230` (md5 `bb2f2779`): 4 nodes, 65 615
propagator runs, **5.84 GB** peak RSS, major heap 747 M words. A temporary counter in `linear.ml`
and `store.ml` (not kept) said where it went: **44 633 Linear runs, 8 230 prunings, 16.9 M
per-term snapshot records built, 16.9 M facts pushed, 14.9 M facts still live on the trail at
exit** -- about 2 058 records per pruning, and about **2 prunings per effective run**.

D-0123's hypothesis was right about the mechanism and wrong about the row. The 8 124-term
objective row ran 8 times in 4 nodes (1 effective run per node). The sink is the **105
`int_lin_le_reif` rows over 3 800 to 4 200 Booleans** (plus 8 123 over 98), which
`reif_lin_le.ml` compiles to two big-M `int_lin_le` rows each: 7 065 runs and 1 005 effective
runs per node, every pruning snapshotting ~4 000 terms, nearly all of them at their declared
bound and so materialising to **no literal at all**.

That number, 2 prunings per effective run, is what decided between the two shapes D-0123
named. **(ii), one shared snapshot per row per fixpoint, divides the retained records by the
prunings per run: a 2× remedy for a 25× problem.** (i), the reason holding only the row and
the trail position, retains nothing per term.

### What I-X6 forbids, and why reading the trail's history at a fixed position is not it

I-X6 forbids a thunk that reads **live** state: "forcing it later must render the derivation
as of the moment the pruning was made, not as of now". The live store is the thing that
moves. The trail below a live entry does not:

- the trail is a stack. `undo_to` pops from the top; a popped slot is overwritten with
  `dummy_entry`; every `apply` allocates a fresh record. So while the entry pushed at
  position `p` is on the trail, every position below `p` holds the **same physical record**
  it held at the push, with the same `old`, `now`, `sup_lo`/`sup_hi` and the same live
  arena id (I-T1, and the arena is truncated only by `backtrack`, to the level's mark);
- a `Store.history` is that cut: `{store; upto = p; witness = trail.(p-1)}`. Its lookups
  (`lo_at`, `hi_at`, `lo_reasons_at`, `hi_reasons_at`) walk each bound's own support chain
  (`sup_lo`/`sup_hi`, newest first) back **past** `p` before answering, so nothing at or
  after the pruning is readable through it, whatever is asked;
- `check_history` refuses, by **physical identity** of the witness, to answer once the trail
  has been unwound below `p` -- including the case where it has been re-pushed to the same
  length with other entries, which a check on positions alone would answer wrongly and
  silently. That check runs on every materialisation, from either half, and is O(1).

So a snapshot taken when the reason is finally asked for is the snapshot that would have
been taken at the push, by construction rather than by copying. The facts are the bounds as
recorded at positions below `p`, the same values the per-term record used to hold, so
**D-0035/I-X9 are untouched**: the reason still justifies the bound as recorded, the
justification is the same `Combine` over the same snapshot, and the whole model suite emits
**byte-identical `.opb`/`.pbp`** (`make check`'s determinism lane and the model tests, below).

**D-0026 amended, one sentence.** "Laziness lives in *when* the reason is materialised, not in
a closure per pruning" was written against a closure over the **live** store (GCS's
`Narrowable*`, I-X6's own failure mode). A closure over a frozen history is laziness in *when*,
with the captured environment a snapshot by I-T1. The type-level discharge D-0026 claimed
("`Reason.lits` takes no store") becomes: a `Later`'s function is handed a `Store.history` and
no store -- `Linear.justified_at`'s signature, the same move `explain_cross_conflict
~opposite` made -- plus the witness check at run time. What remains discipline is that
signature, which is what docs/INVARIANTS.md I-X6 now says.

### The decision

Shape **(i)**:

- `Reason.t` is `Facts of fact list | Later of {compute; empty}`. `because` is unchanged and
  wraps `Facts` (109 producer sites untouched); `because_later ~empty` is the new channel;
  `Reason.facts` is the one place a stored reason becomes its list. `empty` is carried so
  that `is_empty`, which `Analysis` asks per node, stays O(1); `Store.check_agreement`
  asserts it against the materialisation under `BAGUETTE_DEBUG`. **Nothing memoises**: what a
  memo would keep is exactly the per-term list this arm exists not to keep, and a reason is
  asked once by the trace and once per cut by analysis.
- `Store.history`, `history_live`, `check_history`, `lo_support_at`/`hi_support_at`,
  `lo_at`/`hi_at`, `lo_reasons_at`/`hi_reasons_at`, `history_name`, `created_domain`.
- `Linear.snapshot_at h tm` replaces the live read (`snapshot_source store` is now its
  live-history wrapper, kept for the conflict paths and `test_matrix.ml`'s probe);
  `row_snaps_at`, `justified_at`. **Prunings are deferred, conflicts stay eager**: a
  conflict's reason is consumed where it is raised and its justification forced before any
  backtrack, so there was nothing to defer.
- Consumers of a stored reason go through `Reason.facts`: `analysis.ml` (3 sites),
  `alldiff.ml` (2), `element.ml` (2), `cumulative.ml` (1), `bool2int.ml` and `analysis.ml`
  take `lits_of_facts`/`to_string_facts` on plain lists. The claim row did not name these
  files; the edits are one-line type adaptations and no other session holds them.

### Measured after (same instance, same flags; md5 before `bb2f2779`, after `469b5629`, after+`fact_at` `950317c3`)

| | before (`9b1a230`) | after (`ac7a6cc`) | after + `fact_at` (`22ae7b9`) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 60 s: nodes / propagator runs | 4 / 65 615 | 4 / 65 615 | 4 / 65 615 |
| 60 s: peak RSS | **5.84 GB** | **1.80 GB** | **1.77 GB** |
| 60 s: major heap at exit | 747 M words | 221 M words | 214 M words |
| 300 s: nodes / conflicts / propagator runs | 77 / 36 / 342 546 | 67 / 31 / 304 311 | 67 / 31 / 304 311 |
| 300 s: peak RSS | **8.71 GB** | **2.15 GB** | **2.18 GB** |
| 300 s: words allocated / promoted | 39.2 G / 5.3 G | 45.5 G / 6.7 G | 39.1 G / 5.4 G |

The 300 s pair was run twice, once beside `make check` and once on an idle node: the node
counts are identical both times (77 and 67), so the difference is deterministic, not load.
Of the 1.8 GB after, **1.0 GB is the encoding** (D-0123 family C, sub-row (b)), so the
search's share went from ≈1.2 GB per node to ≈0.2 GB per node. The search itself is unchanged
where it is comparable: at 60 s the same 4 nodes, the same 65 615 runs, the same 16 473
effective runs; `make check`'s determinism lane reports the 156 models' `.opb`/`.pbp`/stdout
identical.

**The time cost, measured and located.** Fewer nodes in 300 s (67 against 77) with 33% more
words allocated per node. A counter on `Reason.facts` (not kept) counted **146 055
materialisations of a `Later`, 526 M facts, for about 15 000 Linear entries**: the trace asks
once per entry, and the other ~130 000 asks are conflict analysis -- `Analysis.analyse
~scope:Everywhere` (the decision closure search asks for at each conflict) expands every
reachable entry including the **root-level** Linear entries, about 4 200 expansions of 3 600
facts at each of the 31 conflicts. Before, an expansion found the facts already built; now it
rebuilds them. `fact_at` (commit `22ae7b9`) takes the reason half's materialisation from 17 to
7 words per term by building the fact straight from `value_at`, which puts the words allocated
and promoted back at the baseline (39.1 G / 5.4 G against 39.2 G / 5.3 G) -- and the node
count stays at 67. So the cost is not allocation but the **walk**: 526 M history lookups per
300 s, each a support-chain step or two, about 40 s of the 300. It is paid where the closure
re-expands entries whose level is 0, which cannot contribute a decision, and that is
analysis.ml's to remove (below).

### What it does not decide

- **The decision closure at level 0.** `Analysis.decision_closure`/`~scope:Everywhere`
  expands root-level entries at every conflict; an entry at level 0 rests on level-0 facts
  only and can add no decision to the closure, so stopping the expansion at level 0 would
  remove the ~4 200 re-materialisations per conflict measured above without changing the
  closure. Not done here: analysis.ml is outside this claim, `resolutions`/`antecedents` are
  reported as stats and the change wants its own measurement. A per-conflict memo table in
  `Analysis` is the other shape; a memo on the `Later` itself is not, because what it would
  keep is the list this record exists not to keep.
- Where the remaining ≈0.2 GB per node goes (20 682 entries in 4 nodes; `bool2int`'s and the
  reif rows' own entries, the arena, the watch lists) -- not measured.
- (c) width and (d) the front end, untouched; the 1.0 GB encoding is (b).
- Whether the per-pass snapshots of `alldiff`/`gcc`/`cumulative`/`element` (one per pass,
  I-P6) want the same treatment: not measured on an instance where they dominate. The
  `Store.history` lookups are general and would serve them.
- `Trace.done_` keeps a reference to every entry it has written, overwritten only when a new
  entry lands at the same position; with a `Later` that is a closure, with the old shape it
  was the whole per-term list. Bounded by the trail's depth, not measured, worth a look.

### Addendum, M7-T27 (a2), 2026-11-02 (agent-reason, `wave40-reason2`): the closure stops at level 0 -- correct, byte-neutral, and NOT where the time went

**Done.** `Analysis.decision_closure`'s stop and postcondition are "every node above level 0 is
a root"; `~scope:Everywhere` expands levels above 0 only; a root conflict under the default
scope still resolves level 0 (1UIP at the root is unchanged). Argument: a level-0 node's
support and everything its reason cites precede every level mark, so expanding it can add
only level-0 nodes, which `decision_levels` drops. Two scenes in `test_analysis.ml` (a level-1
conflict resting on a level-0 derived fact, kept unexpanded, `decision_levels = [1]`; a root
conflict still resolved under the default scope).

**Measured, fataepyc-06, `/scratch/arthur/m7t27a2/`.** Before = merged `main` `0f93b38`
(md5 `950317c3`), after = `6ffd37b` (md5 `c8a14140`). All 156 models: `.opb`/`.pbp`/stdout
**byte-identical** between the two binaries (`art/before`, `art/after`), and `make check` ok
(156 passed, determinism lane identical, `check.log`). pattern-set-mining, 300 s,
`--max-heap-mb 60000`: before **69 nodes, 2.17 GB**, after **69 nodes, 2.17 GB**, and the
words allocated are identical to the word (40 137 974 566 both) -- so on this instance the
closure never expanded a level-0 node at all. (Run-to-run variance of the wall-clock limit:
the same `950317c3` binary gave 67 nodes earlier today and 69 now.)

**So the attribution in the main record above was wrong**, and this addendum corrects it with
the measurement (throwaway branch `wave40-reason2-measure`, counters by site, 300 s, log
`fataepyc-06:/scratch/arthur/m7t27a2/count300.err`): 58 nodes, 27 conflicts, **128 842
materialisations of a `Later`, 462.7 M facts**, of which Analysis expansions were **2 288 at
the conflict level (1UIP) and 122 033 at levels above 0 under `Everywhere`** (429.8 M facts);
the remainder (~4 500) is the trace, once per entry. Level 0 was never expanded; 1UIP is
cheap. The sink is the **decision closure resolving every non-root entry at every open level
above 0 back to its decisions, at every conflict**: a decision on this instance propagates
thousands of reif-row prunings at its level, and the levels below the conflict level persist
across conflicts, so the same entries are resolved again at each of them (~4 500 per
conflict). The closure's only consumer is `decision_levels`, i.e. the SET OF LEVELS the
conflict rests on; it does not need the facts.

**Remedy, not done here (analysis.ml/learn.ml, a decision record of its own).** Answer
"which decision levels does this entry rest on" without materialising facts: either (i) a
per-entry, lazily computed and cached set of levels (small: at most the open levels), walked
through supports rather than facts -- the cache is O(levels) per entry, not O(terms), so it is
not the retention (a) removed; or (ii) a per-conflict memo keyed by trail position for the
closure alone, which halves nothing across conflicts and is the weaker shape. The level-0
stop stays: it is correct and costs nothing, and it is the half of the argument (i) needs.

### Addendum 2026-11-06: the cap was hit by the ENCODING, not the proof, and the incumbent counts were wrong

Found while cleaning the node: the run left **2.6 TB in 161 `.opb.rows` files**, the streamed `.opb` body
of M7-T27 (b). The solver splices that file into the `.opb` and removes it (`Encoding.write_opb`,
`at_exit` in `bin/main.ml`), but a run killed by SIGXFSZ or SIGKILL never reaches either, and
`scripts/compare_run.sh` deleted `.opb`/`.pbp`/`.scp`/`.varmap` and did not know the new file. Fixed:
the harness now deletes `$L.opb.rows` on every outcome, before the evidence early-return.

What the files say, joined to `results.tsv` by instance (`rows_files.txt` + `recount.py`, laptop):

| CAPPED (148) | runs | with an incumbent | median wall | the file at 16 384 000 000 bytes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **encoding-capped** | **140** | **0** | 584 s | `.opb.rows`, no `.opb` and no `.pbp` ever written |
| proof-capped | 8 | 8 | 698 s | `.pbp`; their `.opb` median 2.8 GB (0.5–9.5) |

Plus **21 runs that are not CAPPED but left a rows file of 9.2–16.1 GB** (18 TIMEOUT, 3 ERROR): the
20 minutes ended while the encoding was still being written, no incumbent either. So **161 runs
(10 % of 1 600) never finished writing their `.opb`**, and 8 wrote a 16 GB proof.

Three sentences of the record above are therefore wrong and are corrected here, not rewritten:

1. "148 CAPPED: the proof file passed the harness's 16 GB cap at a median 652 s, with a median
   `.pbp` of 16.4 GB and `.opb` of 2.8 GB, 145 of them holding an incumbent" — the medians were taken
   over the 8 runs that had a `.pbp` and `.opb` at all; 140 of the 148 had neither. **The wall is the
   size of the ENCODING** (D-0028's Θ(w) ladder clauses and rows, written at ~28 MB/s for ten minutes),
   and the proof's size only for 8.
2. "Incumbents 675 → 994", "176 TIMEOUT with incumbent", "143 CAPPED with incumbent": the script of
   2026-11-03 tested `objective not in ("-", "")`, and the harness writes `min:-` / `max:-` for an
   optimisation run without a solution, so every optimisation attempt counted as an incumbent. With
   the value actually present: incumbents over the 1 600 instances **698 → 794** (TIMEOUT/CAPPED rows
   only: 455 → 555); of the 346 freed refusals, TIMEOUT **89** with an incumbent / 98 without, CAPPED
   **7** / 137, OPT 11, ERROR 1 / 3. The gain in incumbents is a third of what was written. The
   standings table is unaffected (`challenge_rank.py` reads the tables itself), as are REFUSED
   543 → 212, 0 REJECTED, and the status counts.
3. "This is `M8-bits-encoding`'s population, 148 instances": it is **161 encoding-size runs + 8
   proof-size runs**, and the first number is the one a bits carrier attacks directly: O(log w) bits
   and two bound rows per variable instead of w ladder clauses, so the `.opb` of these models shrinks
   by the ladder's share before any search runs. `M8-bits-encoding-T2`'s first figure should be
   `.opb` bytes at `W = 0` on these 161 (their `.fzn` are kept under `/scratch/arthur/m7t27run/*/work/`),
   not proof bytes on the D-0028 model.

`.opb` and `.pbp` of both runs and the 3.9 GB of `m7t27probe/` are deleted from the node; the `.fzn`
stay (REFUSED/ERROR inputs, what `refusal_causes.py --widths` reads).

## D-0126  M9-no-proof-T1: a solve-without-proof mode exists, as a measurement instrument

**Status**: DECIDED 2026-11-06 (agent-noproof, branch `wave41-noproof`), written before any code.
Amends `docs/SPEC.md` §1 (one paragraph added, none removed) and the premise of D-0046 and
D-0122 as stated below. M9-no-proof-T2 implements it, M9-no-proof-T3 measures with it.

### The decision

`baguette MODEL.fzn --no-proof` solves the model and writes no proof. The mode is **off by
default**, it is a measurement instrument and nothing else, and an answer it prints is not a
result in the sense of SPEC §1 ("a run that produces a correct answer with an unverifiable
proof is a failed run"): it is an unverified answer, and every harness column that holds one
says so. The sentence in `bin/main.ml`'s header, "it is the file that is optional, not the
proof", stays true of every run that does not ask for the mode.

What the mode is for is the three readings the M9 preamble names: the proof's overhead per
instance, which is the only honest reading of D-0121's standings against entrants that run
without a proof; the baseline `M8-bits-encoding-T4` needs, because an encoding's cost is what
it adds to that baseline; and attempts on the instances whose run today ends inside the
encoding. What it is not for is also said there and is not repeated: it is not a remedy for
D-0123's family B (the reasons live in `lib/core` and learning needs them), and without a
proof there is no encoding to compare.

### What it skips, and what it keeps

Skipped, each with the module that does the work today and the invariant that goes vacuous:

- the `.opb` body on disk: `Encoding.row_sink` at `Discard_rows`, which M7-T27 (b) already
  provides and `bin/main.ml` already selects when `--proof` is absent (I-X5 and I-X8 vacuous:
  there is no file to be complete and no row to be committed);
- the `.pbp`: no channel, no `Writer.t` with bytes behind it, no `conclusion` (I-X1, I-X4);
- every pruning's justification and every trace line: `Search` does not call `Justify.emit`,
  `Justify.emit_rup_clause`, `Trace.emit`, `Trace.conflict_line` or `Trace.record_citation`,
  so no `Deferred` thunk is ever forced for the proof's sake (I-X6, I-X9, I-X10, I-S4 vacuous);
- the proof side of a learned constraint's lifetime: `Learned`'s introduction and
  `Retention.retire`'s deletion, and `Justify.wipe_level`/`Writer.wipe_level` on backtrack
  (I-X3);
- the audit I-X2.

Kept, because the preamble's rule is that the mode must not become the path where
justifications rot:

- every `Explanation` (I-P4): the mutators take a `Reason.justified` and have no optional
  form, so a propagator cannot prune without one in either mode. The value is built; what
  is skipped is forcing and rendering it;
- clause learning and PB learning (`learn.ml`, `pb_analysis.ml`, `retention.ml`): they read
  reasons, not the proof, and D-0123 measured pattern-set-mining at the same 5.8 GB without
  a proof file for exactly that reason;
- the independent solution check I-S1 (`Model.check_assignment` in `bin/main.ml`), which
  never looked at the proof;
- the encoding's **accounting**: `Encoding.cost` (ladder clauses, widest declaration,
  direct values) is maintained by counters at the moment a row is minted, not by the sink,
  so `--stats` reports under `--no-proof` what the encoding would have cost;
- every front-end refusal: `Compile` and `Encoding.declare_int_gen` refuse an unrepresentable
  or over-limit width, a repeated gcc variable and an unbounded `var int` in both modes, so
  the accepted language is one language (the D-0065 argument, unchanged). A resource death
  (the heap budget's exit 5, a time limit) is what the mode measures and may differ.

### The id rule, concretely

The one design question of the milestone is how `Explanation.Model_row` ids exist without
rows. The answer is already in the code, and the rule is to keep it that way:

**Every id an `Explanation` value can carry is minted by one of two counters, both of which run
before the search starts and both of which run in both modes.**

1. **Model rows**: `Encoding.commit` (`lib/proof/encoding.ml`) does `t.n <- t.n + 1` and
   *then* looks at the sink; under `Discard` it drops the row and returns the id. Every row
   door (`add_constraint`, `add_int_lin_le`, `add_int_lin_ne`, `add_all_different`,
   `add_equality`, the reified rows) goes through it, and `Compile` stores the returned id in
   the propagator instance, where it becomes `Model_row id`. The ladder rungs are ids by
   arithmetic, `ladder_base + (value - lo - 1)` with `ladder_base = t.n + 1` taken before the
   loop, and the loop asserts it; the hole rows are committed after the ladder and their ids
   stored in `hole_rows`. So `Discard_rows` already counts, and `n_constraints`,
   `ladder_base`, `hole_rows` and every returned id are identical under all three policies.
   Nothing counting-only has to be written. T2 may short-circuit the rung loop under
   `Discard` (`t.n <- t.n + ladder` instead of committing `ladder` throw-away clauses),
   which changes no id because the ids are computed, not read back; the hole rows must still
   go through `commit`.
2. **The direct encoding**: `element` and `alldiff` cite the channelling halves by id
   (`Encoding.direct_lo_id`/`direct_hi_id`/`direct_fwd_id`) inside their `Combine`s. Those
   ids are `Writer.fresh` ids, minted by `Encoding.ensure_direct` and `derive_at_least_one`,
   and the only caller is `Encoding.start_proof`, which runs once between `Compile` and
   `Search.solve` over the names `request_direct` collected. So under `--no-proof` the run
   still builds a `Writer.t`, over a null channel with `~audit:false`, and still calls
   `Encoding.start_proof`: the counter advances in the same order from the same
   `n_constraints`, and nothing is written. After `start_proof` that writer is never emitted
   through.
3. **Everything else is a proof-only id and need not exist**: a trace line's `w_cid`, a
   justification line, a learned row's introduction, a `stated` claim. None of them is
   embedded in an `Explanation` value; they are held beside the runtime objects for the
   proof's sake. T2 may leave them unminted (an `option`, or a `Justify.ctx` whose emitting
   entries are never called). What the search must never do is read one, and that is what
   the stdout lane tests, not a rule this record can state.

A consequence worth stating: the mode skips emission, not minting. `Encoding.t` exists, its
tables are filled, `Justify.encoding` and `Encoding.is_direct_row` answer as before. What is
absent is bytes and the forcing that produces them.

### What it amends, and why the reasoning survives

**SPEC §1.** One paragraph added after "The proof is not a debugging aid"; that sentence is
kept verbatim and still governs every result. The amendment is normative on four points: off
by default, explanation values identical (the id rule), an answer under the mode is not a
result, and the gate always proves.

**D-0046** (one checker, one format). The no-proof mode is not a second format and not a
second checker; `veripb` 3.0.2 remains the sole oracle for every proof that exists. What
D-0046 feared, "a second path that nothing exercises is a place where vacuous passes breed",
is the real hazard here, and it is answered the way D-0046 answered it: the path is
exercised by the gate (T2's lane, every model, every run of `make check`), and no lane under
the mode may assert anything about a proof, because there is none to assert on. A green run
under `--no-proof` says nothing about I-X1; that is why the SPEC forbids every other test
from using it.

**D-0122** (the comparison is "not like for like"). Its caveat was correct and the mode is what
discharges it: T3 produces the standings with the proof's cost removed, which is the reading
D-0122 could not give. Its census survives untouched, because the proof is not what makes
`regular` time out empty on 70 of 94 instances; those rows are search, and the mode will say
by how much.

**The M9 preamble, one correction.** It names "attempts on D-0123's family C (the ladder
deaths)" as the third gain. After D-0125's addendum the population is larger and differently
named: 161 runs (10 % of the 1 600) never finished writing their `.opb` body, at ~28 MB/s for
ten minutes, and 16 still die inside the ladder loop. `Discard_rows` writes nothing, so the
first number is what the mode reaches directly; whether the 16 survive the loop's residual
allocation is a T3 measurement, and the short-circuit in rule 1 is the lever if they do not.

### T2's test plan (M9-no-proof-T2)

- On all 156 models, **stdout byte-identical** between `baguette M.fzn` (proof written and
  deleted, as today) and `baguette M.fzn --no-proof`: every solution, every `==========`,
  every `=====UNSATISFIABLE=====`, in `--all` order where a model is run that way. This is
  the first direct test that proof logging never steers the search. Its proved side is the
  ordinary model run, so the lane costs one unverified run per model; it belongs in the gate.
- `--stats` under the mode prints a line saying the mode is on and that no proof exists;
  `--time`'s `emit` phase reads 0.
- `--no-proof` together with `--proof PREFIX` is a usage error (exit 2), not a silent choice.
- **If stdout ever differs, that is a finding about the PROVED run**: something in `Justify`,
  `Trace` or `Writer` fed a decision, a wake or a reason. Stop and record it; do not make the
  lane pass by changing the no-proof side.
- A unit lane in `test_proof.ml` beside `test_m7t27_streamed_opb_is_byte_identical`: the same
  encoding built under `Retain_rows` and `Discard_rows` has the same `n_constraints`, the same
  `Encoding.cost` and the same ids from every row door.

### T3's measurement (M9-no-proof-T3)

Per instance, on the node, same rules as D-0125 (1 200 s, 16 GiB): wall, CPU and peak RSS
with and without the proof, so the overhead is a number per instance and a distribution per
edition, not M6-T3's "2 to 4 % of CPU" which bounds emission only; how many of the 161
encoding-size runs and the 16 ladder deaths become attempts; D-0121's sixteen standings
re-ranked with the no-proof answers, labelled unverified, beside the proved column, so the
gap to the entrant above splits into "what proving costs" and "what the search is worth".
### Addendum, M7-T27 (a3), 2026-11-06 (agent-a3, wave41-a3): the closure's levels over memoised CITATIONS, exact and byte-neutral, 67 -> 391 nodes in 300 s; the remedy as proposed (a memo of levels) would have been a superset

**Done.** `Analysis.dependency_levels store c ~vars_of` answers what `decision_levels` read off
`analyse ~scope:Everywhere ~criterion:decision_closure`, the same set for the same conflict,
and `Learn.at_conflict` reads it instead of running that walk. The walk over facts stays, as
the reference the unit tests compare against and as the `BAGUETTE_DEBUG` cross-check that
runs beside every call. `Reason.materialisations` counts the `Later` asks the addendum above
counted by hand, and `--stats` prints it as `later`; `Analysis.memo_entries`/`memo_ints` count
the memos built, printed as `cites`. Reproduce on `fataepyc-06`: `/scratch/arthur/m7t27a3/`
holds the gate log, the 2 x 468 artefacts and the runs; the clone is `/scratch/arthur/wave41-a3`.

**The design, and why it is not the one the addendum above proposed.** The first addendum's
remedy (i) was a per-entry, cached SET OF LEVELS, O(open levels) per entry, with the closure's
answer the union of the sets of the facts the conflict rests on. That union is not the
closure's answer. `Frontier` holds ONE node per bound slot (a variable and a direction) and
merges two facts on the same slot into the STRONGER one (`stronger`, M6-T16), so the weaker is
dropped without being expanded. In a bound-split search that is the common case rather than
a corner: a decision `x >= 2` at level 1 is cited by a level-1 pruning, a decision `x >= 3`
at level 2 is already in the frontier when the pruning is resolved, and `x >= 2` arrives on
`x`'s slot, loses to `x >= 3` and is never expanded. The closure names {2}; the union names
{1, 2}. The drop is sound (the cut still entails the dropped fact, so its negation is still
a nogood) and strictly better (the backjump skips level 1), and whether it happens depends on
what ELSE is in the frontier when the fact arrives, which is a property of the conflict and
not of the entry. So no per-entry set of levels reproduces the closure; a union is a
superset, sound and weaker, and a weaker backjump is a different search. test_analysis.ml's
scene 5 is that search in three variables (`x - 3w <= 0`, `x - z <= 0`, `x + w + z <= 6`, so
that `x = 3` is infeasible without any single row seeing it); the union is computed there as
the break and shown to be `[2; 1]` against the closure's `[2]`.

What IS a property of the entry alone is what the walk needs from it: its CITATIONS, i.e.
for each fact its reason read (and each fact read by the reasons of the holes its bound move
settled over, `hole_facts`' rule), the trail position that established it, with that
position's level, direction and root-ness, packed into one int. The walk over citations is
`analyse`'s walk with the facts left out, cell for cell: on one slot a later position is a
stronger bound (I-D3) and the same position is the same fact, so `stronger` is "higher
position wins, equal is a no-op"; the highest expandable cell is resolved first
(`best_expandable`, a heap); the cell is removed when expanded (`Frontier.remove`); a
decision or factless pruning is never expanded; level 0 is never entered. Citations at level
0 or without a support are not memoised at all: such a node contributes no level, and the
only node it could shadow is a weaker fact on the same slot, which sits below it on the trail
and is therefore at level 0 too. The memo lives on the entry (`Store.entry.cites`, `int array
option`, `None` until the closure first reaches the entry) and not in a side table, because
its validity is exactly the entry's life: everything below a live entry is frozen (I-T1, the
argument this record makes for `history`), so what an entry cites, at which level and whether
it is a root cannot change while it is on the trail; `Store.apply` builds a fresh record for
every push, so a popped entry's memo dies with it and nothing has to be invalidated on
backtrack. Scene 6 backjumps below a conflict and conflicts again through the same level-1
entry by another row order: the memo is the same physical array and still right. Attribution
(`entry.prop`, I-T4) is checked on every cited support at memo time and on the conflict's
own facts at every conflict, so a corrupt graph is still refused on first contact (the
mis-stamped scene of test (c) is refused both ways).

**Exact or superset.** The set is EXACT, i.e. the closure's: the same walk over the same
slots, and the gate's determinism lane and the 468 artefacts below are the measurement of
that. Two places where it is a superset by construction, both sound and both unreachable from
`lib/`: an entry that moved BOTH bounds (`Store.fix`, no caller in `lib/`) folds the holes of
both directions where `analyse` folds one node's direction, and its two cells share a
position, so the heap and `best_expandable` may expand them in either order. A superset of the
dependency levels is a nogood over more decisions than needed, which backjumps less far; a
SUBSET would skip a subtree nothing had refuted (M2-L3's finding), and nothing here produces
one, because every citation the walk over facts would have expanded is in the memo and every
merge is the same merge.

**Why the memo is not the retention (a) removed.** It is O(cited facts above level 0) per
entry, one int each, for the entries a closure reaches, filled once; what (a) removed was 7
to 17 words per term of EVERY pruning, filled at the push. Measured below.

**Measured, `fataepyc-06`, `/scratch/arthur/m7t27a3/`.** main = the gate clone `1a0cfa7`
(md5 `1d68c8c1`), after = `wave41-a3` at `ebfa888` (md5 `716a8696`; `0779772` adds the `cites`
counter, md5 `08780450`). `make check` ok in the clone: 3 488 unit checks ok, 0 FAIL, 156 model
tests passed, determinism lane identical; the model tests alone under `/usr/bin/time -v`:
15.7 MB peak RSS, 3.2 s. All 156 models under `--proof`, both binaries: `.opb`, `.pbp` and
stdout **byte-identical, 468 artefacts**, exit codes identical (`art/main.md5`, `art/a3.md5`).
pattern-set-mining, `--time-limit 300 --max-heap-mb 60000 --stats`, the (a2) command, one
binary at a time, the node otherwise carrying two other agents' single-threaded runs:

| 300 s | main `1a0cfa7` | after `wave41-a3` | after, `--proof` | main, `--proof` |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| nodes / conflicts / depth | **67** / 31 / 35 | **391** / 193 / 92 | 393 / 194 / 92 | 65 / 30 / 34 |
| propagator runs | 304 311 | 1 569 676 | 1 576 043 | 296 783 |
| `later` | (no counter; 128 842 by the addendum above) | **29 409** | 29 475 | - |
| `cites` memos / ints | - | 17 192 / 38 212 = **0.3 MB** (run `a3b_300`: 399 / 197 / 92, 2.19 GB) | - | - |
| peak RSS | 1.44 GB | 2.34 GB | 2.31 GB | 1.44 GB |
| top heap (M words) | 184.6 | 298.9 | 295.0 | 185.1 |
| words allocated / promoted | 39.0 G / 5.35 G | 49.5 G / 7.76 G | 49.8 G / 7.80 G | 38.0 G / 5.20 G |
| `.pbp` | - | - | 718 MB | 241 MB |

The materialisations go from 128 842 to 29 409 **for six times the conflicts**: 193 conflicts
materialise 29 409 reasons where 27 materialised 128 842, i.e. ~150 per conflict (the trace's
once-per-entry asks and 1UIP's) against ~4 800. The target was "nodes back toward 77": they
are 391, with the search 92 levels deep instead of 35, and an incumbent (`incumbent=8`) where
main had none. The decision closure was not 13 % of the node cost; it was most of it, and the
first measurement (D-0124, 77 against 67) under-read it because the baseline it compared
against materialised the same walk from facts already built.

**Memory, node-matched.** The 2.34 GB against 1.44 GB is the deeper tree, not the memo. At
equal depth the two binaries are within 0.2 GB: after at 90 s is 52 nodes / depth 27 / 1.49 GB
and at 120 s 97 nodes / depth 51 / 1.61 GB, against main's 67 nodes / depth 35 / 1.44 GB at
300 s and 19 nodes / depth 10 / 1.33 GB at 120 s (`a3_60`, `a3_90`, `a3_120`, `main120`). The
`cites` counter is the memo's own size over the whole run, memos that died with their
entries included: 17 192 memos, 38 212 ints, **0.3 MB**, three orders of magnitude below the
question (most cited terms are at their declared bound and are not memoised). (a)'s memory
is kept: 8.71 GB before (a) at 77 nodes, 2.19 to 2.34 GB now at 391 to 399, and the memo is
none of it. Run-to-run variance of the wall-clock limit, same binary: 391, 393 and 399 nodes.
## D-0128  M7-T27 (d): the front end streams -- family A was the token array, and the fix is a window with one lexeme of lookahead, items built as they are parsed

**Status**: **ACCEPTED**, implemented 2026-11-06 (agent-fe, `wave41-fe`). Closes sub-row (d) of
**D-0123**. Changes `lib/flatzinc/` only: `lexer.ml`, `parser.ml`, `ast.ml`, `builder.ml`, and
one test. Nothing in `core` or `proof` moves; the 156 artefacts of `test/models/` are
byte-identical (stdout, `.opb`, `.pbp`, exit status, and stderr too) between main's binary
(`1d68c8c1`) and this one (`992cd1d4`).

### The measurement, before the fix

Reproduce on `fataepyc-06` with the probes kept under `/scratch/arthur/m7t27d/probe-old-src/`
(main's four-phase pipeline) and `probe-new-src/` (this branch's three passes), each a dune
executable to drop into a checkout; the twelve `.fzn` are the Challenge's, under
`/scratch/arthur/m7t27run/<year>/work/`, and `/scratch/arthur/m7t27d/run12.sh` is the run.

D-0123 counted 14 Challenge runs dead under `--max-heap-mb 8192` with "0 clauses minted", in 25
to 47 s, on `.fzn` of 360 to 850 MB (12 remain after (a)+(b), 460 MB to 1.7 GB). A probe over the
front end's four phases, each held and then dropped, on main's `lib/flatzinc` (`fataepyc-06`,
`ulimit -v` 60 GB, a measurement and not the harness; RSS from `/proc/self/status`, live heap
after a forced major):

| phase | yumi `p_9_..._7_7_zones` (460 MB, 69.3 M tokens, 4.16 M items) | gt-sort `n9_ub10` (1.7 GB, 240.7 M tokens, 15.2 M items) |
|---|---|---|
| `read_file`: the whole file as one string | 0.4 s, 439 MB | 1.2 s, 1 618 MB |
| `Lexer.tokenize`: every token, positioned, in a list then an array | **36 s**, live **5 271 MB**, peak RSS **8 894 MB** | **125 s**, live **18 028 MB**, peak RSS **30 692 MB** |
| `Parser.parse_model`: the whole `Ast.model` | 9 s, the tree alone 1 933 MB | 34 s, the tree alone 6 996 MB |
| `Builder.build`: the `Model.t` | 16 s, 1 093 MB | 32 s, 2 873 MB; 267 s and a peak RSS of 31.4 GB for the four phases |

**The token array is family A.** Each token cost a list cell (3 words), a `lexeme` record (3), a
`Pos.t` (4) and, for an integer or an identifier, its box: about 80 bytes live per token, 100
with the list that `Array.of_list` reversed from, minted for the whole file before the parser
read the first one. 69 M tokens is 5.3 GB live and a 6.9 GB heap; the Challenge's guard fired at
8 192 MB at 25 s, inside `tokenize`, which is exactly what the probe shows at 36 s with the
forced collections. gt-sort's 241 M tokens would have needed a 30 GB RSS to get past the lexer at
all. The tree behind it (1.9 GB on yumi, about 900 bytes per item) is the second copy, alive at
the same time as the `Model.t` it is being built into; the file string (0.4 to 1.6 GB) the third.

### The decision: stream, do not shrink the tree

Two shapes were open. (1) Keep the whole-file pipeline and make it leaner: a token array of
unboxed codes, positions recomputed on demand, a packed tree. (2) Make the front end streaming,
so that nothing it holds is proportional to the file. (2) is taken, because the parser is LL(1)
and never backs up, so it needs one lexeme of lookahead and not an array; because the builder
consumes items in file order and keeps nothing of an item's syntax once it is built; and because
(1) leaves a constant factor that the next edition's 3 GB `.fzn` would spend again.

What changed, and what the module headers now say:

- `Lexer.t` reads the input through a window of 64 KiB (`of_channel`) and holds the current
  lexeme (`cur`, `pos`, `advance`). A token that straddles the window's edge is copied through a
  `Buffer`, one that does not is taken out of the window. The window's size is a parameter, and
  `test_flatzinc` lexes fifteen sources (the kitchen sink, long literals, escapes, every lexical
  error, a missing and a doubled `solve`, a truncated file) through every width from 2 to 17 and
  checks that the `Model.t` or the error with its position is the same as through the default.
  `of_string` goes through the same window, so the straddling path is the unit tests' path too.
- `Parser.iter_items` delivers `Ast.item` values (`Decl`, `Constraint`, `Solve`) in file order,
  skipping `predicate` items as before; the two rules about the model rather than an item --
  exactly one `solve`, the second refused where it stands and a missing one at the end -- live
  there. `Ast.model`, `parse_model`, `parse_string`, `read_file` and `tokenize` are gone.
- `Builder.add_item` builds each item as it arrives and `finish` closes the model. The one
  deliberate exception keeps D-0083: a constraint that arrives after a `var int` with no domain
  was declared is held as syntax until the end of the file, because its domain is inferred from
  ALL the constraints before any is built and the arithmetic family sizes its auxiliaries from
  domains. On a FlatZinc 2.x file every declaration precedes every constraint, so that is every
  constraint or none, and the deferred path is the old path minus the tokens and the tree.

### What it costs, and the one observable difference

- Lexing is faster, not slower: 6.3 s for yumi's 69 M tokens against 36 s, 21.6 s for gt-sort's
  241 M against 125 s, because nothing is retained and the minor heap does the work.
- **A file with several errors reports the first in file order.** Before, the whole file was
  lexed before the parser ran, so a lexical error anywhere (a float literal on line 10 000) was
  reported ahead of a syntax error on line 3. With one error, message and position are identical;
  the straddle test asserts that for every lexical and grammatical error the front end emits.
- **A constraint that precedes the declaration of a name it uses is now refused** with
  `undeclared identifier`, where the whole-tree builder, which applied every declaration before
  any constraint, accepted it. FlatZinc 2.x orders items (predicates, parameters, variables,
  constraints, solve); MiniZinc writes nothing else; no model under `test/models/` and no source
  in the unit tests has one. SPEC 2.1 says "FlatZinc 2.x files" and is not amended.

### After the fix

The real binaries, front end only (`--time --max-encoding-clauses 1`: the first declaration is
refused after `Builder.of_file` and before any encoding, and the `--time` report prints on that
exit path too; `fataepyc-06`, `ulimit -v` 60 GB, `/usr/bin/time -v`):

| instance | `parse` before (main, `1d68c8c1`) | peak RSS before | `parse` after (`992cd1d4`) | peak RSS after |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| yumi, 460 MB | 41.1 s | **12.8 GB** (top heap 12.2 GB) | **21.4 s** | **2.4 GB** (top heap 2.1 GB) |
| gt-sort n9, 1.7 GB | 113.8 s | **38.9 GB** (top heap 37.1 GB) | **44.7 s** | **3.5 GB** (top heap 3.3 GB) |

The front end is 2 to 2.5 times faster and uses a fifth to a tenth of the memory; what remains
is the `Model.t` (1.1 GB and 2.9 GB live) plus the store `Compile` had begun when the budget
refused it. The 2.4 GB on yumi is the probe's 1.7 GB plus `Compile.compile`'s start.

**The twelve, under the harness's exact flags** (`ulimit -v 16777216`, `ulimit -f 16000000`,
`timeout -k 30 1200 main.exe --max-heap-mb 8192 --proof`, plus `--stats --time`; one at a time on
`fataepyc-06`). Before, from the Challenge's own `results.tsv`: all twelve `REFUSED`, exit 5 at
25 to 47 s with "0 clauses minted" and no variable declared. After:

| instance | `.fzn` | `parse` | ends | at | peak RSS |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2015 largescheduling 0800-1 | 538 MB | -- | the `.opb.rows` at the **16 GB cap** (SIGXFSZ, exit 153) | 5:12 | 1.7 GB |

four rows-cap runs and the timeout show none, and their front end is bounded by the 45 s of
gt-sort n9 above.) **Family A is empty**: twelve of twelve pass the front end in 16 to 45 s and
die where D-0123's families B and C die -- four at the encoding's size on disk (D-0125's
addendum: four more of `M8-bits-encoding`'s population), three inside a ladder loop or at the
root with the encoding's heap, four in `compile` with between 2 K and 24 M clauses minted, one in
the harness's timeout still compiling. None is an attempt yet, and this row did not expect one:
D-0123 ordered the sub-rows by payoff and put (d) last. gt-sort n9 is the one to note for
`M7-T8`: with a 1.7 GB `.fzn` the reactive guard let the heap reach 13.2 GB before it acted,
5 GB past the budget, because the alarm runs at the end of a major cycle and `compile` was
allocating 14.65 M propagators between two of them.

### What it does not fix, and the number to carry forward

The front end's memory is now the `Model.t` and nothing else: 1.09 GB for yumi (3.5 M variables,
2.1 M constraints), 2.87 GB for gt-sort (577 K variables, **14.65 M `bool_clause`**, about 196
bytes each: a `constr` record with its `Pos.t` (7 words), the constructor (3), and 40 bytes per
literal for a boxed `Var i` in a cons cell). That is family B's wall, not A's, and it is
`model.ml`'s representation, shared with `compile.ml` and every propagator's set-up; it is noted
here as the next cost of the front end, not changed. The `Pos.t` per variable and per
constraint (32 bytes, 5.6 M of them on yumi) is the cheapest third of it.
## D-0127  M8-bits-encoding-T0: RUP, `pol` and elaboration measured on the checker alone, in the order and the bits encodings

**Status**: **MEASUREMENT**, recorded 2026-11-06, written up 2026-11-09 (agent-spike, branch
`wave41-spike`). Run on
`fataepyc-06` the same day, sequentially, one checker at a time, under `ulimit -v 16777216`:
`~/.cargo/bin/veripb` 3.0.2 (Rust, source d5644ca4), `veripb -e` of the same build, and
`/scratch/arthur/cake_pb` (CakePB of 2026-08-25). No solver code. The instrument is
`bench/bits_spike/` (`gen.py`, `run.sh`, `diag.sh`, `README.md` with the full tables), the table
is `bench/bits_spike/results.tsv` verbatim, the artefacts are under
`fataepyc-06:/scratch/arthur/wave41-spike/out/full/` (111 MB `.opb` and 28 MB `.pbp` at the top
width; not in the repo).

### The question, and the model it was asked on

T1 has to decide how a justification is WRITTEN before `encoding.ml`, `justify.ml` and
`ladder.ml` learn a second representation: as one `rup` line the checker closes by unit
propagation, or as the explicit `pol` our writer emits today. The user's prior was that `pol`
elaborates better, because a `rup` has to be reconstructed by the elaborator before a verified
checker can see it. Both arms of M8 were to be measured with the SAME derivation, over a database
of 10³ to 10⁶ rows.

The derivation is D-0028's two-variable shape, made satisfiable so that every `red`, `pol` and
`rup` is judged (D-0053, D-0066), with one Boolean added so that the conclusion can only be
reached through the derived literal:

```
a in [l, w]   b in [0, w]   z in {0, 1}        l = w//4,  c = l + w//2,  m = c - l + 1
R:  a + b <= c          T:  z  or  b >= m          min z
```

The propagation is the root pruning `Linear` makes from `R` with `a` at its declared lower
bound, `b <= c - l`, i.e. the literal `~b_ge_m`. The proof derives `z >= 1` from `T` and that
literal (a `pol` that CITES the pruning) and concludes `BOUNDS 1 : Z INF`.

- **order**: the eager encoding of PROOF-FORMAT §3, `x_ge_v` and the ladder in the `.opb`, `R` as
  the expansion with its constant against the declared bound. The `pol` is the cancellation of
  Θ(w) rungs: weaken every `a` literal, fold `b`'s ladder up to rung m−1 with a growing multiplier
  (`@lb_v v * +`, the step `lib/core/ladder.ml` describes), weaken `b` above m, saturate. The
  `rup` is `rup +1 ~b_ge_m >= 1 ;`.
- **bits**: `bit_length(w)` bits per variable plus two bound rows; `[b >= m]` is not in the
  `.opb` and is minted by a `red` pair whose witness touches only the fresh atom (the M8
  preamble's shape, NOT D-0031's rotation). The `pol` is `pol @R @Alo + @B1 + s`, three citations.
  The `rup` is the same line as in the order arm.

Both styles carry an `e` pin on the derived literal (M1-T51's control), so a `pol` that derives
something else is refused where it happens. Six variants per arm and style must be refused with
the checker's wording: the claim's literal flipped, the fold stopped one rung too high (a weaker,
TRUE bound), the atom's row cited in the wrong direction, each `red` with its witness flipped, and
`control-noG`, in which the pruning line is a copy of `R` and the pin is dropped.

**The first design was not load-bearing, and the elaborator said so.** It concluded `BOUNDS -c`
on `min -b`, and `veripb -e` wrote `conclusion BOUNDS -5 : 1 INF`, citing **the row** as the
bound's justification: a root bound from declared bounds is a weakening of the row, so the Θ(w)
literal derivation beside it was decoration. Hence `z`, `T` and a conclusion that cites a `pol`
consuming the pruning; `control-noG` is refused at the conclusion in all 16 pairs ("Expected
constraint is not syntactically implied by the constraint at the hint."), which is the evidence
that the conclusion depends on the pruning.

### VeriPB 3.0.2 on the proof (CPU s from `/usr/bin/time -v`; the checker's own `--stats` agrees)

| w | arm | style | `.opb` B | `.pbp` B | verdict | s | RSS MB |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 10³ | order | rup | 90 592 | 188 | V | 0.00 | 19 |
| 10³ | order | pol | 90 592 | 21 696 | V | 0.00 | 19 |
| 10³ | bits | rup | 978 | 542 | **REJECTED**, not RUP | 0.00 | 11 |
| 10³ | bits | pol | 978 | 542 | V | 0.00 | 11 |
| 10⁴ | order | rup | 975 595 | 191 | V | 0.01 | 41 |
| 10⁴ | order | pol | 975 595 | 237 949 | V | 0.05 | 41 |
| 10⁴ | bits | rup | 1 404 | 680 | **REJECTED**, not RUP | 0.00 | 11 |
| 10⁴ | bits | pol | 1 404 | 679 | V | 0.00 | 11 |
| 10⁵ | order | rup | 10 455 598 | 194 | V | 0.20 | 201 |
| 10⁵ | order | pol | 10 455 598 | 2 602 952 | V | **4.09** | 175 |
| 10⁵ | bits | rup | 1 746 | 787 | **REJECTED**, not RUP | 0.00 | 11 |
| 10⁵ | bits | pol | 1 746 | 785 | V | 0.00 | 11 |

the order `.opb`: 0.15 s at 10⁵, 1.8–1.9 s at 10⁶. So the `rup` CHECK is ~0.05 s and ~0.7 s, the
`pol` ~3.9 s and ~381 s: **×94 for ×10 in width.**

### Elaboration (`veripb -e`) and `cake_pb` on it

| w | arm | style | elab B | elab s | elab RSS MB | cake_pb | s | RSS MB |

| 10³ | order | rup | 2 407 | 0.00 | 19 | V | 0.02 | 26 |
| 10³ | order | pol | 20 017 | 0.00 | 19 | V | 0.03 | 29 |
| 10³ | bits | pol | 491 | 0.00 | 11 | V | 0.00 | 1.6 |
| 10⁴ | order | rup | 27 661 | 0.02 | 43 | V | 0.36 | 260 |
| 10⁴ | order | pol | 221 520 | 0.05 | 43 | V | 0.39 | 293 |
| 10⁴ | bits | pol | 619 | 0.00 | 11 | V | 0.00 | 1.5 |
| 10⁵ | order | rup | 325 165 | 0.22 | 231 | V | 4.09 | 2 863 |
| 10⁵ | order | pol | 2 439 023 | 4.08 | 207 | V | 4.75 | 3 213 |
| 10⁵ | bits | pol | 718 | 0.00 | 11 | V | 0.00 | 3.0 |
| 10⁶ | order | rup | 3 750 169 | 2.67 | 1 936 | V | 34.33 | 4 310 |
| 10⁶ | order | pol | 26 639 026 | 380.86 | 1 634 | V | 49.27 | 4 370 |
| 10⁶ | bits | pol | 826 | 0.00 | 11 | V | 0.00 | 3.1 |

What the elaborator of this build re-emits, measured on these files and not assumed from
D-0102: labels are dropped and every citation renumbered; the `e` pins are **dropped entirely**;
a `rup C ;` becomes `rup C : <ids> ;` with the ids its propagation used and `~` for the negated
claim (in the order arm the m−1 rungs it walked plus `R`, ~7.5 bytes a rung); a `pol` is copied
as it is; a `red` becomes `red C : witness : subproof` / `qed;`, an explicit empty subproof; the
conclusion keeps its hint. **Elaborating costs what checking costs** (2.67 s against 2.58 s,
380.9 s against 383.1 s): the elaborator is the checker with the hints written down, and a `rup`
costs it nothing extra to "reconstruct". `cake_pb` cannot parse a labelled proof (it fails on the
first `@G` line) and **exits 0 on a refusal**, saying `c Checking failed …`; on the elaboration it
verifies all twelve accepted pairs. Its RSS is the CakeML heap, 4.3 GB at 10⁶ in both styles of
the order arm.

### The variants

Every one of the 56 variant runs was refused by VeriPB with a checking error, and the wording
is the one the claim needs: the flipped `rup` claim with "The constraint is not implied by
reverse unit propagation (RUP) from core and derived database."; the wrong `pol` at the `e` pin
with "Expected constraint is not equal to the constraint at the hint."; the flipped `red`
witness with "Proofgoal #1 could not be autoproven. Please add an explicit subproof for proofgoal
#1."; `control-noG` at the conclusion as quoted above.

One of them is refused for the wrong reason, and that is a finding. **`B2`, the half of the atom
pair that says `b >= m -> b_ge_m`, is vacuous for a root pruning.** The atom a root pruning mints
is decided by the model (b ≥ m is impossible under `R` and `a`'s lower bound), so the negation of
`B2` contradicts the database and every redundance goal is implied whatever the witness: D-0053's
vacuity one step out, not over a contradictory database but over a contradictory `¬C`. The
checker refuses the wrong witness here only because its unit propagation does not SEE the
contradiction (three constraints, two variables, over bits). With `a`'s lower bound at 0, in the
first design at w = 10, the same wrong witness was `s VERIFIED`. The solver is not unsound for it
(a `red` whose negation contradicts the database derives an implied constraint, witness or not),
but a test of `ensure_atom`'s witness must mint an atom the model does not decide, or it tests
nothing.

### Which `pol` operator is quadratic (`diag.sh`, one operator kind per proof, order arm)

| w | variant | ops | `.pbp` B | checker s | RSS MB |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 10⁵ | `weaken`, every literal of a and b | 175 000 | 2 264 011 | 0.21 | 171 |
| 10⁵ | `sum`, `@lb_v +` for v < m | 50 000 | 589 009 | 17.17 | 171 |
| 10⁵ | `fold`, `@lb_v v * +` for v < m | 50 000 | 977 899 | 12.69 | 169 |
| 10⁵ | `foldT`, the fold from the 2-term row `T` | 50 000 | 977 899 | 3.07 | 167 |
| 10⁶ | `weaken` | 1 750 000 | 24 389 013 | 2.49 | 1 152 |
| 10⁶ | `sum` | 500 000 | 6 389 011 | **1 754.35** | 1 166 |
| 10⁶ | `fold` | 500 000 | 10 777 902 | **1 291.64** | 1 199 |
| 10⁶ | `foldT` | 500 000 | 10 777 902 | 290.99 | 1 221 |

Weakening is linear and cheap, 1.4 µs an operation at 10⁶ (D-0028's 2w-weakening `pol` was 12 s
at that width on the same checker, and the whole of its cost is here). **Adding a rung into an
accumulator of Θ(w) terms costs Θ(w) per addition**, with or without the multiplier, which is what
makes the fold Θ(w·m): the same fold started from a two-term row (`foldT`, whose accumulator
grows to Θ(m)) is four times cheaper at both widths, and every variant but weakening is ×95 to
×102 for ×10 in width: quadratic, in w for the fold from `R` and in m for the fold from `T`. The
`sum` variant, which cancels nothing, is slower than the fold, which removes one term a step
(1 754 s against 1 292 s at 10⁶). The checker's `+` is not in-place. The run's `pol` (4.09 s,
383 s) is cheaper than its fold alone because the `a` weakenings come first and shrink the
accumulator before the fold starts; the exponent is the same.

### What this says

1. **In the order arm, `rup` wins on every axis the checker can measure.** The same Θ(w)-rung
   cancellation is 197 bytes and ~0.7 s as a RUP check, 28 MB and ~381 s as an explicit `pol`
   at w = 10⁶, and the exponent differs: the `pol` is quadratic in w, the RUP check linear and
   dominated by reading the `.opb`. PROOF-FORMAT §2a's rule "prefer `pol` over `rup`; `rup`
   makes the checker search" is true for a derivation of O(1) citations and false for one of
   Θ(w): there the search IS the cheap part, because unit propagation along the ladder is linear
   and the explicit arithmetic is not.
2. **The prior that `pol` elaborates better than `rup` is the opposite of what the elaborator
   does.** It copies a `pol` and writes a `rup` as its hint list, seven times smaller at 10⁶, in
   the time it takes to check either. `cake_pb` then checks the hinted RUP in 34 s and the
   `pol` in 49 s. Nothing is "reconstructed": the hints are the propagation the checker ran
   anyway.
3. **In the bits arm there is no `rup` for a bound that crosses a row.** Refused at 10³ already
   and at every width: unit propagation over `A >= l`, `B >= m` and `A + B <= c` on bits finds
   nothing, which is GCS's observation on this checker. Every such step is a `pol`, and that
   `pol` is three citations, 0.4 ms, 11 MB and under 1 kB elaborated, flat from 10³ to 10⁶.
4. **The bits arm's price is the atom pair**: two `red` lines of O(log w) bytes per atom, plus
   the second direction (`B2`) wherever the literal has to re-enter a row. One of the two is
   unjudged for a root pruning. D-0031's objection (a witness that permutes existing literals)
   does not arise: the fresh-atom witness is accepted beside a neighbouring atom, since nothing
   else mentions it.

### The sentence T1 takes from this

**Write a justification as `rup` wherever the checker's unit propagation closes it, which is the
order encoding's ladder walks and any clause over atoms that already exist, and as `pol` only
where it cannot, which is every bound that crosses a bits row; a Θ(w)-token `pol` is quadratic
for VeriPB 3.0.2, its elaboration is the `pol` itself, and a `rup` elaborates to a hint list the
verified checker handles faster.**

Two consequences for the rows that follow:

- The order arm below the threshold keeps its ladder-walk justifications but should EMIT them as
  `rup`, not as the fold the writer builds today, and `--stats` should count tokens per `pol` so
  that a Θ(w) one is visible. That is a change to `justify.ml`/`ladder.ml`'s emission, not to
  any propagator (D-0026's split holds), and it is the cheap half of M8.
- `ensure_atom`'s tests must mint an atom under a decision, never at the root, and the
  `--stats` counter of introduced atoms the preamble asks for must be there from T2's first
  commit: the pair is the only cost the bits arm has, and it is paid per atom, not per pruning.

What this did not measure, named so that it is not read into the tables: the solver's own cost
of writing either form (none of this ran the solver), a learned clause's `rup` over derived
atoms in the bits arm (only the row-crossing bound was written), and `cake_pb` on a `red` with a
non-empty subproof (the elaborator emitted empty ones, because the autoprover discharged every
goal).
