## D-0148  M7-T31: a factless pruning that settled over a hole is not a root of the decision closure; the refused branch nogoods on hrc were that, not the assignment shape

Status: DECIDED
Date: 2026-11-19
Task: M7-T31 (agent-proofbugs, `wave50-proofbugs`).
Touches: `lib/core/analysis.ml` (`rests_on_nothing`, used by `analyse`'s `mk_node` and by
`dependency_levels`' `cite`), `lib/core/search.ml` (`median_values`, a test-only knob),
`test/unit/test_analysis.ml` (scene 7), `test/models/opt_global_settles_hole_sat.fzn`.
Follows D-0137 section 13.1 and the WORKLOG note "three findings from the M10
measurements", D-0124's a3 addendum (the closure over memoised citations), D-0077 (the
assignment decision), M1-T44/M1-T57 (a settle's line cites the holes it walked over).

### 1. The two reproducers, and what they had in common

**A.** D-0137's own, on binary `28c4a51c` (code `9fb9b09`, identical in `lib/` and `bin/`
to `457eb7f`): `2017_hrc_exp1-1-5670` with `--search activity --restarts luby
--phase-saving`, phase saving then taking D-0077's assignment `x = s`, refused at line
620 348 at *"The constraint is not implied by reverse unit propagation (RUP) from core and
derived database"*. **B.** The orchestrator's second one, on current main (`f689aae`, binary
`35fb5d77`), where phase saving branches `x <= s` and no assignment is ever taken, on the same
instance with `--search alternate --restarts luby --phase-saving`, refused at line 983 748
(`@c971723`, the branch nogood of node 3 935, a second child at level 80) at the same
wording. So the assignment shape was not the cause, and B is what was dissected.

### 2. The measurement

An instrumented copy of the binary (not committed; `fataepyc-06:/scratch/arthur/
wave50-proofbugs-dbg`, `BAGUETTE_DBG_NG`/`BAGUETTE_DBG_NODE`) printed the decision stack, the
closure's levels and the nogood, and at node 3 935 the whole trail, with every entry's level, old
and new domain, reason facts with their supports, and the trace line ids written for it. The
same run's proof was byte-identical to the uninstrumented one.

- The nogood kept 15 of 80 decision levels. Each of the 65 dropped decisions was added back
  in turn (`addback.py`, one checker run each), and **only level 41** (`X_INTRODUCED_2859_ <= 0`)
  makes it RUP, and the clause of all 80 is RUP too.
- Replaying the conflict's facts over the trace lines of the live trail, under the 15 kept
  decisions (`sim.py`), the chain breaks at one line, the one of trail entry 815, at level 61,
  `X_INTRODUCED_2086_` from `1..3` to `1..1`, **with an empty reason and not a level start**,
  whose line is `@c970126 rup +1 ~X_INTRODUCED_2086__ge_2 +1 X_INTRODUCED_2226__ge_1 >= 1`.
  Entry 815 is the learned unit `X_INTRODUCED_2086_ <= 2` (`@c959341`, level 0), re-applied
  at that node by `Search.apply_globals` with `Reason.none`. The value 2 was a hole, punched
  at level 41 by entry 565 citing `X_INTRODUCED_2226_ <= 0` (entry 562, from the level-41
  decision), so the push settled to `<= 1`, and `Trace.settle_facts` gave the line the
  hole's facts. Every line the chain needs is on the page and live, so the nogood lacks a
  premise and no line is missing.

### 3. The cause

`Analysis` called a node a ROOT, never expanded, when its supporting entry had no facts
(`Reason.is_empty`), and its header said why that was safe, "a decision, a constraint posted
at this level, or a pruning that genuinely follows from a model row alone", whose level the
closure keeps, which is conservative. That holds for a factless entry that landed exactly
where it was pushed. It does not hold for one that SETTLED, because its trace line cites
the facts of every hole the settle crossed (M1-T57), exactly as a propagator's settle
does. The closure pinned the entry's own level (61, kept
anyway here) and never folded the holes, so the hole's level (41) left the nogood. Both
walks, the memo over citations and the walk over facts, used the one rule, which is why
BAGUETTE_DEBUG's cross-check agreed with a wrong answer.

The shape needs a factless push at a level above a hole on its variable. `apply_globals`
makes one at every node for every learned unit and for the branch-and-bound bound, so main
can reach it at default flags (section 5). Restarts multiply the learned units and the
dynamic orders vary the levels, which is why D-0137 saw it only under those flags. A's
assignment shape made it likelier still, because D-0077's sibling removes `x = s` as a HOLE at the
node's level, and the split `x <= s` punches none.

**The GCS lead** (`restarts-nogoods-weighting.md`, "The proof lifecycle", point 1, about a
restart that forgets root-level lines the next pass relies on) was checked and does not apply. A
trace line carries its trail entry's level (`Trace.emit_to_page`), a restart to `t` wipes
levels above `t` only, whose entries it pops, and `Writer.wipe_level` refuses level 0. So
no line of a surviving entry is deleted, and section 2 found every needed line live.

### 4. The fix

With `Analysis.rests_on_nothing store p e`, an entry is a root when its reason is empty AND it is
a level start or settled over no hole (`Store.settled_over_lo`/`_hi` both empty, the same run
of holes `Trace.holes_below`/`holes_above` compute for the line). A factless settle is then
expanded like any settle, into the reasons of the holes' removers, by both walks (the memo's
`cites_of` already folded holes, it was never asked). Its own level is no longer pinned,
which is right because its line needs the level-0 unit and the hole lines and no decision. A DECISION
that settles stays a root, because it is assumed and its settle step is `Search.bridges`' line,
whose ancestors the nogood keeps through `protected` (M1-T55/D-0070).

The root rule is shared with the 1UIP walk, so a factless settle at the conflict level is
now resolved there as well instead of standing in the cut. Both cuts are sound. No run
below learned a different clause because of it (the default lane is byte-identical).

### 5. The failing-first tests

- `test/models/opt_global_settles_hole_sat.fzn`, 7 variables of at most 5 values. At default
  flags, `t = 3` punches `obj <> 3` at level 1, the first solution `obj = 4` installs
  `obj <= 3`, and at the re-entry of level 2 that bound settles to `obj <= 2`, a factless
  entry resting on level 1; a level-3 conflict rests on it. `f689aae`'s binary writes the
  nogood `~e_ge_1 \/ p_ge_1` and 3.0.2 refuses it at line 44 at the RUP wording, and the fix
  writes `~e_ge_1 \/ ~t_ge_3` (the only changed line) and the proof is VERIFIED, OPT 0.
  Its stdout is the same under both binaries.
- `test_analysis.ml` scene 7 (`test_factless_settle_is_expanded`) builds a hole at level 1, a
  single-term row pushing `o <= 3` factlessly at level 2 and settling to `o <= 2`, a conflict
  resting on it. With the old rule restored three checks fail (the closure names `[2]`, a set
  under which brute force finds the model satisfiable), and with the fix the closure is `[2; 1]`,
  the memo and the walk agree, and the entry's memo is the hole remover's level-1 citation.
- No mutation lane, because no rule kind and no line shape is new. Only the decisions a
  nogood names change.

### 6. The sweep

The knob `BAGUETTE_TEST_VALUE_CHOICE=median` (test-only, read from the environment, never a CLI flag, in
`Search.median_values`, wrapped last, after `phased`) replaces every decision's value by
`indomain_median`'s, so an interior median is an assignment everywhere. Run on `fataepyc-06`
over the 183 suite models (`test/models/` minus PENDING, with the new one) and the lane
corpus's 27 (instance, budget) pairs at their node budgets, every proof checked, with the
fixed binary (`fix-50d9221`, md5 `68b3d753`) and the same code with the old root rule
(`unfixed-50d9221`, `b17cd31c`):

| configuration | suite, fixed | corpus, fixed | proofs changed by the fix |
|---|---|---|---|
| default | 183/183 VERIFIED; 182 byte-identical to `f689aae` | (the lane) | the new model only |
| median | 183/183 | 27/27 | none |
| `--search alternate --restarts luby --phase-saving` | 183/183 | 27/27 | the new model only |
| `--search activity --restarts luby --phase-saving` | 183/183 | 27/27 | none |
| median + alternate + `luby:1` + phase saving | 183/183 | 27/27 | 2 suite (`backjump_unsat`, `backjump_deep_unsat`), 1 corpus (`2012_mspsp_hard_01@10000`) |
| median + activity + `luby:1` + phase saving + `--reuse-trail` | 183/183 | 27/27 | 6 corpus (`bacp-22`, `filters_dct_2_2`, `rcpsp_12`, `foxgeesecorn_54`, `mspsp_hard_01`, `pigment15b`) |

1 233 runs, every one VERIFIED with the fix. Under the old rule the only refusal in the
1 233 was the new model under `alternate`. The shape occurs in the ten runs the last column
names, and there the checker found the hole some other way (the disequality's own `.opb`
rows, when its operands' facts are derivable), so those nogoods were unsupported by their
trace but not refused. That is also why the 189-model gates never saw it. With the fix, hrc
under B verifies (OPT 2, 10 328 nodes instead of 10 117) and under A, on `457eb7f` plus this
commit, verifies too (BOUNDS 2, 8 086 nodes), and A without the fix still refuses at line 620 348
(`main-9fb9b09.exe`, re-run).

### 7. What changes on purpose

A proof changes only where a factless push settled over a hole that the closure reached, and the
nogood names the hole's levels instead of the push's. The differential lane's nine recorded
configurations are byte-identical (232/232 with the fixed binary). The three strategy
configurations (`restarts`, `activity`, `alternate`) had no reference on this branch when it
was measured; their gate-53 references are compared at the merge (section 8 if any differ).

### 8. The lane at the merge (2026-11-19, after `origin/main` at `681a9e6` was merged in)

The three strategy configurations' references (gate 53) are on the branch now. Run with this
branch's binary, every run of `restarts`, `activity` and `alternate`, plain and debug, equals
its reference, so the fix changes no lane run under any configuration. The only differing runs
are `fifo` and `lbd`, identical under current main's binary (D-0149 section 5).

## D-0149  M6-T23: the `--time-limit` overshoot on cargo and cable was the stop never being asked, inside a PB analysis and inside a conflict's trace, and not the finaliser; and D-0137 section 13.2's alarm is gone on main

Status: DECIDED
Date: 2026-11-19
Task: M6-T23 (agent-proofbugs, `wave50-proofbugs`).
Touches: `lib/core/pb_analysis.ml` (`?stop`, the `Stopped` fallback), `lib/core/ladder.ml`
(`lift ?stop`, `Ladder.Stopped`), `lib/core/trace.ml` (`emit ?stop`, `Trace.Stopped`),
`lib/core/justify.ml` (`operand_hash`), `lib/core/search.ml` (the conflict arm and
`pb_at_conflict` pass `cfg.stop`; `stats.stopped_in_trace`), `bin/main.ml` (`at=trace`).
Follows D-0136 (M6-T21: `retire`'s sweep, the poll inside `Engine.propagate`, `fired=`),
D-0137 section 13.2 and 13.3, D-0145 (J1, the memo's hash).

### 1. Finding 2 (D-0137 section 13.2): no alarm on current main

`BAGUETTE_DEBUG=1` on `2017_hrc_exp1-1-5670`, binary `f689aae` (which has D-0142 section 1's
`f9bf6c4`), 1 500 s limit: at default flags OPT 2 in 8 343 nodes with and without the proof
(the 296 MB proof VERIFIED), under `--search activity --restarts luby --phase-saving` OPT in
3 115 nodes, under `--search alternate --restarts luby --phase-saving` OPT in 10 117 nodes.
Neither `Not_at_fixpoint("I-P7: ...")` nor `Bad_watch("M6-T22: ...")` fired in any of the
four. Both were D-0142 section 1's two false alarms, measured on `28c4a51c`, which predates
the fix; engine.ml and prop/clause.ml need nothing. (The `alternate` run is D-0148's refused
proof, and no invariant fired there either, which D-0148 section 3 explains.)

### 2. Finding 3: what the overshoot was

D-0137 section 13.3 read the overshoot as the finaliser after the stop. Measured on
`fataepyc-06` with `--time-limit 300` under an outer wall of 2 400 s, binary `f689aae`, the
`limit:` line's `fired=` (D-0136) says otherwise on both instances. The time is before
the stop says yes, inside one node, where nothing asks it.

| instance | proof | `fired=` | exit | nodes, conflicts | where the time went (perf, from 302 s) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `2017_cargo_challenge01_0s_1913` | no | never | killed at 2 400 s | 461, 15 | one PB analysis |
| `2017_cargo_challenge01_0s_1913` | yes | never | killed at 2 400 s | 461, 15 | the same |
| `2020_cable_tree_wiring_R046` | no | 302.23 s | 302.70 s | 1 505, 71 | (none) |
| `2020_cable_tree_wiring_R046` | yes | 1 500.09 s | 1 509.5 s | 254, 1 | the first conflict's trace |

**Cargo, with or without the proof.** A frame-pointer build (`baguette-fp`, D-0145) put
90.3 % of the run under `Pb_analysis.analyse` -> `step` -> `Ladder.lift` (89.7 %), whose fold
adds one ladder row per rung with `Learned.combine` (56 %) and re-sorts the whole row in
`Learned.make` each time (34 %), with the GC around it. The 16th conflict's analysis did not
end in 2 100 s. D-0136 had found that conflict analysis needed no poll, which was true of
the instances it measured.

**Cable, with the proof.** 254 nodes and one conflict, 252 levels down. Its `Trace.emit`
writes the whole branch's lines, 1.9 GB, and from 302 s to 452 s 93.3 % of the samples were
in `Justify.find_in_bucket`'s `==` walk. An instrumented build counted 1.65 M memo lookups
for 300 M bucket steps, in buckets of 4 700 to 6 500 entries, each a chain
`Combine [k * Combine [... Combine [Model_row i; ...]]]` differing from its neighbours only
in row ids two to seven levels down. The shallow hash read a `Term` operand by its
constructor alone (it did before J1 as well, since J1 changed the hash function and not its depth).
The stop is asked at node entry and inside propagation, and a trace is neither.

**The finaliser was never the time.** From `fired=` to exit, 6.6 s on cable with the proof,
0.5 s without it.

### 3. The fixes

1. **PB analysis asks the stop** (`974c77d`). `Pb_analysis.analyse ?stop` checks it before
   every elimination, and `Ladder.lift ?stop` before every rung's `combine`. Yes gives the
   new fallback `Stopped`, and the conflict arm carries on with the clause path, exactly as
   for any other fallback, so the stop lands at the next node entry. Nothing PB analysis
   abandons has been written.
2. **A conflict's trace asks the stop** (`3523070`, every entry since `aab586a`).
   `Trace.emit ?stop` checks it before each trail entry. Yes restores the writer's level
   and raises `Trace.Stopped`, which the conflict arm turns into `Limit_hit`
   (`stats.stopped_in_trace`, `at=trace` on the `limit:` line). The lines already written
   are a valid prefix, because each is RUP from the model and from earlier lines (oldest
   first, Trace's header), and nothing else of the node is on the page yet.
3. **The memo hashes an operand by its content** (`bc8aa58`). `operand_hash` walks a
   `Term`'s, `Cut`'s or `Resolve`'s operand depth first, over at most 48 nodes and
   `hash_width` elements per list. A nested `Deferred` is a constant whatever its `forced`
   says, so forcing a thunk still cannot move a key, and the equality is still `==`, so no
   emitted byte can change. Measured, 3.96 M lookups per 300 M steps (was 1.65 M), the
   biggest bucket 388 entries. Those 388 are structurally IDENTICAL, one physical copy per
   decision level of the same `Combine` rebuilt by its propagator, which no hash separates.
   That is what is left of the walk, and the remedy is D-0140's J1 alternative (an id
   stamped in each explanation at creation), which needs an `Explanation` field and a
   record of its own. Not done here.

In every run without a limit the stop is `fun () -> false` (or the node budget's
`nodes > n`, which cannot turn true inside a node), so fixes 1 and 2 change nothing there.

### 4. After

Same machine, same flags, every stopped proof checked by 3.0.2 (64 GB cap for the checker,
whose runs on these 1.9 GB `.opb` files need 7 to 16 GB):

| instance, limit | binary | `fired=` | `limit:` wall | process exit | `at=` | proof |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| cargo, 300 s, no proof | `f689aae` | never | - | killed at 2 400 s | - | - |
| cargo, 300 s, no proof | `85cc1b0` | 300.07 s | 300.07 s | 300.11 s | node | - |
| cargo, 300 s, proof | `f689aae` | never | - | killed at 2 400 s | - | truncated |
| cargo, 300 s, proof | `85cc1b0` | 300.05 s | 300.06 s | 300.12 s | node | VERIFIED NO CONCLUSION |
| cable, 300 s, no proof | `f689aae` | 302.23 s | 302.23 s | 302.70 s | node | - |
| cable, 300 s, no proof | `85cc1b0` | 300.32 s | 300.32 s | 300.73 s | node | - |
| cable, 300 s, proof | `f689aae` | 1 500.09 s | 1 506.66 s | 1 509.52 s | node | (not checked) |
| cable, 300 s, proof | `85cc1b0` | 304.82 s | 312.05 s | 314.96 s | node | VERIFIED NO CONCLUSION |
| cable, 300 s, proof | `aab586a` | 300.09 s | 307.11 s | 310.40 s | trace | see section 5 |
| cable, 120 s, proof | `85cc1b0` | 123.88 s | 133.40 s | - | trace | VERIFIED NO CONCLUSION |
| cable, 120 s, proof | `aab586a` | 120.04 s | 129.74 s | 131.13 s | trace | VERIFIED NO CONCLUSION |

Stop to exit, the finaliser's share, is 0.04 to 0.07 s on cargo, 7 to 10 s on cable with the
proof (deleting the live ids of 252 open levels and flushing a 1.2 to 2.5 GB file), as
before the fixes. The overshoot past the limit goes from more than 2 100 s to 0.1 s on cargo
and from 1 209 s to 10 s on cable. Cargo's search is unchanged up to the stop (461 nodes and
15 conflicts both ways). With `85cc1b0`, cable's first conflict wrote its whole 1.9 GB trace
in about 280 s where `f689aae` took 1 200 s (fix 3 alone), and the stop then landed at the
next node entry. `aab586a` polls at every trace entry where `85cc1b0` polled at every 64th,
which is why it stops inside the second conflict's trace and why the 120 s run fires at
120.04 s rather than 123.88 s.

### 5. What the fixes cost, and what they change

- **Bytes.** Fix 3 is bucketing only, and measured so. Cable at a 300-node budget with the
  proof writes the same stdout, `.opb` and 1 887 164 408-byte `.pbp` (md5 `eee608b4`) under
  `f689aae` in 1 847 s and under `bc8aa58` in 278 s (6.6 times faster, the same 21 GB peak).
  Fixes 1 and 2 act only when the stop says yes inside a node, which a run without a time
  limit never does, nor a node budget (`nodes > n` cannot change inside a node).
- **The suite and the lane.** On the merged branch, 193 suite models with the proof are
  byte-identical to current main's binary (`681a9e6`) except D-0148's new model. In the
  differential lane, 301 plain and 289 debug runs, every run equals its reference except
  48 plain and 39 debug runs in `fifo` and `lbd`. The `fifo` and `lbd` runs (51 plain, 49
  debug) are byte-identical (stdout, `.opb`, `.pbp`, observations) between this branch's
  binary and `681a9e6`'s, so those differences are main's, from the retention hook merged
  after the references were recorded (`36c1312`, D-0139). Nothing in this row changes a
  lane run.
- **The M6-T9 lane, found by the gate.** `test_endtoend`'s stopped-satisfaction lane uses a
  stop that COUNTS its calls (`m6_after 6`), and the new polls asked it inside the first
  conflict's trace, so it stopped there instead of at the 7th node. D-0136 had already made
  `stop_poll_runs = 0` the node-entry-only contract for such a predicate. The two new polls
  follow it now (`inner_stop`, `c707051`) and the lane states it in its config, which is
  what it always meant: it had run on the default config only because its scene never
  reached `Engine.propagate`'s 128-run poll.
- **Not done.** The 388-copy buckets (section 3, fix 3) are what remains of the memo walk;
  the remedy is an explanation id, which is D-0140 J1's alternative and needs its own
  record. The finaliser's 7 to 10 s on a 2 GB cable proof is the `del` of every live id of
  252 open levels and the flush, linear, and was not touched.
  `2020_hoist-benchmark-for-minizinc_PU_3_8_5` (D-0137 section 13.3, strategy flags only)
  was not re-measured.

## D-0152  M11-complexity-T4 part 2: search, analysis and retention without their per-node and per-conflict scans; 5 to 17 % of the instructions at 40 000 nodes without the proof on five of D-0140's six instances, every byte the same

**Status**: **DONE** (part 2 of M11-complexity-T4, which closes the task), recorded 2026-11-19
(agent-batch4b, `wave52-batch4b`). The contract is D-0140 §5's rows S1 to S6, A1, A3, R1 to R4, L2,
J6's `search.ml` site and P2's `Learned.combine` half, and D-0144 §4. Files changed:
`lib/core/search.ml` (not the PB-analysis call site, which M8 holds this wave), `lib/core/analysis.ml`,
`lib/core/retention.ml`, `lib/core/learned.ml`, and the tests `test_search_strategy.ml`,
`test_retention.ml`, `test_learned.ml`, `test_analysis.ml`. Measured on `fataepyc-06` against
`main` at `ef6e659`, binary `9571b17ca68c59e3fd0b7e335b156211` (gate 57's), outputs under
`/scratch/arthur/wave52-batch4b-runs/`.

### 1. What was already done, and what is not done

- **R1 and R2** were done by D-0139 (M10-T4): `Retention.reduce` is O(1) unless the policy is due,
  and `holds` is a hash lookup. Nothing left.
- **S3's store half** was D-0142 (`Store.is_level_start` in one load); its search half is below.
- **J6** in `trace.ml`, `justify.ml` and `writer.ml` was D-0145; `learn.ml`'s was D-0144. Only
  `bridges` was left, below.
- **A2** stays, as D-0140 said: it is the backjump's definition.
- **A3** (`check_attribution`'s `List.exists Var.equal` per citation) is NOT done. D-0140 measured it
  "nv", and the cheap form needs `Engine.in_scope` handed to `Analysis.analyse`, whose only solver
  caller is `Learn.at_conflict` in `learn.ml`, a file this batch did not claim. A per-analysis memo
  of sorted scopes inside `analysis.ml` would sort a learned clause's scope to answer one query, which
  costs more than the scan.
- **P2's `Learned.combine` per rung** is NOT done. The fold lives in `ladder.ml`, which M8 holds this
  wave, and the change (one combination of all rungs) moves the `Checked` additions and so possibly
  the overflow point and its message, which reach `--stats`. D-0144 §1 and its WORKLOG request stand.
- **R4 was done and reverted** (§3).

### 2. The fixes, and why each keeps the bytes

One commit per fix. Where the argument is not a line long, the old code is kept as the
specification and compared, either under `BAGUETTE_DEBUG` at every call (so the debug pass of the
differential lane exercises it) or in a unit test on random inputs.

**S1, `count_learned_activity`** (`8366c18`). Per trail entry of every node, the instance id was
looked up with two polymorphic `List.mem` over every learned instance id. It is now one byte load
from `learned_kinds`, indexed by `id - first_learned_id`, grown by doubling at registration.
`learned_kind` answers "none" below the boundary and for an id nothing registered, which is when
neither list held it, and the table is never iterated, so the determinism argument the lists were
kept for holds. Counters only. Test: `test_search_strategy.ml`, against the two lists on 50 random
registrations, past two growths.

**S3, `decision_entries`** (`552ba14`). Per conflict, `bridges` asked `Store.is_level_start` at every
trail position. It now reads `Store.level_marks`: an entry is a level start iff an open mark sits at
it, the marks are monotone (I-T2), an empty level shares its position with the next, so the marks
below the trail's end with repeats dropped are the scan's positions in the scan's order.
`decision_entries_scan` is the old walk, compared under `BAGUETTE_DEBUG` at every call and on a
6 000-step random walk of a store (5 623 states with two levels at one position).

**S4, `unfixed` and `first_fail`** (`345e707`). `unfixed` asks `Domain.is_fixed` (two loads) instead
of `Domain.size > 1` (a hole count); they agree on every stored domain by I-D1 and I-D2. The staged
`sequence`'s liveness test likewise. `first_fail` stops at the first candidate of size 2: every
candidate is unfixed (`type order` says so, and `unfixed` and both arms of `sequence` filter for it)
and the comparison is strict, so nothing later can replace it. On a Boolean model that is the first
candidate. Test: the same random walk, with holes punched, against the full scan.

**S5, the nogood's `kept` filter in `dfs`** (`62c7641`). A polymorphic `List.mem l ls` per nogood
literal, depth squared per conflict, is now `level_set ls`, one byte per level. A list with a
negative level (none exists) would be answered by `List.exists`, so the function is `List.mem` on
every list. Test: 2 000 random level lists.

**S6, `apply_globals`** (`3179e37`). The learned units were reversed at every node and each one's
justification built before its bound was tested. The forward list is now kept beside the reversed
one (`push_global`), and a unit whose bound is already in force is skipped before anything is built:
exactly the case `Domain.set_lo`/`set_hi` answer `Unchanged`, on which `Store.apply` does nothing.

**S2, the citation texts** (`34f5077`, kept after §3's revert). `register_learned` and
`register_learned_pb` rendered every literal of every learned clause, unit and PB row into the
`Retention.cite` message, which only a `Cited` exception or `cited_by` reads. `Retention.cite_lazy`
stores a `Lazy.t` over the same immutable values (the clause instance's literal list, the unit, the
row), so the text is the same when it is read. `cite` keeps its signature. Test in
`test_retention.ml`.

**R3, the `fifo`, `lbd` and `tiered` orders** (`024c118`). `reduce` hands `evict` the live list
oldest first (`add` appends with the next `e_seq`, `retire` only filters), so `fifo`'s sort was the
identity: one pass checks the order and the sort runs only on a list that is not sorted (stable sort,
total order, so the sorted list is the list). The three policies compare with `Int.compare` and
`Bool.compare`, which give the polymorphic `compare`'s signs on ints and bools. Test: both policies
against the polymorphic sorts, on the live list and a shuffled one, at six caps.

**J6, `bridges`' origin** (`5ec5722`). A thunk through `Justify.emit_rup_clause_lazy`, as `Trace`'s
since D-0145. The origin is never written to the `.pbp`.

**L2, `Learned.to_linear_row`** (`62c9acc`). Asked on every learned clause (`Learn.at_conflict`'s
`l_converts`, for `--stats`' `convertible`): `ladder_form` sorted the rungs with the polymorphic
`compare` and `to_linear_row` grouped them with a `List.partition` over the whole remainder per
variable. `rung_compare` is `String.compare`, then `Int.compare` twice, the polymorphic order on a
`(string, int, int)` triple, and on the sorted list a variable's rungs are the contiguous prefix the
partition returned. Not "under `--stats` only": the predicate is computed in `learn.ml`, which this
batch did not claim, and the CLI does not tell the search whether `--stats` is on. Test:
`test_learned.ml`, against the old code copied as the reference, 5 000 random rows (1 229 with a
linear form).

**A1, the 1UIP walk** (`b9e266e`). Each resolution step rebuilt the node list, counted its
conflict-level nodes for `one_uip`, folded it for the expandable node of largest support, appended
the fresh cells with `@` and filtered the expanded cell out, five passes over the frontier per step.
Now the frontier's cells carry a creation number and a removed cell is marked dead in place (the live
cells in creation order are the old list: cells were only appended and filtered); the count of live
conflict-level cells is kept at the three places a cell's node changes; and a max-heap on
(support, creation number), pushed whenever a cell takes an expandable node and cleaned lazily (an
entry is current while its cell is live and still holds that very node; `mk` builds a fresh node per
fact, so physical equality cannot see an old one come back), gives the fold's choice, ties to the
earliest cell. The criterion's `view` carries the count and a lazy node list, so `one_uip` never has
the list built. The risk D-0140 named, "ordering, ties follow the cell order", is what the heap's
second key is for. Both the count and the choice are checked against the old passes under
`BAGUETTE_DEBUG` at every step, and in `test_analysis.ml` on 3 000 random walks (6 580 steps, roots,
four levels, supports that tie). `Frontier.create ()` without a level keeps the merge-only behaviour
M6-T16's test compares against `add_node`.

### 3. R4, done and reverted (`34f5077`, `d4e8477`)

R4 keyed `Retention`'s duplicate table on the learned row (`Learned.equal`, `Learned.hash`) instead
of its text, and dropped the per-entry text `e_key`, which nothing read. The count is the same
(the rendering is injective over a compiled model: `Lit.render` on (sanitised owner, kind, value),
`Compile.check_name_collisions`, the auxiliaries named away from every sanitised name), the bytes
were the same, and no instruction was saved within the noise (§4). But the table then held every
learned ROW, about twelve words per term, where it held the row's text, and the peak RSS rose by
6 to 8 % at 10 000 nodes (mspsp 301 → 321 MB, openshop proof 609 → 660 MB, rcpsp_11 129 → 138 MB,
QR72 91 → 98 MB). Reverted. A key that is both small and free to build would be a hash of the row
with the text kept only on collision; it was not worth a structure at a gain this file could not
measure.

lists while the database is still small), not the part that grows: the growing part, late minus

### 5. Byte identity

- **The differential lane** on `b9e266e` (every fix but §3's revert): `make diff ARGS="--tier all
  -j 24"` **301 of 301 runs equal** the reference, and `--debug --tier all -j 24` **289 of 289**,
  where S3's and A1's cross-checks run at every call. The lane covers the default, audit off,
  no-proof, `lbd`, `fifo`, the `-po` variants, `nopb`, `bits0`, and restarts, activity and alternate,
  which run `apply_globals`, `count_learned_activity`, the `kept` filter and the analysis under every
  strategy.
- **The measurement runs** (§4): 36 of 36 identical in stdout, `--stats`, `.pbp` and `.opb`, for the
  final binary and for each intermediate one at 10 000 nodes.
- **The unit suites**, `dune runtest --root . --force` under `ulimit -v 4000000` at `d4e8477`:
  rc 0, no failure, every D-0152 test passing (12 lines), peak RSS 99 MB.
- **The gate**: `make check` on a fresh node clone at `d4e8477` (`/scratch/arthur/wave52-batch4b-gate.sh`, gate 57's script with no `--update` line): rc 0, peak RSS 99 MB (`make_check_wall 25.87 s peak_rss 98724 kB`), and all 193 models' stdout, exit code, `.opb` and `.pbp` byte-identical to gate 57's binary `9571b17c` (0 differences). In the same script, on the final binary `d12feec0`: the lane 301 of 301 and the debug pass 289 of 289 equal, the scaling lane rc 0 (the table above).

### 6. What would reverse this

- A criterion other than `one_uip` that reads `v_nodes` in a hot loop would pay `Frontier.nodes`
  per step again; the lazy list costs nothing only to a criterion that reads the count.
- `first_fail`'s early stop rests on `type order`'s contract that every candidate is unfixed. An
  order that hands it fixed variables would get a different variable; `Debug` does not check it.
- If the learned database must hold rows anyway (an evicting policy that re-derives, or a
  duplicate-merging step), §3's key becomes free and should come back.
## D-0153  M8-bits-encoding: PB conflict analysis over rows with a bits term -- every bits block is INSTANTIATED through its atom's bridge before the analysis resolves on it

Status: DECIDED (built, measured; the bits0 lane reference is the orchestrator's to re-record after the gated merge)
Date: 2026-11-19
Task: M8-bits-encoding, D-0134 section 11's lift (agent-pbbits, `wave52-pbbits`).
Touches: `lib/core/ladder.ml` (the bits arm at its foot: `bits`, `instantiate`,
`derive_instantiated`), `lib/core/pb_analysis.ml` (`?bits`, the conflict row and every reason
instantiated, `Mixed_row` fallback, `bits_bridges`, `bits_of_ctx`), `lib/core/prop/linear.ml`
(`pb_row ?bits_n`), `lib/flatzinc/compile.ml` (`pack_linear`/`pack_arith_row`'s `~mixed` now
carries the bit counts; the dispatch block is untouched), `lib/core/search.ml` (the PB-analysis
call site, one argument), `test/unit/test_ladder.ml` (section (e)), `test/unit/test_compile.ml`
(the mixed row is the .opb's row), `test/models/bits_pb_learn_sat.fzn`,
`bits_pb_order_pivot_sat.fzn`, `bench/bits_spike/probe_pbbits.sh`. `learned.ml` is NOT touched.
Follows D-0134 section 11 (the gap and the design), D-0132 sections 2.1-2.8 (the bridges, the
atom at level 0), D-0130 sections 5 and 7, D-0044 (the clause path stays), D-0127 (where `rup`
is and is not enough).

### 0. The sentence

A row with a term on the bits encoding is offered to PB conflict analysis as the .opb holds it
(`a * 2^i` on `x_bit_i`), and before anything resolves on it every bits block is replaced
through ONE line the proof already has or mints at level 0 -- the bridge of the atom at the
bound in force (B2 for an upper bound, B1 for a lower, D-0130 section 5.1), the declared-bound
row at a declared bound, and for the pruned block of a reason the PIVOT's own atom -- so the row
that reaches `Reduce`, `Ladder.lift`, the criterion and `Pb` is over order literals and atoms
only, and the learned row is stated by `ia` as before.

### 1. Checker facts, measured before writing (`bench/bits_spike/probe_pbbits.sh`, VeriPB 3.0.2 d5644ca4, fataepyc-06, 2026-11-19)

Model M (satisfiable, x = 4, y = 7, z = 1): `x, y in 0..7` on 3 bits, `z in 0..3` on the
ladder; R1: `x + z <= 5` (mixed), R2: `x + y >= 11`. The scene: the decision z >= 3, R1 pushes
`x <= 2` (pivot `~x_ge_3`, a bits term pruned), R2 conflicts. Model S (satisfiable): R3:
`z + y <= 2`, R4: `x + z >= 4`; the decision x <= 1, R4 pushes z >= 3 (an ORDER pivot in a
mixed reason), R3 conflicts.

| probe | line(s) | verdict |
|---|---|---|
| p1 | the conflict row at the conflict `pol @R2 @x3b + @uby +` (B2 of `x_ge_3`, y's declared high) = `5 x_ge_3 >= 2`; the reason at the pivot's atom `pol @R1 @x3a +` (B1) = `3 ~x_ge_3 + ~z_ge_1..3 >= 1` (both pinned by `e`); `pol @i1 3 d`; `pol @i0 @r1 5 * +`; `ia +5 ~z_ge_1 +5 ~z_ge_2 +5 ~z_ge_3 >= 2` | **s VERIFIED** |
| p2 | B1 cited where B2 belongs in the conflict row's instantiation | **refused** at the `ia`: "Expected constraint is not syntactically implied by the constraint at the hint." |
| p3 | B2 cited where B1 belongs in the reason's | **refused**, same wording |
| p4 | the learned row over-claimed (degree 3: `z <= 1`, true in the model, not what the derivation gives) | **refused**, same wording |
| p5 | B1 of `x_ge_3` under the flipped witness `x_ge_3 -> 1`. FIRST over m.opb, where it was ACCEPTED: R2 forces `x >= 4` at the root, so the flipped witness is right in every model (D-0132 section 5.4's lesson). Over t.opb (R1 alone, x = 0 feasible) | **refused**: "Proofgoal #1 could not be autoproven. Please add an explicit subproof for proofgoal #1." (p5ok, the right witness, s VERIFIED) |
| p6 | ALTERNATIVE "the bits row itself as an antecedent": `pol @R2 @R1 + @uby +` (x's whole block cancels, no atom), `ia +1 ~z_ge_1 +1 ~z_ge_2 +1 ~z_ge_3 >= 2` | **s VERIFIED** -- and STRONGER than p1 (`z <= 1` against `z <= 2`): the reason is tight here |
| p7 | ALTERNATIVE "the sparse chain as the ladder of a bits term": the staircase `X' <= 2 + 2 x_ge_3 + 3 x_ge_5` over two minted atoms and their link, as `rup` | accepted at 3 bits |
| p7w | the same staircase at 8 bits (atoms at 100 and 200) | **refused**: "The constraint is not implied by reverse unit propagation (RUP) ..." -- D-0127's caveat, as D-0134 section 11 argued |
| p8 | p1's learned row as a bare `rup` | accepted at 3 bits; not relied on |
| s1 | S's scene: `pol @R3 @lby +`; `pol @R4 @x2b +` (B2 of `x_ge_2`, x's bound read at the propagation); `pol @i1 ~z_ge_2 + ~z_ge_3 +` (the reduction's weakening); `pol @i0 @r1 +`; `ia +6 x_ge_2 +1 ~z_ge_2 +1 ~z_ge_3 >= 1` | **s VERIFIED** |
| s2 | B1 cited where B2 belongs in the reason | **refused** at the hint wording |

So the shape is the one D-0134 section 11 named: the row INSTANTIATED at the propagation (p1,
s1); a wrong bridge is refused at the `ia` that states the learned row, at the checker's
judgement on the `pol` (p2, p3, s2); the sparse chain as a ladder is not one step and its `rup`
does not survive width (p7w). The third shape (p6) is stronger where it applies and is left as
the next step, for the reasons in section 2.5.

### 2. The decisions

1. **Where the bits are lifted: in the reason row and the conflict row, before anything
   resolves.** `Ladder.instantiate ~bits ~row ~pivot ~falsified` finds every bits block of the
   row by its bit 0 (one pass over the sorted terms) and adds, at multiplier `a` (the block's
   coefficient on bit 0), one line per block: a POSITIVE block `a * X'` (a row helped by a large
   x) reads x's UPPER bound u -- B2 of `x_ge_(u+1)`, leaving `a K x_ge_(u+1)` and the degree
   lowered by `a (u - lo)`, or `@ub` at the declared high, leaving nothing; a NEGATIVE block
   reads the LOWER bound l -- B1 of `x_ge_l`, leaving `a k ~x_ge_l`, or `@lb`. The bridges are
   summed and added to the row in one `Learned.combine` (they name disjoint variables). A bit
   left over, a block of a variable the encoding does not know, or a pivot outside the declared
   range is `Mixed_row`, a fallback with its reason, never a row with a bit in it. So no learned
   row, no criterion, no level computation and no `Pb` instance ever sees a `Lit.Bit`.
2. **Which bound: the one in force under the frozen predicate, and the PIVOT's atom for the
   pruned block.** The bound is read off the same `falsified_before ~at` the reduction uses
   (I-X6), by binary search over the declared range for the tightest `u` whose atom is reported
   falsified (O(log w) asks of the bound history). Its atom is then falsified under that
   predicate, so the block contributes to the slack exactly what the integer propagator read.
   The block of the pivot's variable, when its direction matches the pivot's, is instantiated at
   the pivot's own value (B1 of `x_ge_v` for the pivot `~x_ge_v`, B2 for `x_ge_v`), which puts
   the pivot in the row at `a k_v` (resp. `a K_v`): the learned row names the pivot, and the
   entry that falsified it may have pushed further. The arithmetic, for an upper push from
   `Linear` with the others at their bounds: Linear deduced `a X' <= K` with `K / a < k_v`; the
   instantiated row is `a k_v ~x_ge_v + (falsified atoms) >= a k_v - K`, slack `K < a k_v`, so
   the pivot is propagated and `Reduce`'s postcondition (slack exactly 0 after the division)
   holds. A pruning that settled past a hole can fall short, and the postcondition says so: a
   fallback (3 such in the suite at `W = 0`, section 5).
3. **The conflict row the same way, at the conflict, with no pivot.** Every atom is then
   falsified and the slack is the integer slack `Linear` found negative.
4. **Minted on demand, at level 0.** `bits.bridge` is `Encoding.ensure_atom` (through
   `Pb_analysis.bits_of_ctx`), which writes the `red` pair and its sparse links the first time
   the atom is named and memoises it after; almost every atom asked for is already on the page,
   because the trace names the same bounds. A bridge is a level-0 line never deleted before the
   conclusion (D-0132 section 2.8), so pb_analysis.ml's I-S4 discharge stands with one more kind
   of leaf (its header says so) and the I-S4 `Debug.check` at the call site is unchanged. The
   atoms are minted during the analysis, before the learned row's `pol`, also when the analysis
   later falls back; that is a level-0 line like any other, and it keeps the debug and release
   builds on the same line order. `ensure_atom`'s precondition (no root contradiction) holds:
   PB analysis runs at a conflict below the root.
5. **Not taken: the bits row itself as an antecedent (p6).** Adding conflict and reason with
   multipliers that cancel the pivot variable's whole block is IntSat's integer elimination, and
   p6 shows it can learn more. It leaves every other variable's block in the learned row, and a
   `Bit` is a literal the criterion, `asserting_level`, the pivot choice and `Pb` cannot read (it
   is never falsified by a bound); where the reason is not tight, `b * slack_C + a * r` can be
   non-negative and the conflict is lost to rounding, which `Reduce` exists to repair over 0-1
   literals and has no counterpart for over an integer block. It would be its own row, with a
   bits-aware slack.
6. **The row is offered as the .opb holds it, which needs `Linear.pb_row ?bits_n` and
   `compile.ml`'s `~mixed`.** D-0132 section 2.7 packed a mixed `Linear` WITHOUT its row; now
   `~mixed` is `None` (no bits term: the order expansion, byte for byte what it was) or
   `Some bits_n` (`Encoding.bits_n`), and `Linear.pb_row ~bits_n` spells a bits term as
   `a * 2^i` on `x_bit_i` with the same `a * lo` fold. `test_compile` asserts that the row
   offered is the committed .opb row term for term; the `int_lin_le`, `int_lin_eq`, arith and
   `bool2int`-over-bits faces all go through it. `pb_row` also lost its quadratic `acc @ block`
   (the same list).
7. **No `learned.ml` change, no new `Explanation` constructor, no search.ml change beyond the
   call site's `~bits:(Pb_analysis.bits_of_ctx ctx)`.** The derivation is `Combine`s of
   `Model_row`s; `Justify` writes it as it writes every PB derivation (D-0131: `pol`, stated by
   `ia`).

## D-0151  M7-T28 continued: `regular`'s reasons on the letters (every tail recurses into the dead flags' own lines, so a learned clause names cells and not states), `inverse` native in two stages (channel filtering, then all_different over each array from cited root lemmas), and `member` designed with probes

**Status**: **DONE** (2026-11-19, agent-globals2, `wave51-globals2`). The contract is ROADMAP row
M7-T28 and D-0146's two open items: section 5's "smaller reasons (on letters only) are the
obvious next lever" and section 7's `inverse` design. Section 1 is `regular`'s reasons (design,
checker probes before the OCaml, implementation, measurement), section 2 `inverse` (stage 1,
stage 2 and its API, the Challenge), section 3 `member` (a design record with probes, no code),
section 4 what was checked.

### 1. `regular`'s reasons on the letters

**1.1 What D-0146 left.** A flag death's reason was its dead predecessors (`s <= 0` facts), a
letter pruning's the dead flags on its edges. 1UIP learning then cut on FLAGS: a learned clause
named states of one row's automaton, which only that row's propagator can read back, and on the
nonograms of D-0146 section 6 nearly every clause sat in the stock histogram's `>= 16` bucket.

**1.2 The design: recursion through the flags' own lines.** The literature's explanation of a
layered graph -- Gange, Stuckey and Szymanek, "MDD propagators with explanation" (Constraints
16(4), 2011), on the decision diagram Pesant's filtering (CP 2004) walks; the g-nogoods of
Katsirelos and Bacchus (AAAI 2005), whose literals are the variables' removed values -- explains
`x_i <> v` by killing every `v`-edge of layer `i` ABOVE (its source unreachable), BELOW (its
target unable to reach the end) or by its LETTER (the value removed), and the letters it cites
are the ones where an edge leaves a LIVE state. GCS (`dev_docs/regular.md` on fataepyc-06) does
not compute such reasons at all: GCS does not learn, so its `Regular` justifies with the whole
current domain and cache-gated `~state[i][q]` lines.

The proof is what decides the shape here. A tail of letters only is in general NOT RUP in one
line against the rows and the backward lemmas: a state's death several layers past the letters
that caused it is a case split over the intermediate letters' values, which unit propagation
cannot do. It IS RUP once the flags it passes through are dead on the page -- and they are: every
flag death is a trail entry whose trace line Trace writes, oldest first, before any line that
rests on it. So the rule is:

- where D-0146 cited a dead flag `s(i,q) <= 0`, cite the TAIL of the line that killed it, which
  is letter facts by the same rule one level down. Assume the new tail and that flag's line
  fires (its tail is a subset), so every argument of D-0146 section 3.4 goes through unchanged;
- a letter is cited only where it must be: in a forward death (P1), per value `v` of `x_i`'s
  alphabet, if every predecessor on `v` is dead, recurse into their tails; otherwise `v` is out
  of the domain and is cited as the WEAKEST bound excluding every such value (`x_i >= v+1` for
  the largest below the live lower bound, `x_i <= v-1` for the smallest above the upper one), or
  inside `[lo, hi]` through the hole's remover. A backward death (P2) the same with successors.
  A value removal (P3) takes, per state with an edge on `v`, the dead side whose tail adds fewer
  new facts. A flag fixed to 1 (P4) takes the tails of the rest of its layer; a flag killed by
  the one fixed in its layer (P5), that one's tail; a conflict, the union of what it reads;
- the tails are kept as the STRONGEST fact per letter and direction (`x >= 3` subsumes
  `x >= 2` through the ladder), so a tail has at most two facts per letter however deep;
- a flag moved by anything but this instance (under the engine, a decision on a flag) has no
  tail of ours and is cited as itself.

"Recurse rather than cite" is Gange's preference: it keeps the cited letters at the FRONTIER, so
a death far from a decision cites the decision, not the letters it forced on the way.

**1.3 Checked on the checker first.** `bench/regular_spike/gen_letters_probe.py` is a Python
reference of the five steps of `regular.ml` with these reasons, run on random automata (Q = 3
to 5, letters of 2 to 4 values, 4 to 6 letters, one or TWO bound decisions per round so a
domain-consistent propagator meets conflicts below the root) and three nonogram automata; the
proof is every pruning in trail order, as Trace writes it. `probe_letters.sh`, VeriPB 3.0.2
(`d5644ca4`) on fataepyc-06, 60 scenes:

| what | verdict |
|---|---|
| the 60 proofs, every line letter-tailed (19 end in a conflict) | **60 accepted** |
| each line with a non-empty tail, its LAST fact dropped (578 variants) | 539 refused at the RUP wording, 39 accepted (the fact was redundant for unit propagation: the explanation is greedy, not minimum) |
| every flag line removed, up to the first letter or conflict line with a tail (40 variants) | 12 refused at the RUP wording: the flags' own lines are load-bearing; in the other 28 the line happened to be RUP alone |

**1.4 As built.** `lib/core/prop/regular.ml` only (its header rewritten around it): the letters
are SLOTS (one per distinct variable of the word), a reason under construction is stamped
scratch arrays indexed by (slot, direction) -- no hashing on the common path, D-0146 section 5's
lesson -- and each flag line's tail is kept per flag as packed (key, value) pairs WITH the trail
entry it belongs to. A tail is read back through the entry that moved the flag now
(`Store.hi_support`/`lo_support`), and a cache hit is that same entry by physical equality, so a
flag revived by a backtrack and moved again by a decision is cited as itself, never through a
stale tail. No new `Explanation` constructor, no `deriving_ahead`, nothing outside the module.

Tests: `test/unit/test_prop.ml`'s new brute force audits every reason (2 747 over 300 automata x
2 narrowing rounds, 341 of them conflicts): each is SOUND over the DECLARED domains -- every
accepted word satisfying the facts keeps the claim -- and no fact names a flag the propagator
moved (675 flag facts, all on flags the scene fixed); widest tail 5. D-0146's brute force
(I-P1, domain consistency, I-P2), its veripb proof and its three mutation lanes (`lemma-rhs`,
`death-fact`, `no-lemmas`) all hold unchanged: the `death-fact` line's tail is now the one fact
`x1 <= 3`, the WEAKEST bound excluding the letter 4 under the decision `x1 <= 2`. The four
`regular` models verify.

**1.5 Measured.** Two runs, on fataepyc-06, over the instances D-0146 section 6 found reaching
`regular` alone (`/scratch/arthur/wave51-globals2-regonly.lst`, 65: 20 nonograms, 20
pentominoes in three models, 10 peaceable, 15 traveling-tppv), each re-flattened with this
branch's mznlib (the `regular` route is D-0146's, unchanged). "Before" is main at this branch's
base (`9c1b8e6`, the same `lib/` and `bin/` as `e34e133`), "after" this branch.

*(a) The widths, without the proof.* The stock `--stats` width histogram stops at a `>= 16`
bucket, and that is where 98 to 99 % of the learned clauses land on both sides -- the first
reading of the proof-on run below would have called the change a no-op. So the 40 nonograms
and pentominoes were run again on binaries whose bucket is widened to 4 096 (a two-line edit
of `search.ml`'s histogram in throwaway clones; nothing else differs), 120 s, `--no-proof`
(`bench/regular_spike/meas_width.sh`, `summ_width.py`), with a third binary, **V1**, that
prefers the letter's own bound to the recursion wherever both are available (Gange's other
choice: the local literal first):

| 40 instances, 120 s | complete | nodes/s | learned clauses | width: mean | width: median of the per-run medians |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| main (flag reasons, D-0146) | 16 | 40.6 | 68 287 | 321.1 | 594 |
| **V0** (this branch: recursion first) | **20** | **107.5** | 161 561 | **80.0** | **50** |
| V1 (the letter's bound first) | 20 | 108.2 | 166 790 | 83.8 | 75 |

The learned clauses are FOUR times shorter on average (and twelve times at the median run),
the node rate 2.6 times higher (smaller reasons to materialise, shorter clauses to watch), and
four more instances complete in the time. V1 changes little; V0 is kept, being the slightly
shorter and faster of the two on the instances both solve (mean 27.5 s against 32.5 s).
Not every instance moves the same way: `2012_nonogram_non_awful_5` is solved by main in 71 s
and by neither variant in 120 s (16 351 nodes), so shorter clauses do not always mean a better
search -- the cut lands elsewhere, and the backjumps with it.

*(b) The answers, with the proof.* All 65 instances, 300 s, proof on, `--max-heap-mb 8192`,

| 65 instances reaching `regular` alone | complete | incumbent | no answer | nodes/s | proofs |

| before (main, flag reasons) | 19 | 17 | 29 | 34.4 | 19 VERIFIED |
| after (letter reasons) | **20** | 17 | 28 | **54.5** | **20 VERIFIED**, none rejected |

By family, complete before -> after: nonograms 12 -> 10 of 20, pentominoes 4 -> 6 of 10,
pentominoes-int 2 -> 3 of 5, pentominoes-zayenz 1 -> 1 of 5, peaceable 0 -> 0 of 10 (an
incumbent on all ten, both sides), traveling-tppv 0 -> 0 of 15 (an incumbent on seven, both
sides). Gained: the three
`pentominoes_05` (2011, 2013 int, 2020), each in about 100 s where main timed out; lost:
`2012_nonogram_non_awful_3` (284 s before) and `non_awful_5` (87 s before), the instance the
width run already showed. On the 17 instances both sides answer, the time goes from 671 s to
507 s in total, faster on 11 of them. (D-0146 section 6 counted 18 complete with the binary
`08361947`; main has moved since, and completes 19 here.)

**Reading.** The lever D-0146 named is real and measured: learned clauses four times shorter,
the node rate up by half with the proof on (2.6 times without it), and the pentominoes, whose
letters take one value per tile, are where it pays in answers. On the nonograms the count does
not move up: two are lost, and the 1UIP cut over cells lands on a different, shorter, not
uniformly better clause. What to try next for them is no longer in the reasons: a search
that restarts and keeps its phases (M10's alternate configuration, M7-T30's row), so that the
deeper backjumps a shorter clause allows stop costing the work they discard.

### 2. `inverse`, native in two stages

**2.1 The route.** `mznlib/fzn_inverse.mzn` keeps std's index-set restrictions (`f[i] in
index_set(invf)` and the mirror, which tighten the declarations when the flattener can) and
replaces std's `invf[f[i]] = i` element chains by ONE call `baguette_inverse(f, fmin, g, gmin)`,
the two first indices carrying the index sets (FlatZinc arrays are 1-based); both arrays empty is
`true`. `Model.Inverse` with its oracle arm, `Builder`'s `baguette_inverse` arm, SPEC 2.1's row
and relation (normative), `Compile.post_inverse`.

**2.2 Stage 1: channel filtering** (`lib/core/prop/inverse.ml`, new). The `.opb` holds D-0146
section 7.1's channel clauses, both directions, each `x = v` split into its two order halves,
with every literal about a constant or a value outside a declared domain FOLDED at compile time
(the row is dropped when a literal is true, the literal when it is false, so a constant that
contradicts the relation leaves the empty row), and a unit row wherever a declared domain reaches
outside the other index set. One call restricts every value to the other index set, then makes
`j in dom(f_i) <=> i in dom(g_j)` hold both ways; a second call changes nothing when no variable
repeats across the arrays (`~idempotent` is packed only then: an involution passes the same
variables twice and the second pass can owe the first). Consistency **Checking**: arc consistent
on each channel pair, not domain consistent on `inverse` (a value set no matching covers is
all_different's to see). Every pruning is ONE `rup`: removing `i` from `g_j` because `j` is out
of `dom(f_i)` cites the weakest bound excluding `j` (or the hole's remover), LAST, after the bound
fact that pins `g_j` to `i` when `i` is a bound -- D-0146 probes `i1` to `i3`. I-X10:
`Single_row` (`test/unit/test_trace.ml`'s table).

**2.3 Stage 2: all_different over each array, from CITED root lemmas.** Both arrays are
permutations, so `all_different(f)` and `all_different(g)` are implied, and `alldiff.ml` over
each prunes what a matching sees and the channel does not -- the pigeonhole `f1, f2, f3 <= 2`
over `1..5`, which leaves the channel with `g3, g4, g5` in `4..5`. Its Hall derivations cite the
pairwise rows `x <> v \/ z <> v` by id. The `.opb` must not state them (an implied row posted is
a stronger model nothing checks); they are ROOT LEMMAS, `rup` from `CH(i, v)` and `CH(k, v)`
(probe `i4`), or from the restriction rows for a `v` outside the other index set. What D-0146
section 7.3 left open was the API, since a lemma's id exists only once `Encoding.start_proof` has
written it and alldiff is built at compile time:

- `Encoding.add_cited_lemma` registers a lemma like `add_root_lemma` and returns a HANDLE;
  `Encoding.root_lemma_id` resolves it once the proof has started (`None` before, and for ever
  under `--no-proof`). The lemmas are written in registration order, retired by the end-of-run
  sweep. The comment line before them is D-0146's, byte for byte, when no lemma is cited, so a
  model with only `regular`'s backward chains writes what it wrote before.
- `alldiff.ml` gets ONE thing, said in its header: `make ?lemma_rows`, and `row` resolving a
  lemma handle to its id when a derivation is rendered. The counting, the cancellations and every
  `pol` are the ones a model row gets -- a `pol` cites a derived line exactly as a model row.

`post_inverse` posts one such alldiff per array when its operands are pairwise distinct
variables (a repeat is an involution's or a unification's, and alldiff's Hall test is by name)
and the model does not already post `all_different_int` over the same set; it requests the
direct encoding of the array, as `post_all_different` does. A constant in an array is left to
the channel. Lemmas: one per pair of positions per shared declared value.

**Whether alldiff's derivations survive citing proof lines, measured on the solver's own
output** (the stage-2 probe D-0146 asked for): `test/unit/test_mutation.ml`'s `inverse` instance
(18 cited lemmas) verifies and its two lanes are refused at the RUP wording -- `channel-fact`
(the channel pruning `g2 >= 2` under the decision `f1 <= 1`, its excluding fact dropped) and
`lemma-rhs` (a pairwise lemma's degree raised); `test/models/inverse_unsat.fzn`, the pigeonhole,
is refuted at the ROOT by stage 2 (34 nodes under stage 1, 1 node now) and its UNSAT proof, whose
conclusion rests on alldiff's Hall `pol`s over lemma ids, is VERIFIED; and the Challenge's
`2011_black-hole_10` (one inverse over 52 positions, 138 K cited lemmas, 345 K proof lines) is
refuted at the root in 24 s and VERIFIED UNSATISFIABLE by 3.0.2 in 4.8 s, where the decomposition
timed out at 1 200 s in wave 43 (Chuffed: UNSAT in 0.1 s).

**2.4 Tests and models.** `test/unit/test_prop.ml`, brute force over 400 random scenes (f and g
of 2 or 3 positions, some of different lengths, f sometimes declared one value wider on each
side, random bound narrowings and holes): I-P1, channel consistency after the call, I-P2, and
every reason SOUND over the declared domains (1 420 reasons, 127 conflicts) -- the scene's holes
are punched with no facts, as a root hole is, so the audit holds every solution to them the way
the page holds it to a root line. `test/unit/test_compile.ml`, eight inline scenes brute-forced,
solved and veripb-checked: SAT under search, index sets from 0 and 1, a constant in `f`, a
constant no `g` can mirror (UNSAT), declared domains wider than the index sets, three `f` into
two `g` (UNSAT), and an involution `f = g`. Models from `mznlib/test/inverse_src_*.mzn`
(MUST-EMIT `baguette_inverse`, MUST-NOT-EMIT `int_eq_reif`): `inverse_sat`,
`inverse_unsat` (the pigeonhole), `inverse_offset_sat` (index sets `0..3` and `10..13`, a
constant folded into `f` by the flattener, a set domain); every proof VERIFIED.
`check_mznlib.sh`: 29 ok, 0 failed.

**2.5 The Challenge.** Selected by SOURCE as a superset (`\binverse\s*\(` in the model or its
includes: 70 instances, `/scratch/arthur/wave51-globals2-inv-cand.lst`), then counted by the
route the FLATTENED model takes, D-0146 section 6's rule (`bench/regular_spike/inverse_routes.sh`):
all 70 reach `baguette_inverse` -- black-hole (15, one call over 52 positions), elitserien
handball (20, 21 calls over 14), p1f (5, 11 to 16 calls over 12 to 17), p1f-pjs (10, 9 to 21
calls over 10 to 22), tdtsp (15, two calls over 11 or 21), travelling-thief (5, one call over 10
or 20). Each run re-flattened by its own checkout's mznlib (main reaches std's decomposition),
300 s, proof on, 8 GB heap budget, every complete answer checked by veripb 3.0.2
(`bench/regular_spike/meas_pair.sh`; `/scratch/arthur/wave51-globals2-meas-inv/`; binaries
`bb8ccd8b` main at `9c1b8e6`, `d5581237` this branch at `c9d46e1`, the same `lib/` as the head):

| 70 instances reaching `baguette_inverse` | complete | incumbent | no answer | proofs |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| main (std's decomposition) | 3 | 12 | 55 | 3 VERIFIED |
| this branch (channel + stage 2) | 3 | 12 | 55 | 3 VERIFIED, none rejected |

By family the two agree everywhere but two instances: `2011_black-hole_10` is refuted at the
root in 24 s by stage 2 (main timed out), and `2015_p1f_13`, UNSAT in 58 s under the
decomposition, times out natively. The three incumbents whose value both runs report are
equal; tdtsp keeps 10 incumbents of 15, elitserien and black-hole stay without an answer
where they were. Two refusals are the heap budget's, not the route's
(`2023_travelling-thief_n20_k20`: the decomposition aborts at the OCaml allocation failure
and the native route is refused by the 8 GB budget, both at 135 s; `2025_black-hole_layout_14`:
main times out, the native run is refused at 314 s). Stage 1 alone was run on the first eight
instances (all black-hole) before the run was narrowed to two binaries for time: it answers
one of them, where main answers two and stage 2 three -- `2013_black-hole_6` is refuted at the
root by the decomposition and by stage 2, not by the channel alone.

**Why the reach did not move, measured rather than guessed.** Two causes, both outside the
inverse propagator, each found on its family:

- *black-hole: 99 % of the run is `Element.add_facts`.* `perf` on a frame-pointer build
  (`2011_black-hole_20`, stage 1): 99 % in `Element.pass`, 93 % of it in the `List.mem` of
  `add_facts`' quadratic dedup (polymorphic compare of facts holding `X_INTRODUCED_` names).
  3 to 27 nodes in 300 s on main and on this branch alike: the 102 `array_int_element` of
  the model, not the inverse, hold the search. Filed as a cross-session request (M11).
- *p1f: the native route learns NOTHING.* On `2015_p1f_13` stage 1 and stage 2 both run with
  `learned = 0` (main: 523 in 58 s). A debug build of `Learn.at_conflict` on stage 2: all 128
  conflicts of a 15 s run give an EMPTY cut, and the ones printed are `all_different_int` Hall
  conflicts with no facts (the model posts 145 all_different; stage 1, which adds none, learns
  nothing either) -- and
  `alldiff.ml` reports its conflicts with `Reason.none` on purpose (its comment: the Hall
  argument is a `pol`, and `rup ~facts >= 1` would not be RUP). A factless conflict gives the
  1UIP walk nothing to resolve. Under std's decomposition main learns, presumably because the
  decomposition's reified rows, which do report facts, meet the contradictions before alldiff
  does (not measured further). The fix is alldiff's, and has its precedent:
  give the Hall conflict its facts and write its `pol` AHEAD of the `rup` (`deriving_ahead`),
  as cumulative (D-0096) and element (D-0101) did -- the next row, not this one, since
  alldiff.ml here carries only the lemma-row hook.

### 3. `member`: the design record, with probes, no code

D-0122: 40 instances. std's `fzn_member_int(x, y)` is `exists(i)(x[i] == y)`: `n` reified
equalities and a clause. ROADMAP's note called it "a disjunction of equalities over a View".

**3.1 The rows.** A SELECTOR Boolean `b_i` per position, introduced by the mznlib `let` the way
`regular`'s flags are (so a selector is a store variable and its death a trail entry), the clause
`OR_i b_i`, and per position `i` and value `v` of `y`'s declared domain the two halves of
`b_i /\ y = v -> x_i = v` over order literals,

    ~b_i \/ y <> v \/ x_i >= v        ~b_i \/ y <> v \/ x_i <= v

constant halves folded as `inverse` folds them: `2 n |dom y|` clauses of at most four literals,
`n` Booleans, one direction suffices (with `b_i` and `x_i = w <> y`, the row at `v = y` already
forces `x_i = y`). No direct encoding.

**3.2 The propagator it implies.** Domain consistency is cheap: `v` in `dom(y)` survives iff some
live `b_i` has `v` in `dom(x_i)`; `b_i` dies iff `dom(x_i)` and `dom(y)` share no value; when one
selector is left it is fixed to 1 and `x_i` and `y` are made equal domain-wise; with two or more
left, nothing about the `x` can be pruned. Every pruning one `rup`, its tail on the letters by
section 1's rule -- a selector is to `member` what a state flag is to `regular`.

**3.3 Measured on the checker** (`bench/regular_spike/gen_member_probe.py`,
`probe_member.sh`, 3.0.2 on fataepyc-06; `x1, x2, x3, y` in `1..4`, a model row `x3 <> 2`
standing for a hole the page holds):

| probe | content | verdict |
|---|---|---|
| m1 | `y <> 2` (interior), facts `x1 >= 3`, `x2 <= 1`, the hole of `x3` | VERIFIED |
| m2 | m1 with `x1 >= 3` dropped | refused, RUP wording |
| m3 | `y <= 3`, every `x_i <= 3` | VERIFIED |
| m4 | one position left: `x1 <= 2` from `y <= 2` and the facts `~b2`, `~b3` | VERIFIED |
| m5 | the same claim on the LETTERS alone (`x2 >= 3`, `x3 >= 3` for the selectors) | refused, RUP wording |
| m5b | m5 after the two SELECTOR deaths `~b2 \/ ~(y <= 2) \/ ~(x2 >= 3)` and the same for `b3` | VERIFIED |
| m6 | a wrong pruning (`y <> 2` with `x2` free) | refused, RUP wording |
| m7 / m7b | the selector `b1` fixed as the last one, letters alone / after the two selector deaths | refused / VERIFIED |
| m8 | `sol` y = x2 = 3 with `b2` | VERIFIED SATISFIABLE |
| m9 | `sol` of a word no position matches | refused, "falsifies the constraint" |

m5 against m5b is the design fact worth keeping: a selector's death is a case split over `y`'s
values (`b2` with `y <= 2` and `x2 >= 3` contradicts on `y = 1` and on `y = 2` separately), so a
letters-only line is RUP only once the selectors' own lines are on the page. That is exactly
section 1's situation, and its answer applies unchanged: selectors as store variables, their
deaths trail entries with letter tails (each RUP alone by a sweep over `y`'s values, m5b's first
two lines), and every later line recursing into those tails. Not built: the row's next step is
the propagator, its brute force and lanes, and the census of which Challenge instances reach
`fzn_member_int` once flattened.

### 4. What was checked, and what was not changed

- **Files.** `lib/core/prop/regular.ml` (the reasons), `lib/core/prop/inverse.ml` (new),
  `lib/core/prop/alldiff.ml` (the lemma-row hook only, said in its header),
  `lib/proof/encoding.ml` (the root-lemma block: a count, `add_cited_lemma`, `root_lemma_id`),
  `lib/flatzinc/{model,builder,compile}.ml` (the `Inverse` arms, `post_inverse`),
  `mznlib/fzn_inverse.mzn`, SPEC 2.1 (normative row and relation), PROOF-FORMAT section 4 (the
  `regular` note, the `inverse` row), ARCHITECTURE section 1 and CLAUDE.md's map. No
  `Explanation` constructor, nothing in `search.ml`, `learn.ml`, `analysis.ml`, `trace.ml`,
  `retention.ml`, `writer.ml` (`wave50-proofbugs`) or in `bin/main.ml`, `output.ml`,
  `tools/baguette.msc` (`wave51-flags`).
- **The M2-T10 oracle** (`BAGUETTE_CONSISTENCY=1`) on the seven `regular` and `inverse` models:
  `CHECKED: regular (domain)` x8 and x1, `all_different_int (domain)` x4 on each SAT inverse
  model (the stage-2 instances), `inverse (checking)` with no obligation at its level, no
  violation; `regular_opt` skips nine instance-checks over the tuple cap, as in D-0146.
  `BAGUETTE_DEBUG=1` and the I-X2 audit on: all seven VERIFIED.
- **Pre-existing, not this branch:** `test/unit/test_retention.ml`'s five `deep shipped` checks
  fail on main from `36c1312` on (bisected: `a0b50da` 0 failures, `36c1312` 5) -- the M10-T4
  hook that routes learned instances through `Retention.gate`. A cross-session request is filed
  for its owner; `dune runtest --root . --force` on this branch fails on exactly those five.
- **Gate** (fresh clone of `wave51-globals2` at `d1df37f` on fataepyc-06, binary `0ec2649f`,
  `/scratch/arthur/gate53.sh` with its two `--update` lines removed, `make -k check` under
  `ulimit -v 4000000`): rc 2, and only from the five pre-existing `test_retention` checks above
  (main `9c1b8e6` fails the same five); everything else passes -- fmt clean, width lint clean,
  determinism 195 models identical, `check_unlimited` ok, 104 mutation checks, model tests 195
  passed; peak RSS 100 104 kB. Every test model against main's binary at the branch base
  (`bb8ccd8b`, `9c1b8e6`): 181 of 195 byte-identical in `.out`, exit code, `.opb` and `.pbp`;
  the 14 differences are the three `inverse_*` models (the old binary cannot read
  `baguette_inverse`, four artefacts each) and the `.pbp` of `regular_opt` and `regular_unsat`
  (the letter reasons; `regular_sat` and `regular_set_sat` solve at the root and are

  default-configuration runs equal the reference; the 117 that differ are all in the `fifo`,
