## D-0162  M7-T29 (the `fplen` half): `connect__0086_02` is a correct refusal under SPEC 2.1; capping a variable from the objective would be a dominance argument, and is PROPOSED for the user, not built

Status: PROPOSED. Nothing changed in the solver; the SPEC sentence in section 3 awaits the user.
Date: 2026-11-19
Task: M7-T29, the `fplen` half (agent-fplen, `wave54-fplen`).
Touches: `test/unit/test_flatzinc.ml` (one `reject` case pinning the shape). No solver code.
Follows D-0083 (bounds inference, which already called this refusal correct), D-0121.

### 1. The cause

`2021_MZNC_connect_connect__0086_02` is the only one of the five `connect` instances with a
positive floor-plan cost (`dFPUnitCost__PERIM = 100`, `nFPUnits = 0`; the four others have both
costs 0, so `fpSz = [0, 0]`). Its perimeter branch states only
`fpSz[c] >= fpPosXY_F[c] - fpPosXY[c]` and `fpSzCost[c] = fpSz[c] * 1`, and the objective
minimises `PIPECOST + SUPPCOST + FPCOST`. Flattened: `int_lin_le([-1,1,-1],[fplen,X2775,X2773],0)`
(`X2775` in 54939..112000, `X2773` in 0..1) and `int_lin_eq([1,-1,-1],[FPCOST,fplen,fpwid],0)`,
then `OBJ__PHASE_1 = FPCOST + SUPPCOST + PIPECOST`. Nothing bounds `fplen`, `fpwid`, `FPCOST` or
`OBJ__PHASE_1` above: the model's solution set really is unbounded in them (any `fplen >= 54938`
extends a solution). SPEC 2.1's inference MUST be sound for every solution, so no rule, extended
or not, may bound them. The refusal (binary `c72c48e2`) names `fplen`, lower bound 54938, and
three other undomained variables.

### 2. What a bound would need

The only finite bound is a DOMINANCE one: `fplen` occurs in one lower-bound row and with a positive
coefficient in the minimised cost, so any solution with `fplen > max(X2775) - min(X2773) = 112000`
is matched by one with `fplen = 112000` and a strictly better objective. That keeps the optimum and
loses solutions, so it violates 2.1's soundness sentence as written, and the `.opb` would encode
the capped model: VeriPB would certify the optimum of a model the user did not write, by an
argument it never checks (or the cap has to be derived in the proof, a `red` whose witness moves
`fplen` to a value depending on other variables, which the order encoding does not express as a
substitution).

### 3. The SPEC sentence it would need (for the user)

> A `var int` with no declared domain that occurs only (a) in rows bounding it from below and
> (b) with a positive coefficient in a chain of equalities defining a minimised objective (the
> mirror for maximise) MAY be capped at the largest value its lower-bound rows can require. The
> capped model has the same optimal value, not the same solutions; a solution printed is a
> solution of the original model, and the proof certifies the capped model, which the
> diagnostic on stderr says.

### 4. What the cap would buy (measured on a hand-patched `.fzn`, binary `c72c48e2`)

`fplen` declared 54938..112000 and `fpwid` 24992..62000 by hand
(`/scratch/arthur/wave54-fplen-runs/fplen_capped.fzn`), everything else as flattened. The model
then compiles, but it has the four siblings' shape: `PIPECOST` is declared 0..216000000,
`SUPPCOST` 0..86000000, and 217 auxiliaries 0..1000000. On the order encoding the `.opb` passed
51 GB within five minutes, still in the encoding (stopped by its PID; the siblings were CAPPED at
about 370 GB in wave 41, ELIGIBILITY-wave41). With `--bits-above 10000`: see section 5.

### 5. The bits run

Same patched `.fzn`, `--bits-above 10000 --width-warn none --proof --time-limit 1200
--max-heap-mb 16384`, under `systemd-run -p MemoryMax=32G`: 1 166 variables on bits (110 held back
by `element`), `.opb` 0.93 GB. The run stopped on the HEAP BUDGET after 15 min 25 s (exit 5,
peak RSS 26.2 GB), with no solution printed and a 0.77 GB `.pbp` (nothing to verify). So the cap
alone does not make the instance answerable: it would turn a refusal at parse time into a
memory death in the search, the fate of 14 other wide instances in D-0121. The user's call is
whether that is worth a normative sentence that changes what the proof certifies; this record's
recommendation is NO for now, and to revisit it with the bits encoding's `element` (the 110
held-back variables).

## D-0163  M9-no-proof-T5: the default run keeps its proof -- `./<model>.opb` and `.pbp` in the current directory, `./baguette-proof` under MiniZinc, overwritten by the next run, and the directory still the user's to confirm

**Status**: DONE 2026-11-19 (agent-keepproof, branch `wave54-keepproof`). Implements the user's
decision of 2026-11-19 recorded in the ROADMAP row: a run without `--proof` writes its proof and
KEEPS it, under a name taken from the model; `--proof PREFIX` chooses the name; `--no-proof` is
the run without a proof. The directory is the proposal on record, not yet confirmed.

### 1. What a run without `--proof` did, and does

Until this row, `bin/main.ml` opened `Filename.temp_file "baguette" ".pbp"`, wrote the proof into
it and deleted it at the end, and wrote no `.opb` at all (`Encoding.row_sink` stayed at
`Discard_rows`, so the model rows were dropped at the door). The answer such a run printed came
with a proof nobody could check, which SPEC §1 ("a primary output") did not mean.

Now `parse_args` resolves the prefix once. `opts.proof_prefix` is `None` exactly under
`--no-proof`, and every other run is a `--proof PREFIX` run with PREFIX from
`default_proof_prefix`: the rows stream to `PREFIX.opb.rows`, the `.opb` is written before the
proof, the `.pbp` is opened at `PREFIX.pbp`, and nothing is deleted. The temporary file and its
cleanup closure are gone. A consequence for D-0161 §6's request to `compile.ml`: `Discard_rows`
now means `--no-proof` and nothing else, so it IS the no-proof signal at compile time that
request said was missing.

### 2. The naming rule, in one function

`default_proof_prefix` in `bin/main.ml`, whose header states the rule and that the directory is
the user's to confirm. Changing it is an edit to that function alone.

| Model given | Files kept | stderr |
|---|---|---|
| `DIR/foo.fzn` | `./foo.opb`, `./foo.pbp` (current directory) | nothing (M1-T49) |
| `DIR/foo` (no `.fzn`) | `./foo.opb`, `./foo.pbp` | nothing |
| `DIR/x.pbp` | `./x.pbp.opb`, `./x.pbp.pbp` (only `.fzn` is dropped, so a model is never its proof's name) | nothing |
| `/tmp/mznfileXXXXXX.fzn` (MiniZinc) | `./baguette-proof.opb`, `./baguette-proof.pbp` | one line with both full paths |
| anything, with `--proof P` | `P.opb`, `P.pbp` | nothing |
| anything, with `--no-proof` | none | nothing |

The MiniZinc case, measured on 2.10.1 with a fake solver that logs its argv, cwd and
environment: `minizinc --solver S m.mzn` runs the solver in the caller's cwd with argv = the
flags, then `/tmp/mznfile<6 random chars>.fzn`. Neither the argv, the environment nor the `.fzn`
names the `.mzn`. A name from the model would be a new meaningless name on every run, so the
rule recognises MiniZinc's temporary name (`mznfile*.fzn`, the prefix of MiniZinc's
`FileUtils::TmpFile`) and uses a fixed `baguette-proof` in the cwd, and says where on stderr,
because the user never typed that name. `tools/baguette.msc` gains `--no-proof` as a `bool`
extraFlag beside the existing `--proof` string flag (measured: MiniZinc passes `--no-proof` only
when given). So `minizinc --solver baguette --proof out m.mzn` names the proof and
`--no-proof` skips it. Checked end to end with the real MiniZinc and the built solver: the
default run leaves `baguette-proof.opb`/`.pbp`, which veripb verifies (`VERIFIED BOUNDS`).

The alternative for MiniZinc was to recognise any model in the temp directory. It was not taken
because a user who keeps a model in `/tmp` would get `baguette-proof` instead of its name.

### 3. Overwriting

A file of the same name is overwritten without a word, as `--proof PREFIX` always did and as a
compiler overwrites its output: it is the previous run's proof. The cost of that choice is that
two runs of the same model, or two MiniZinc runs, in the same directory at the same time write
over each other's proof. Give each its own `--proof`. A refusal before the solve (exit 2 at the
front end) writes nothing; a resource death mid-proof prints the existing INCOMPLETE warning,
now worded "A proof was being written" since the user may not have asked for one.

### 4. The lanes and tests that ran without `--proof`

Found by grep over every script, test and bench file that names the binary. SPEC §1 says
`make check` always proves, so the in-gate ones take a scratch prefix, not `--no-proof`.

- `test/unit/test_endtoend.ml`: the M7-T32 flag runs name `--proof plain` in their temp dir when
  the run names none, and the lane ends by checking no default-named proof appeared. New lane
  `test_m9t5_default_keeps_proof`, 12 checks: (a) the default run keeps exactly `./keep.opb` and
  `./keep.pbp` in its cwd, veripb accepts them, stderr is empty, nothing appears beside the
  model; (b) a second run overwrites them with the same bytes; (c) a model without `.fzn`;
  (d) `mznfileQ1w2E3.fzn` gives `baguette-proof`, veripb accepts it and stderr names both full
  paths; (e) a refused model exits 2 and leaves no file.
- `mznlib/test/check_mznlib.sh`: the second, output-only run of a flattened model names
  `--proof "$tmp/<n>_again"`.
- `scripts/diff_lane.sh`: a configuration with `proof=no` must carry `--no-proof` in its flags,
  and a proof column other than yes/no is refused. The one such line, `noproof`, already did, so
  no reference moved.
- `scripts/corpus_run.sh` `NO_PROOF=1`: its documented meaning was "the solver still writes its
  proof to a temporary file, so this removes the checker and the artefact, not the logging"
  (config b of D-0080). Kept: it now passes `--proof "$L"` and deletes the pair unchecked. The
  one difference is that the `.opb` is now written too. `SOLVER_ARGS=--no-proof` beside it
  replaces the prefix (the two flags together are exit 2).
- `bench/learning_baseline.sh`: the two `--stats` runs name `--proof "$WORK/s"`.
- Already explicit, unchanged: `scripts/compare_run.sh` (`--proof "$L"`), `run_model_tests.sh`,
  `verify_proof.sh`, `check_determinism.sh`, `check_unlimited.sh`, `scaling_lane.sh`,
  `shrink.sh`, `bench/run_bench.sh`, `bench/fuzz/run.py`, the `bench/perf` scripts. The
  historical one-off scripts under `bench/m6t9`, `bench/bits_spike` and `bench/regular_spike`
  all pass `--proof` or `--no-proof`, or go through `corpus_run.sh`.

`*.opb` and `*.pbp` are in `.gitignore`, so a plain `git status` cannot show a stray proof. The
gate's stray check therefore uses `git status --short --ignored` and a `find` outside `_build`.

### 5. The gate

First gate, fresh clone of `6b8ba3d` in `/scratch/arthur/wave54-keepproof-gate` (binary
`b4a16e86`, against gate 64's `d7a1ef00`): `make check` rc 0 (4 278 ok, 198 models passed, 25 s,
peak RSS 99 MB); stdout, exit code, `.opb` and `.pbp` of the 198 models run WITH `--proof` equal
to main's binary (0 differences, so proof mode is byte-identical); the differential lane 301 of
301 equal to the reference, its debug pass 289 of 289; the scaling lane ok on every line;
`bench/diff` unchanged, nothing re-recorded. The stray check then found `./wide.opb`/`.pbp` and
`./justover.opb`/`.pbp` (2.1 MB and 0.7 MB) in the clone's root: `scripts/check_unlimited.sh`
had eight runs without `--proof` that the first grep missed, because their solver call and its
flags sit on separate lines. They now name `--proof "$TMP/scratch"` (`26f9b89`, a script-only
change). A line scanner over every tracked script, joining continuation lines, then found no
other run of the solver without `--proof` or `--no-proof`.

Second gate, fresh clone of `26f9b89` in `/scratch/arthur/wave54-keepproof-gate2`: `make check`
rc 0 (4 278 ok, 198 models, 26 s, peak RSS 100 MB), the same binary `b4a16e86` (so the lanes
above stand), and no `.opb` or `.pbp` anywhere in the clone outside `_build/`, `test/out/` (the
model lane's own output directory) and the two tracked fixtures under `bench/control/`, by
`find` and by `git status --short --ignored`.

### 6. What the user must still confirm

- **The directory.** The current directory is the proposal on record. The alternatives are the
  model's own directory (which would write into `test/models/` when a model there is run
  without `--proof`), or a fixed proofs directory. Either is a one-line change to
  `default_proof_prefix`, plus SPEC §4.1's bullet and the lane `test_m9t5_default_keeps_proof`.
- **The MiniZinc name.** `./baguette-proof`, fixed, overwritten by the next run, with a line on
  stderr. A per-run unique name would never collide but would pile up files in the cwd.
- **Overwriting.** Chosen silent, like `--proof PREFIX` and a compiler. Refusing to overwrite
  would make the second run of a model fail until the user deletes the first proof.

## D-0164  M11-complexity-T11: what black-hole keeps per node, and Element's foreign-hole clauses built lazily

Status: DONE (the fix); section 7 stays open
Date: 2026-11-19

By agent-heap (branch `wave54-heap` for the probe, `wave54-heap-fix` for the fix, both on
the hub). Base: `wave53-alldiff` tip `b7e1ca9` (M7-T33, not yet merged), binary `45b8a3c7`.
Runs in `/scratch/arthur/wave54-heap-runs/`, copied to `/cluster/arthur/baguette-results/wave54-heap/`.

### 1. The question

D-0155 section 4 and D-0156 section 4 left one finding open. `2011_black-hole_9` without
`--proof` held 6.3 GB RSS after 39 nodes, and with M7-T33 black-hole x4, black-hole_layout x3 and
ghoulomb x1 stop at the 8 GB heap budget (rc 5) within about 90 s. Which structure holds the
memory, and is it (a) data that should be released on backtrack and is not, (b) data that is
legitimately live along the branch but too big per entry, or (c) something cumulative across the
run?

### 2. Method

A probe on `wave54-heap` (`lib/core/search.ml`, the seven commits marked PROBE, not for merging):

- `BAGUETTE_HEAP_PROBE=K`: every K nodes a full major GC, the live heap (`Gc.stat`), the words
  reachable from the search's roots `(store, engine, ctx, trace, stats)`, and the MARGINAL share of
  the trail, the explanation arena, the propagator instances and, per propagator family, of that
  family's trail entries together with their arena slots (each hidden in turn and
  `Obj.reachable_words` taken again). `unreached` = live minus reachable, which is where a
  module-level table would show.
- `BAGUETTE_HEAP_QUICK=1`: `Gc.quick_stat` at every node, no forced GC.
- At `BAGUETTE_NODE_LIMIT` with the probe on: DESTRUCTIVE drops in a fixed order (writer audit
  table, writer tags, `Justify` memo, `Justify` stated, trace, the arena slots family by family,
  the arena, the trail), live heap after each.

memtrace is not usable: OCaml 5.1.1 has no `Gc.Memprof`.

### 3. What is retained

**Without `--proof`, base binary, `2011_black-hole_9`** (probe every 5 nodes):

| node | trail | live | arena share | element entries + slots |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 5 | 7 047 | 121 MB | 26 MB | 6 322 / 32 MB |
| 10 | 12 179 | 244 MB | 135 MB | 10 919 / 154 MB |
| 15 | 18 767 | 725 MB | 579 MB | 16 694 / 633 MB |
| 30 | 24 924 | 1 194 MB | 965 MB | |
| 40 | 24 928 | 1 193 MB | 965 MB | 22 007 / 1 082 MB |

`unreached` is 0 at every probe and the instances' share is 0, so nothing is held outside the
search's roots and nothing is (c). Between nodes 15 and 20, and on `2013_black-hole_4` between
nodes 20 and 25 where the trail shrinks back to 17 746 entries, the live heap follows the trail
and not the node count: what a backtrack pops is released. So it is not (a) either. It is (b):
live along the branch, and far too big per entry, about 49 KB per `array_int_element` entry at
node 40 and growing with depth (4.7 KB per entry at node 5), so the heap is superlinear in the
trail.

The structure: `Element.index_hole_clause` (`lib/core/prop/element.ml`, M7-T21 / D-0084), called
by `pos_gone` for each dead position whose index value is an interior hole punched under a decision
by another propagator. It built `Explanation.clause (unit :: List.map Lit.negate (Reason.lits
e.reason))` EAGERLY: the puncher's whole reason materialised as fresh literals. `dead_positions`
calls `pos_gone` for every dead declared position at every pruning (`alo`, `push_lo_expl`,
`push_hi_expl`, `hole_expl`, `no_position_conflict`), so one pruning copied O(dead positions x
puncher facts) literals, and the puncher's facts themselves grow along the branch (an element
reason carries its index holes' punchers' facts, `index_hole_facts`). On black-hole the 102
element constraints share ONE index, `X_INTRODUCED_107_` over 1..416 (the widest variable of the
model), each with its own constant array and a result over 1..52. Every hole one instance punches in
that index is a foreign hole for the 101 others, and a pruning walks up to 416 dead positions.

**With `--proof`** the eager copies were only part of it. The quick probe (`p5/`) shows the heap
flat until the first failure deep in the tree, then a jump at that one node: base 1 661 -> 4 182 MB,
fix 763 -> 3 242 MB at node 30 of `2011_black-hole_9`, then +100 to +350 MB per later failure. At
the first failure `Trace.emit` writes a line and its derivation for every entry of the branch
(about 25 000), and each written derivation stays reachable until its level is wiped. The drops at
node 40 (`p7/`, fix, live 2 660 MB):

| dropped (in this order) | live after | share |
|---|---|---|
| writer audit table (`Writer.live`, origin closures) | 2 335 MB | 325 MB |
| writer `tags` + `by_lvl` | 2 145 MB | 190 MB |
| `Justify` memo | 1 804 MB | 341 MB |
| `Justify` stated (claim index) | 1 471 MB | 333 MB |
| trace | 1 454 MB | 17 MB |
| explanation arena (forced derivations) | 233 MB | 1 221 MB |
| trail (reasons, `cites` memos) | 93 MB | 140 MB |

All of it is (b) as well: proof state of the open levels, wiped by `Justify.wipe_level`. Dropping
the arena slots family by family after the four tables above (`p12/`): element's slots free 60 MB,
then `all_different_int`'s free 1 161 MB, inverse, int_lin_le and decisions nothing. So the
largest single holder in proof mode is the FORCED derivations of `all_different` prunings, about
530 entries on the branch and 2.2 MB each, held by `Explanation.force`'s memoisation once their
lines are written (element's derivations cite them, which is why dropping element's slots first
frees little). Without `--proof` the same 530 entries hold 15 MB: what is big is the rendered
derivation, not the snapshot it is built from.

Without `--proof` one more (b) item shows in `--stats` on `2013_black-hole_4` (300 s, fix): the
decision-closure citation memos (`Store.entry.cites`, M7-T27 a3), 13 163 memos and 231.6 MB.

### 4. The fix (one commit on `wave54-heap-fix`, element.ml only)

1. `9e6a230`: the puncher is still found eagerly (I-X6: which entry punched the hole is live store
   state), its literals are not. The clause is built inside `Explanation.deferred` from the
   puncher's `Reason.t`, which is frozen data (a `Facts` list, or a `Later` reading a history that
   is valid while the puncher is on the trail, and the puncher is below the pruning, so it outlives
   every arena slot that can hold the thunk). Same literals in the same order.

It changes neither the type `Explanation.t`, a proof rule nor the search.

Tried and reverted (`e0a57bb`, reverted by `3b32af4` on `wave54-heap`): one clause per hole,
cached per index value with the puncher entry it was built for, so that every pruning citing the
hole shares one node. Same proof bytes, but no gain on bh9 with `--proof` (live 2 660 -> 2 657 MB
at node 40, RSS 5 644 -> 5 620 MB) and 7 958 -> 7 518 MB on bh4, because section 3's proof-mode
holder is alldiff's derivations rather than these clauses. Its cache also keeps popped puncher
entries alive (75 MB on bh9 without `--proof`). Not worth a cache.

### 5. Measurements (fataepyc-06)

Binaries: base `45b8a3c7` (`b7e1ca9`), fix `c4cd4783` (`9e6a230`). The probe binaries (the same
code plus the inactive probe, whose own node limit exits at once): base `3e8c79ae`, fix `af833694`.

Equal nodes (node limit 40, same trail length at every probe, so the same search), probe binaries,
`perf stat -e instructions:u` (`p3/`):

| run | RSS base -> fix | instructions base -> fix |
|---|---|---|
| bh9 `--no-proof` | 2 127 -> 839 MB | 132.4 G -> 111.9 G (-15.5 %) |
| bh4 `--no-proof` | 6 044 -> 1 719 MB | 645.1 G -> 471.4 G (-26.9 %) |
| bh9 `--proof` | 5 424 -> 4 344 MB | 686.9 G -> 670.8 G (-2.3 %) |
| bh4 `--proof` | 11 655 -> 7 977 MB | 2 109.6 G -> 1 938.0 G (-8.1 %) |

The `.pbp` of each proof pair has the same sha256 (bh9 `468e80ec...`, 551 MB; bh4 `fb65a630...`,
1.13 GB).

The same with the clean binaries and the CLI's own node limit (`BAGUETTE_NODE_LIMIT=40`, M6-T9,
which writes the proof to its end; `p10/`):

| run | RSS base -> fix | instructions base -> fix | `.pbp` (same sha256) |
|---|---|---|---|
| bh9 `--proof` | 6 726 -> 5 644 MB | 800.4 G -> 776.8 G (-3.0 %) | 617 MB `e29e8967...` |
| bh4 `--proof` | 11 656 -> 7 958 MB | 2 134.6 G -> 1 960.8 G (-8.1 %) | 2.50 GB `f08cdbd5...` |

The Challenge setting, `2013_black-hole_4`, 300 s, `--max-heap-mb 8192` (`p9/`, clean binaries):

| | base | fix |
|---|---|---|
| `--proof` | rc 5 at 92 s (heap budget), 8.42 GB | rc 0, time limit, 42 nodes, 8.02 GB |
| `--no-proof` | 125 nodes, 6.60 GB | 154 nodes, 2.04 GB |

The 15 black-hole and black-hole_layout instances at 30 nodes with `--proof` (`p4/`), peak RSS
base -> fix: bh4 11 292 -> 7 098 MB, bh12 8 243 -> 6 382, bh14 12 136 -> 10 847, bh16 3 467 ->
2 255, bh18 4 879 -> 3 031, bh20 3 218 -> 2 350, bh9 5 145 -> 4 152, layout_3 4 706 -> 4 103,
layout_14 10 787 -> 10 106, layout_17 6 525 -> 5 168, layout_25 12 352 -> 11 140, layout_27 3 861
-> 2 599. bh6, bh10 and bh17 finish under 400 MB either way.

### 6. Bytes and the gate

- Every `test/models/*.fzn` (200) solved with `--proof`, plus the 15 black-hole instances at
  `BAGUETTE_NODE_LIMIT=30`: stdout, exit code, `.opb` and `.pbp` sha256 of fix against base,
  215 of 215 identical (`p4/results`).
- fix on a fresh clone (`gate/`): `make check` under `ulimit -v 4000000` rc 0, 200/200 models,
  0 FAIL. `make diff ARGS="--tier all -j 16"`: FAIL, 18 of 301 runs differ from the reference,
  `2020_lot-sizing_pigment15b.psp` in 12 configurations and `2011_cyclic-rcpsp_easy_6@2000` in 6,
  exactly the runs wave53-alldiff's handoff says must be re-recorded at its merge. The same lane
  on the BASE binary fails on the same 18 runs, and the kept observations of base and fix are equal on 300 of 301 runs. The one
  that differs is lot-sizing's `activity` configuration, which dies at the lane's 4 GB cap in
  both (the cap wave53-alldiff's `--update` already hit): base with rc 134 "allocation failure
  during minor GC" before printing its encoding counters, fix with rc 2 "Out of memory" after
  them. Rerun twice each with the same cap (`p8/`), base and fix both die with rc 134, so where
  the 4 GB cap is hit is not deterministic. With the cap at 24 GB both complete (rc 0, 4.27 GB peak RSS) and their observations, proof hashes included, are equal.

### 7. What is left, not done here

- With `--proof`, black-hole still grows 100 to 350 MB per deep failure and reaches 2.66 GB live
  (5.6 GB RSS) at node 40 of bh9. The holders are section 3's table: alldiff's forced derivations
  (1.16 GB), the `Justify` memo (341 MB) and claim index (333 MB), the writer's audit table (325 MB,
  on by default in the CLI) and its tags (190 MB). They are proof state of the open levels. Shrinking
  the largest means not keeping a forced derivation once its line is written: its id is what a
  later citation needs, and the `Justify` memo already holds that under the `Deferred` node's
  identity. But `Explanation.force` memoises the tree by design, `Justify`'s hashing reads the
  forced head, and a re-forced tree has new inner nodes, so whether the bytes stay the same needs
  its own argument and measurement. That touches `explanation.ml` and `justify.ml` and is a
  decision of its own, not attempted here. The other way in is the size of alldiff's derivations
  themselves, 2.2 MB of heap each.
- The per-pruning `dead_positions` list is still built eagerly, one deferred thunk per dead
  position per pruning (about 8 KB per element entry at node 40 without `--proof`), and an element
  reason still copies its index holes' punchers' facts (`index_hole_facts`).
- `Store.entry.cites` (231.6 MB on bh4 without `--proof`).

### 8. To land

The fix touches only `lib/core/prop/element.ml`, which nobody claims in the current table. The
branch is built on `wave53-alldiff` (M7-T33), so it lands after that merge, as the one commit
`9e6a230` cherry-picked onto main and gated there (the alldiff merge re-records the lane's
lot-sizing and cyclic references first). The probe commits on `wave54-heap` are not to be merged.

### 9. Landed on main ahead of M7-T33 (orchestrator)

The fix touches `element.ml` only, which main holds since D-0155, so it was cherry-picked onto main
(`bb59854`) as its own branch `wave54-heapfix` instead of waiting for wave53-alldiff's merge. The
numbers of section 5 were measured over wave53-alldiff's tip; on main the gate checks that every
artefact stays byte-identical (gate 69, WORKLOG).


## D-0166  M11-complexity-T12: what a proved run keeps once a line is written; four holders shrunk byte for byte, the largest is the user's call

Status: DONE for sections 2 and 3 (every byte the same). OPEN for the user: section 5.
Date: 2026-11-19
Task: M11-complexity-T12 (agent-live, `wave54-live`). Follows D-0164 section 7.
Touches: `lib/core/justify.ml` (the claim index's packed keys, the memo's chained table, shared
`Combine` origins), `lib/proof/writer.ml` (the audit keeps the origin alone, `by_lvl` as runs),
`test/unit/test_justify.ml` (`test_representations_m11t12`). `lib/core/explanation.ml` is
unchanged.

### 1. The question

D-0164 section 3 found 2.66 GB live on `2011_black-hole_9` with `--proof` at node 40, held by
alldiff's forced derivations (1.16 GB), the `Justify` memo (341 MB) and claim index (333 MB), the
writer's audit table (325 MB) and its tags (190 MB). For each holder, which part must outlive the
line it wrote and which part is kept only because nothing dropped it?

Measured on a throwaway base, main `f5c7973` with `origin/wave53-alldiff` merged (main stops at 13
nodes on black-hole) and agent-heap's PROBE commits, plus counts per table at the node limit:
3 131 911 memo entries (3 130 755 of them inner `Combine`s, 462 `Deferred`, 694 `Clause`),
25 888 claim keys holding 4 868 262 literals (16 387 keys over 20 literals: the trace lines),
3 371 554 live ids in the audit table and in `tags` alike. With `BAGUETTE_MEMO_STATS=1` the memo
takes 3 391 406 lookups to node 40 and answers **none** of them.

### 2. What each holder must keep, and what it kept for nothing

| holder | read again after the line is written | kept only because nothing dropped it | done |
|---|---|---|---|
| claim index (`stated`) | the clause as a SET, for `defining_line`'s equality test and `wipe_level` | a fresh `Lit.t` record and `Ge` block per literal of every key, 68 bytes a literal | key packed to two ints a literal over interned names: 333 -> 76 MB |
| memo | the key's identity (`==`), its hash, the id and the level, for the hit test and the wipe | a tuple, a record and a list cons per entry, and the hash again as a cons per level, about 93 bytes | one 48-byte cell per entry in a chained table, the per-level hashes in int buffers: 342 -> 244 MB |
| audit table (`live`) | the id's presence (I-X2, `is_live`, the end sweep `live_ids`), its origin for a failure report | the level (it is the id's tag, in `tags`), and one origin closure per `Combine` line | the origin alone, one closure per `Combine` shape: 325 -> 132 MB |
| `tags`, `by_lvl` | each live id's level, for `wipe_level`'s doomed set | one cons per id in a level's bucket, whose ids are almost always consecutive | the bucket as runs of consecutive ids: 189 -> 118 MB |
| alldiff's forced derivations | the head's identity and shallow hash (memo hit), the whole tree for `Explanation.lits` (the D-0026 agreement check under `BAGUETTE_DEBUG`), `Pb_analysis.cited_ids`, and a re-emission after the memo entry's level is wiped while the explanation lives on | nothing, within the type: see section 5 | not done, 1.16 GB stays |

The memo's entries are kept as they were, each one. Every lookup keys on a physical value, so an
entry cannot be dropped while its key is reachable without risking a second line, and the memo
cannot know which keys a later derivation will reach.

### 3. Why the bytes cannot move

- Claim index: the packing is injective (one interned id per name string, so two names share an
  id exactly when `String.equal` holds, which is what `Lit.equal` compares; kind, sign and value
  are their own fields), so two packed keys are equal exactly when the sorted literal lists were
  equal. Nothing iterates the table. The interned names are never wiped, so an id stays stable
  for as long as any key can use it.
- Memo: a lookup compares the full hash, then `==`, and a slot's chain is newest first as a bucket
  was, so it answers what the bucket of that hash answered; growing the table keeps each hash's
  cells in their order. A wipe removes from a slot exactly its cells at the wiped level or above.
- Audit: `live` and `tags` gain and lose ids at the same four sites (`fresh_lazy`, `wipe_level`,
  `delete_many`, `delete_core`); nothing re-tags an id, so the report's level read from `tags` is
  the level the entry held. An origin is rendered only by the report, the mutation knob and
  `--stats`' widest `pol`, and a shared `Combine` closure renders the same string (the key packs
  both integers and is used only where both fit in 31 bits).
- `by_lvl`: a run is extended only when the new id is the next one at the same level, and a bucket
  read from each run's `hi` down to its `lo` lists the same ids in the same order as the list did,
  so `wipe_level` computes the same doomed list and writes the same deletions.

`test_representations_m11t12` drives 5 000 derivations over four interleaved levels past the
table's growth, a run broken by an interlude at another level, and clauses that differ by kind,
sign, name or order, through hits, wipes and re-derivation.

### 4. Measurements (fataepyc-06, `2011_black-hole_9`, `--proof`, node 40)

Binaries on the throwaway base: before `d1e5e20a`, after `b28d132a` (the same PROBE code, which
is inert without `BAGUETTE_HEAP_PROBE` except for the node limit). Runs in
`/scratch/arthur/wave54-live-runs/`.

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| live heap at node 40 | 2 660 MB | 2 041 MB |
| peak RSS (probe off) | 4 346 MB | 3 648 MB |
| instructions (`perf stat`, probe off) | 670.7 G | 656.3 G (-2.2 %) |
| wall (probe off, shared node) | 118.9 s | 121.8 s |
| `.pbp` md5 | `1d8104fe` | `1d8104fe` |

The drops after the change (same order as D-0164's): audit origins 13 MB (was 129), audit table
119 MB, `tags` + `by_lvl` 118 MB, memo 244 MB, claim index 76 MB, trace 16 MB, element's arena
slots 61 MB, all_different's 1 160 MB.

### 5. For the user: alldiff's forced derivations (1.16 GB) and the memo that never hits

Every forced derivation is held by its arena slot through `thunk.forced` (and `thunk.compute`,
which `force` sets to a closure returning it) for as long as its trail entry stands. After the line
is written the solver reads it again only in the four ways of section 2's last row. None of the
options below is taken.

| option | what changes | bytes | memory on bh9 node 40 | cost |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| A. keep (now) | nothing | same | 1.16 GB stays | none |
| B. a thunk records its emitted id and level, drops its forced tree, keeps its original closure and re-forces on a later read | `Explanation.t`'s `thunk` record (a field) | same if every thunk is deterministic (I-X6 says it closes over a snapshot) and a re-forced tree shares no non-thunk node with another live one; argued, then measured | most of 1.16 GB (the closures hold about 15 MB, D-0164) | a re-force per later read: debug agreement walks, `cited_ids`, a re-emission after a wipe |
| C. replace the forced tree by `Model_row id` once written | no type change | a citation after the line's level is wiped names a deleted id; `Explanation.lits` loses the cited literals, so the D-0026 agreement check under `BAGUETTE_DEBUG` fires on the parents | most of 1.16 GB | not sound as it stands; rejected |
| D. make alldiff's derivations smaller (share the axiom chains, fewer inner `Combine`s per line) | `lib/core/prop/alldiff.ml` only | same if every line is the same | unknown, the tree is 2.2 MB of heap per derivation | its own task |
| E. memoise only roots and `Deferred`s, not a `Combine` reached as another `Combine`'s `Term` | `justify.ml` only | same if no non-thunk node is shared by two derivations or twice in one; that is explanation.ml's stated discipline ("a thunk is the ONLY shared node"), not a property of the type, and a violation would write a duplicate line, still valid | most of the memo's 244 MB here (3.13 M inner entries, 0 hits) | the discipline becomes load-bearing for the bytes; a `BAGUETTE_DEBUG` check could keep the full memo and assert no inner hit |

Recommendation: B, which takes the largest holder without touching any proof line, if the user
accepts a field on `thunk`; E is cheap, but it makes a comment-level discipline load-bearing for
the bytes, and that should be the user's call too.

### 6. Gate

Fresh clone of `wave54-live` at `c46952f` from the hub (`/scratch/arthur/wave54-live-gate`, binary
`214e74d1`) against gate 69's `22620b60`: `make check` rc 0 (4 289 ok, gate 69's 4 279 plus the 10

## D-0156  M7-T33: all_different's two pigeonholes carry their facts under a decision, derived ahead of the conflict line, so 1UIP learning resolves from them; and `Alldiff.excl` cites its ladder rungs without a name lookup per rung

Status: DECIDED (built, measured, gated on fataepyc-06; the diff-lane references of the runs listed in section 7 are the orchestrator's to re-record after the gated merge)
Date: 2026-11-19
Task: M7-T33, and D-0145 section 5's `Alldiff.excl` leftover (agent-alldiff, `wave53-alldiff`).
Touches: `lib/core/prop/alldiff.ml` (`push_conflict`, `distinct_facts`, `pass`'s `push`,
`regin_pass`'s failed matching, the term's `rungs`, `rung`, `excl`, `overshoot_cancel`, the
header), `lib/proof/encoding.ml` (`consistency_ids`, additive), `test/unit/test_prop.ml` (the
M7-T33 section), `test/models/alldiff_conflict_learn_sat.fzn` and
`test/models/alldiff_regin_conflict_learn_sat.fzn` with their expected outputs.

### 1. The finding

D-0151 section 2 found that `2015_p1f_13` under the native `inverse` learns 0 clauses, and
traced it to all_different. Both of its pigeonholes reached the store as a push that must fail:
stage 1 pushes the surplus variable of a Hall interval past its own upper bound, stage 2 pushes
the first unmatched variable past its upper bound, and `Store.apply`'s `Failed` arm pairs the
derivation with `Reason.none`. That is sound, because search.ml's D-0040 arm writes the
derivation and the decision nogood closes the branch. But `Learn.at_conflict` gets an empty cut,
so no all_different conflict ever produced a 1UIP clause.

### 2. The change

Under a decision, both pigeonholes are now reported with their facts, under
`Store.deriving_ahead` (`push_conflict`). `Trace.conflict_line` then writes the derivation
first and `rup ~facts >= 1` after it, which is cumulative's arrangement (D-0096) and element's
(D-0101). Nothing outside `alldiff.ml` changed on the solver side.

The facts are chosen so that every literal the derivation leaves in its row is the negation of
one of them. The `rup` line is then unit propagation against one line.

| what the derivation leaves | where it comes from | fact on the tail |
|---|---|---|
| a Hall member's `~x_ge_lo` / `x_ge_(hi+1)` | `excl`, when `hall_cancels` cannot cancel a bound a decision moved | that bound (`hall_facts`) |
| a deep hole's clause `~x_eq_v \/ ~facts` | `Gone_hole`, for a hole the value set excludes | the REMOVER's facts (`hall_facts` names the excluded holes only) |
| the surplus variable's `~y_ge_lo(y)` | the telescoped forward channelling | `y >= lo(y)` |
| the surplus variable's residue `y_ge_(b+1)` | the telescope, when `overshoot_cancel` has no root upper bound to cancel it with | `y <= hi(y)`, with `hi(y) <= b`: unit propagation walks the rungs `hi(y)+1 .. b` |

The last row is the crossed opposing bound that `Store.apply`'s `Failed` arm says a conflict line
needs and a pruning's reason does not carry. So stage 1's facts are `remove_reason`'s (both bounds
of `y`, then the Hall set's) and not `prune_reason`'s. Stage 2's are `hall_facts` over the whole
violating set A, value set B. A fact is listed once (`distinct_facts`): three members holed by
the same remover would otherwise list its tail three times. A root-established fact whose literal
the derivation cancelled is still listed. That is harmless, since Analysis drops root nodes from
every cut, and it is element's choice too.

AT THE ROOT NOTHING CHANGES. With no decision there is no branch to learn from, every bound the
derivation reads is root-established and cancelled, and the derivation closes to `0 >= 1`, which
search.ml's root arm writes. Every root refutation is byte-identical (measured, section 6). A
test (`M7-T33 root`) holds the root conflict to `Reason.none`.

Why the push test agrees with the store. Stage 1's pigeonhole arm reads `y` from the pass's
snapshot, whose `s_hi <= b` the live bound can only undercut (I-P6), so `bound > y.s_hi` holds
live too. The `n = k` arm reads `y` live. Stage 2 never reaches its emptying push under a
decision any more. The removals of a Regin pass never empty a domain (a removal never takes
`M(y)` from `y`), so `remove_one`'s conflict arm stays as it was.

No new `Explanation` constructor, no change to `justify.ml`, `explanation.ml`, `store.ml` or
`search.ml`.

### 3. Lanes

`test/unit/test_prop.ml`, the M7-T33 section, on two SAT scenes (D-0053). In each, a decision on
`k` confines or holes `x1..x3` through three single-variable propagators (`int_le` / `int_ne`) that
all watch `k`. The engine's FIFO runs all three before the all_different they wake, so the
conflict is all_different's by construction.

- (a) driven by hand: the stage-1 conflict (k <= 2 confines three variables to 1..2) and the
  Regin conflict (k = 2 holes 2 in three variables of 1..3) are all_different's, `c_ahead`, carry
  facts (`~x3_ge_3`, the crossed bound, and `~k_ge_3`, the holes' remover), list no fact twice,
  satisfy `Store.agreement_holds` (D-0026), and `Learn.at_conflict` returns `Some`. The root
  pigeonhole is still factless.
- (b) under search, the model's own order, audit on. Both learn 2 clauses (0 before), both proofs
  verify. The pinned conflict lines are `rup +1 x3_ge_3 +1 x1_ge_3 +1 x2_ge_3 >= 1 ;` and
  `rup +1 k_ge_3 >= 1 ;`, each written right after its `pol`. Four refusal lanes, each asserted
  on the full RUP sentence AND on the line number in "Checking error at":
  - standalone: the line alone against the `.opb` is refused (I-X10, cumulative's lane);
  - no-pol: the honest proof without the `pol` ahead of the line is refused at that line, so
    the derivation carries it in sequence too (unlike element's, D-0101 section 2);
  - no-crossed (stage 1): the line without `y`'s upper bound is refused;
  - no-fact (stage 1): the line without its last fact, a Hall member's bound, is refused.
  The Regin line has one fact, so no fact can be dropped without corrupting the claim itself
  (test_mutation.ml's trap 3).

On the code before this change, every (b) lane fails at "the conflict line is on the page".

### 5. `Alldiff.excl` without a name lookup per rung (D-0145 section 5)

`excl` cites the ladder rungs between an excluded value and the current bound, O(width) rungs
per excluded value, and each went through `Encoding.consistency_id`, which finds the variable by
NAME (`Encoding.find`, a string hash). D-0145 measured that at 12.4 % of
`2011_cyclic-rcpsp_easy_6`'s proof mode. `Encoding.consistency_ids t x` (additive, no signature
changed) looks `x` up once and returns the function `consistency_id t x` is, from the record
`find` returned. That record never changes once `x` is declared: a redeclaration with other
bounds is refused, and `lo`, `hi`, `ladder_base` and `repr` are immutable. Each all_different
term keeps it in a lazy field, forced the first time a derivation cites one of its rungs, and
`excl` and `overshoot_cancel` cite through it. Same ids, same order, so every byte is the same.

Proof mode at 10 000 nodes, `perf stat -e instructions:u`, CLI default (audit on), one run each
on fataepyc-06 (binaries `64ec63e0` main at `9a9c461`, `4d06f9d4` at `b543817`):

| instance | main | `b543817` | change | wall main / branch | `.pbp` |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `2011_cyclic-rcpsp_easy_6` | 646.22 G | 581.31 G | -10.0 % | 90.5 / 82.9 s | identical, 2.02 GB |
| `2013_rcpsp_11` | 194.28 G | 194.31 G | 0.0 % | 35.7 / 34.4 s | identical, 421 MB |

A flat `perf record` of the branch on cyclic (2 000 nodes) no longer shows `Encoding.find` or
`caml_hash` in its top 40 symbols. `Alldiff.rung` itself is 1.4 %. What is left of the
derivation's cost is allocation (the `range` lists, one `Model_row` term per rung), which is the
derivation's size and not a lookup. Gate on `b543817` alone: `make check` rc 0 (4 243 unit
checks, 0 FAIL, 198 models), every model's `.out`/`.opb`/`.pbp` equal to main's, lane 301/301,
debug lane 289/289.

### 5b. `Alldiff.hole_cite` without a whole-trail walk per hole (D-0155 section 4)

Added at the orchestrator's request once agent-element's D-0155 had removed element's own walk.
`hole_cite` asks, for every hole in a snapshotted domain, which trail entry removed it, and at
which level. `remover_index` answered by walking the WHOLE trail backwards, because when it was
written an entry did not carry its position. Since M6-T15 it does (`pos`), so `hole_cite` now
asks `Store.remover ~before:(Store.trail_length store)` (D-0088, a binary search over the
variable's entry history) and reads the level off `e.pos`. It is the same entry: the walk's
predicate is `Store.remover_scan`'s, started at the same position, and `Store.remover` is
checked against that scan by physical equality under `BAGUETTE_DEBUG`. Element made the same
move in D-0155. Its own commit (`cc9d94d`).

Measured on top of main `c058ada` (D-0155 merged), `perf stat -e instructions:u`, proof on, one
run each, binaries `643f44e9` (main, element's gate binary) and `b1d01d50` (main plus `cc9d94d`
alone):

| `2011_black-hole_10` | to the end (UNSAT at the root) | 52.23 G, 7.2 s | 15.92 G, 2.5 s | stdout, `.opb`, `.pbp` (49 MB), stats equal |
| `2011_black-hole_20` | 20 nodes | 1 846.0 G, 262 s | 174.5 G, 29.4 s | equal (`.pbp` 278 MB) |

Peak RSS is unchanged (363 MB and 2.99 GB). With part 1 as well, the Challenge run in section 4
shows what the family does at 300 s.

### 8. What would reverse this

- A refused alldiff conflict line on a satisfiable model. That would mean a literal the
  derivation leaves in its row has no fact, which is the D-0075 shape again.
- A family where learning from alldiff conflicts costs more than it prunes (long Regin tails
  from many removers). The tails are bounded by the violating set's facts, and the measurement
  in section 4 is where to look first.

## D-0165  D-0161 request 1: `Alldiff.snap_of` keeps only what needs the store; the values lost below and above the window are rebuilt inside the `Deferred`

Status: DONE (gate green, section 4)
Date: 2026-11-19

By agent-snap (branch `wave54-snap`, on top of `wave53-alldiff`'s tip `b7e1ca9`, which it merges
after). Touches `lib/core/prop/alldiff.ml` only. Runs in `/scratch/arthur/wave54-snap-runs/`,
copied to `/cluster/arthur/baguette-results/wave54-snap/`.

### 1. What changed

D-0161 section 6 request 1. `snap_of` built, for every variable of the constraint at every
snapshot, `s_gone`: every declared value the variable has lost, tagged `Gone_below`, a hole cite,
or `Gone_above`. That is two `range` lists of up to the declared width per variable per pass.
Only the derivations read the below and above runs (`alo_over`, `hall_cancels`), and they all run
inside a `Deferred` (`prune_expl`, `remove_expl`, `conflict_expl`). The reason reads only the holes
(`hall_facts`). So under `--no-proof` none of it was ever read, and with a proof most of it was not.

- The snapshot now holds `s_holes`, the interior holes with their cites, and nothing else of that
  list. A hole's cite reads the trail (`Store.remover`, the level of the remover), so it stays
  EAGER. Its cost on black-hole is D-0155's request, not this one.
- `gone s` rebuilds the full list when a derivation is forced: `range s_dlo (s_lo - 1)` tagged
  `Gone_below`, then `s_holes`, then `range (s_hi + 1) s_dhi` tagged `Gone_above`. These are the
  values, the order and the tags `gone_of` produced, so `alo_over` emits the same summands in the
  same order. `hall_cancels` counts the excluded values of the two runs directly, which gives the
  same two numbers the filter over `s_gone` gave.
- The root flags `s_lo_root`/`s_hi_root` stay EAGER, because they read the bound supports as they
  stand at the snapshot. They now call `Store.at_root` (one comparison against the first level
  mark) instead of `Store.level_of_index ... = 0` (a binary search over the open levels). Same
  answer by I-T2. `hole_cite` makes the same substitution. A `Store.history` (D-0124) was not
  needed for this, and it would have tied the derivation's forcing to the history being live.

### 2. Why it is sound (the rule, also in `alldiff.ml`'s header)

I-X6 forbids a thunk to READ the store. It does not forbid a thunk to COMPUTE from numbers the
snapshot froze. The below and above runs are functions of `s_dlo`, `s_lo`, `s_hi`, `s_dhi` and two
constant tags, so building them at forcing time gives exactly the list the snapshot would have
built. What does need the store (the supports' levels, the holes' removers) is still read at
snapshot time. No proof line can move, and every proof is byte-identical (section 4).

- `make diff ARGS="--tier all -j 16"`: 18 of 301 runs differ from the reference, the SAME 18 lines
  as the base's own lane (`/scratch/arthur/wave53-alldiff-runs/final/gate/diff.log`, same binary
  md5): cyclic x6 and lot-sizing x12, wave53-alldiff's pending re-record. Nothing else.
- `--debug`: 6 of 289 differ, the same 6 lines as the base's debug lane (cyclic x6).
- `make scaling ARGS="-j 16"`: ok, every line within its threshold. `bench/diff` untouched.

### 5. What this leaves

- `holes_of` still lists `range lo hi` for a holed domain and cites every hole at every snapshot.
  Only `hall_facts` reads the holes outside a derivation, and only the holes a Regin value set
  EXCLUDES. Making the cites lazy needs the remover's level as it stood, so it would go through a
  `Store.history` (D-0124) and its liveness check. That is D-0155's request, and it is the one that
  matters on black-hole.
- `snap_of` still runs for every variable at every pass, and the record is allocated whether a
  pruning follows or not. It is now cheap per variable (two O(1) root tests and a `has_holes`
  test), so I left it.
## D-0168  M11-complexity-T13: a thunk is released once its line is written; the memo lets go of what the closure built

Status: DONE (every byte the same; gate in section 6).
Date: 2026-11-20
Task: M11-complexity-T13 (agent-thunk, `wave55-thunk`). D-0166 section 5 option B, decided by D-0167
item 6 on the user's delegation.
Touches: `lib/core/explanation.ml` (the `thunk` record, `force`, the smart constructors, the
header), `lib/core/justify.ml` (the thunk's line, the memo's window and its release, the debug
checks), `lib/core/trace.ml` (`derive_ahead` emits the thunk, not its forced head: claimed on the
branch), `lib/core/pb_analysis.ml` (a comment in `cited_ids`), `test/unit/test_justify.ml`,
`docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` section 4.

### 1. What changed

`Explanation.thunk` gains two fields. `line` is `No_line` until `Justify.emit` has written the
thunk's derivation, then `Line { cid; level; epoch; owner }`: the id, the writer's level, the
`ctx`'s wipe count when it was written and the `ctx`'s serial. `captures` says whether the last
forcing may hold a node the closure did not build (section 3). `compute` is now the original
closure, never replaced. Once the line is written the thunk is RELEASED: `forced` is dropped, and
the memo cells its emission made are taken out (`Justify.release_window`), except the cells of
captured nodes. Before, the tree stayed reachable from `forced`, from the closure `force` put in
place of the original, and from the memo's keys (the forced head and every inner `Combine`).

Every reader, and what it does now:

| reader | before | now |
|---|---|---|
| a later `emit` of the thunk (a citing `Term`, `derive_ahead`, a conflict) | memo hit on the thunk or its forced head while the level lives | `Justify.live_line`: the recorded id while no wipe has reached its level (`wiped_at.(level) <= epoch`), and only for the `ctx` that wrote it; the thunk is no longer a memo key |
| `emit` after a wipe of that level | the same physical tree written again, every cell gone with the wipe | the closure forced again and that tree written again, then released again |
| `Pb_analysis.cited_ids`, `Explanation.lits` (the D-0026 agreement walk under `BAGUETTE_DEBUG`), the readers that match a forced head (`Search.weakened_row_only`, `close_root_conflict`, the conflict arm of `dfs`) | the cached tree | `force` runs the original closure again and does not keep the result |
| `Trace.derive_ahead` | forced the explanation and emitted the forced HEAD, so the line was the head's memo entry | emits the thunk itself (a released thunk is not forced again just to ask whether it is a decision) |

### 2. Why every byte is the same

A second `emit` is answered under exactly the condition the memo entry answered: an entry made at
level `l` died at the first `wipe_level k` with `k <= l`, and `wiped_at` is stamped for every
level from `k` up to the highest level a line was recorded at. A re-emission writes the closure's
tree again rather than the old physical one. The two are the same derivation because a thunk
closes over a snapshot (I-X6); the memo answers the two alike because each node of the tree is
either CAPTURED (a value the closure did not build: held physically by both forcings, its cell
kept, found as before) or BUILT (new at each forcing, reachable from its tree alone, so no lookup
can present it again, and its cell can go without changing any answer).

D-0166 section 5 stated B's condition as "a re-forced tree shares no non-thunk node with another
live one", and explanation.ml's header said a thunk is the ONLY shared node of a derivation. That
is false, measured: on `test/models/alldiff_regin_hole_element_unsat.fzn` a conflict's derivation
holds an eager `Combine` the trace had already written as another entry's line (the first
version of this change, which took out every cell of the window, raised on it under
`BAGUETTE_DEBUG`), and on the suite 39 cells are captured nodes first written inside another
thunk's emission (`element_foreign_hole_rup_sat/unsat`, `element_shared_result_root_unsat`).
Taking those cells out happened not to change a byte on the 198 models, but it would have on the
first later lookup. So the release keeps them, and needs to know which they are.

### 3. Telling captured from built, and what it costs

The first way was a second forcing at every release: a node both forcings hold physically was
captured. Measured on the lane's default runs it costs what the closure costs: `cyclic-rcpsp_easy_6`
+36.7 % instructions, `rcpsp_12` +15.5 %, `rcpsp_11` +7.4 %, `mspsp_hard_01` +2.9 %, and
`2011_black-hole_9` +5.3 % (all_different's closures are about 49 M instructions each). Rejected.

What is built instead is a FRAME per forcing (explanation.ml, "what a forcing builds"): the smart
constructors (`clause`, `linear`, `cut`, `combine`, `resolve`) note every node they build in a
ring of the last 256, and `citable`, through which every operand passes (`term`, `cut`,
`resolve`, `linear_term`), looks the operand up there by identity, newest first. An operand that
is a memoisable node and is not found, or a root that is not, sets `captures`. A forcing with no
capture is released with every cell of its window taken out and no second forcing; one with a
capture is forced a second time, and a node the two forcings share keeps its cell; if the two are
not `same_derivation`, the thunk is not released (it keeps its tree and its cells, as before T13).
The lookup is exact in the direction that matters: a node found was built in this forcing; a node
not found (captured, or built more than 256 nodes earlier) is treated as captured and only costs
a second forcing. The frame rests on every node being built through the smart constructors;
nothing in `lib/` builds a `Term (c, e)` or a node directly.

`BAGUETTE_DEBUG` forces every release a second time and requires the same derivation, requires a
forcing that recorded no capture to share no node with its second forcing, requires every node an
emission found already written by ANOTHER derivation (a hit on a cell outside its own window) to
be captured, keeps every cell taken out in a ghost table and raises if a lookup would have found
one, and compares every later forcing of a released thunk with the original, which a released
thunk keeps under `BAGUETTE_DEBUG`.

### 4. Measurements (fataepyc-06)

`2011_black-hole_9 --proof` at node 40, on a throwaway base: main `fa5628f` with
`origin/wave53-alldiff` merged and agent-heap's PROBE commits (`/scratch/arthur/wave55-thunk-runs/`,
`meas` clone). Binaries: before `3379d493`, after `55097e1a` (the same PROBE code).

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| live heap at node 40 | 2 041 MB | 658 MB |
| the memo's share (drop order of D-0166) | 244 MB | 9 MB |
| all_different's arena slots | 1 160 MB | 2 MB |
| peak RSS (probe off) | 3 646 MB | 1 777 MB |
| instructions (`perf stat`, probe off) | 656.3 G | 651.6 G (-0.7 %) |
| wall (probe off, shared node) | 120.2 s | 105.1 s |
| `.pbp` md5 | `1d8104fe` | `1d8104fe` |
| thunks released, cells taken out | | 819, 3 390 743 |
| second forcings at release, re-forcings after | | 0, 0 |

The lane's 27 default-configuration runs at their budgets, `--stats --proof`, main's binary
`214e74d1` against `da7b1545` (this change before formatting): stdout and `.pbp` equal on all 27;
instructions from -28.7 % (`rcpsp_11@10000`, 247.0 -> 176.1 G: the memo no longer keeps the
inner cells its lookups walk) through -7.4 % (`rcpsp_12`), -4.1 % (`cyclic-rcpsp_easy_6`, peak RSS
187 -> 71 MB), -2.9 % (`lot-sizing`) to +0.35 % (`openshop_gp10-4@300`, which releases nothing),
every one within +2 %. Re-forcings after release: 1 631 on `lot-sizing` (9 342 released), 24 on
`evm-super-compilation`, 0 elsewhere; their cost is inside those instruction counts.

The suite's 198 models, main's `214e74d1` against `da7b1545`, `--proof`, with and without
`BAGUETTE_DEBUG`: 198 x 4 artefacts equal both ways; 483 thunks released, 6 forced a second time
at release (captures), 18 written again after a wipe, 40 captured nodes kept, no debug check
raised.

### 5. What it costs in clarity

`Explanation` now carries mutable global state for the frames, its smart constructors are no
longer pure (they note what they build while a thunk is forced), and the memo has a second life
cycle beside the wipe (the window, its kept cells, its ghost). Each is stated where it lives. The
sentence "a thunk is the only shared node" is gone from the header, replaced by what was measured.

### 6. Gate

Fresh clone of `wave55-thunk` at `a8762eb` from the hub (`/scratch/arthur/wave55-thunk-gate`,
binary `40638833`) against gate 70's `214e74d1`: `make check` rc 0 (4 312 ok, gate 70's 4 289 plus
the 23 of `test_release_m11t13` and the reworded thunk counts; 198 models, peak RSS 100 MB),
198 models x 4 artefacts equal (`out`, `rc`, `opb`, `pbp`), lane 301/301 and debug 289/289 equal
to the reference, scaling ok, `bench/diff` untouched. Nothing to re-record. The tip after
`a8762eb` adds documentation only.

## D-0169  M11-complexity-T14: the cost per node against Gecode on the same tree (codes-cp QR48, XOR clauses); four byte-identical cuts, -12 to -16 % instructions per node without proof, and two measured proposals

**Status**: **DONE** for the cuts, recorded 2026-11-20 (agent-pernode2, `wave55-pernode`). Two
PROPOSALS (section 5) wait for the user. Files changed: `lib/core/engine.ml`, `lib/core/store.ml`,
`lib/core/prop/pb.ml`, `lib/core/prop/clause.ml`. Measured on `fataepyc-06`, outputs and scripts under
`/scratch/arthur/wave55-pernode-runs/` (`timeit.sh`, `quick.sh`, `prof.sh`, `tools/cats.py`), copied to
`/cluster/arthur/baguette-results/wave55-pernode/`. The node was shared with other agents throughout:
the load is given beside every timing, and the instruction counts (`perf stat -e instructions:u`, minus
a 1-node run of the same binary, so parsing and set-up are out) are the robust number.

### 1. The same tree

codes-cp `models/minweight_chk.mzn`, `ENC=1` (each parity check a chain of XOR, flattened by MiniZinc
2.10.1 into `bool_clause`), QR48, weight <= 8, `bool_search(x, input_order, indomain_max)`. "3 fixed" is
`dom/sym_p47_w8_basis.dzn`, "2 fixed" `dom/sym_p47_w8_f2_basis.dzn`. Gecode 6.4.0 gets its own
flattening (`bool_xor` native: 249 xor, 138 clauses, 2 linear, 48 `bool2int`); baguette's has 1 134
`bool_clause`, 48 `bool2int`, 2 `int_lin_le`. Both visit 29 779 and 108 699 nodes, UNSAT, with 14 890 and
54 350 failures. Gecode's nodes/s is its own `solveTime`; baguette's is the CPU time of the whole run.

| | 3 fixed: instr/node | nodes/s | 2 fixed: instr/node | nodes/s |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Gecode 6.4.0 | 28 000 | 214 000 | 26 800 | 223 000 |
| baguette `--no-proof`, main `214e74d1` (load 8) | 1 572 000 | 3 080 | 2 268 000 | 1 860 |
| baguette `--no-proof`, this branch `c308784d` (load 29-31) | 1 379 000 | 3 560 | 1 911 000 | 2 060 |
| baguette with proof, main (load 8-12) | 2 935 000 | 1 760 | 3 535 000 | 1 190 |
| baguette with proof, this branch (load 30-34) | 2 715 000 | 1 880 | 3 157 000 | 1 140 |

Propagator runs per node: Gecode 57.5 and 55.2 propagations; baguette 413.4 and 613.6 runs
(`bool_clause` 219 and `learned_clause` 177 per node on 3 fixed). So baguette makes 7 to 11 times more
runs per node, and each costs 6 to 7 times more than one of Gecode's. The 2-fixed nodes/s with proof
on this branch is lower than main's only because the load was three times higher: its instruction
count is 10.7 % lower.

### 2. Where a node's instructions go (main, 3 fixed, `--no-proof`)

`perf record --call-graph fp` with the `baguette-fp` switch (D-0145's method), each sample assigned to the
first matching category walking its stack (`tools/cats.py`), share of cycles times instructions per node:

| item | share | instr/node | Gecode | why |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| per-run dispatch: `Engine.run_one`'s bracket (`Fun.protect`), counters, closures, the seed heap and the FIFO | 24 % | 380 k | the same work, done 7 times as often and more expensively | 413 runs per node, each through two or three closures; `caml_apply2` alone is 5.6 % |
| learned-clause upkeep: their runs (`Pb.quiet` over 9 to 16 literals), the advisor asks, `sync_watched` | 24 % | 370 k | does none (no learning) | 177 runs per node, **0.00 effective** |
| conflict analysis: 1UIP, `Analysis.dependency_levels`, the PB attempt that always falls back | 15 % | 240 k | does none | one per failure, 14 890 |
| the wake walk (`watchers_of_new_entries`): per trail entry, every static watcher's trigger and advisor, and the sort of the woken learned clauses | 13 % | 206 k | its own, much cheaper | `List.sort_uniq` over up to hundreds of ids per entry |
| model clause runs (`Pb.quiet`/`Pb.pass`) | 11 % | 180 k | one xor propagator per link | each XOR is 4 three-literal clauses; 219 runs per node |

Under all of it: dune's dev profile compiles every module opaque, so no cross-module function is ever
inlined (`Var.to_int`, `Domain.lo`, `Store.get` are calls, a two-argument one goes through `caml_apply2`).
GC is 6 %, the two cardinality rows (`int_lin_le`, i.e. `Linear`) 2.8 %.

**A correction to the codes-cp note** (WORKLOG, 2026-11-20): `Pb.status` and `Pb.next_free` are not the
two cardinality rows. Those are `int_lin_le` rows, propagated by `Linear` (2.8 %). `Pb` is the code of
every CLAUSE (`Clause.t = Pb.t`, D-0044, M2-L12), and the 13 % was the clauses' `Pb.quiet` walk. So
D-0085/D-0087's watched slack for PB rows has nothing to act on here. The scheme that would act on the
clauses, watched literals for `bool_clause`, removes runs, and the runs are `--stats` counters
(`props`, the per-family table), so it is outside a byte-identical row.

### 3. What was cut, every byte the same

One commit each, measured on 3 fixed `--no-proof`; stdout, every `--stats` line and the `.opb`/`.pbp`
md5 were compared with main's at every step.

| commit | lever | instr/node | binary |
|---|---|---|---|
| `2672822` | `Store.run_as`: the run bracket as `match f x with`, no `Fun.protect` and no closure per run; no wake walk after a run that pushed nothing (nine runs in ten) | 1 572 k -> 1 478 k (-6.0 %) | `214e74d1` -> `6d275ffe` |
| `7ed6938` | the woken learned clauses of one entry sorted in a scratch array by a non-allocating heapsort (`sort_desc_uniq`), the order `List.sort_uniq` gave | -> 1 452 k (-1.8 %) | `4537224b` |
| `47fd373` | `Pb.status` reads the record's fields; `Pb.falsified` is its `Unsat_lit` test in one comparison, for `quiet` and the learned watches | -> 1 398 k (-3.8 %) | `7f87a297` |
| `c052d0b` | the seed heap's sifts as top-level functions, no closure per push or pop | -> 1 378 k (-1.4 %) | `ec418e1e` |

All four, on the merged tip (`c308784d`): 3 fixed `--no-proof` -12.3 %, 2 fixed -15.8 %; with proof -7.5 %
and -10.7 %. Each rule is stated where it lives (`Store.run_as`, `sort_desc_uniq`, `Pb.status` and
`Pb.falsified`, `heap_up`), with the argument that it computes what the old code computed. Clarity
cost: one small heapsort in `engine.ml` and a scratch array argued like `pb.ml`'s; the rest is shorter.
Tried and reverted: skipping the closure call for `Propagator.advise_always` by physical equality, -0.5 %,
not worth the trick.

### 4. Gate

Fresh clone of `wave55-pernode` at `c531645` (which merges `origin/main` `42feb27`, the alldiff merge that
re-recorded the lane's reference; the branch then merged `f41498a`, the thunk merge of D-0168, whose `lib/` changes
are disjoint from these four files, after this gate): `make check` rc 0; 200 models x 4 artefacts (stdout, exit code, .opb,

### 5. Proposals (the user decides)

| # | proposal | measured | consequence |
|---|---|---|---|
| a | **Build the solver with dune's release profile** (a `dune-workspace` with `(profile release)`, and the dev profile's warning flags restated for release so the lint stays as strict) | on this branch: 3 fixed 1 379 k -> 1 149 k instr/node (-16.6 %), 2 fixed 1 911 k -> 1 581 k (-17.3 %); `--stats` and stdout identical | every cross-module call can be inlined; the cost is incremental rebuilds (a change to a module recompiles its dependents) for every session, and the build directory of every clone changes once |
| b | **Do not propagate learned clauses when they cannot prune**: on this model under the fixed search they never do (0.00 effective runs per node, and `skipped 0`: no backjump ever happens) | `BAGUETTE_PROPAGATE_LEARNED=off` on this branch: same trees, stdout and **both proofs byte-identical**; `--no-proof` 3 fixed 1 379 k -> 862 k (-37.5 %), 2 fixed 1 911 k -> 819 k (-57.1 %); with proof -20 % and -36 % | needs a rule for WHEN (by search mode, or adaptive on the effective rate), and changes the work counters; on models with backjumps learned clauses do prune (D-0138), so it cannot be unconditional |

Not proposed here, because the row forbids it and it is a separate decision: learning less (the 15 %

## D-0170  M7-T34: `member` without width-proportional rows -- `b_k -> x_k = y` as four bound clauses and two big-M rows over the declared overlap, the threshold clauses now lemmas written ahead of the lines that walk a hole

Status: DONE (built, measured on the 35 Challenge instances, gated on a fresh clone; the
orchestrator merges)
Date: 2026-11-20
Task: M7-T34 (agent-member2, `wave55-member`, from `wave53-member`'s `1a913cf`), D-0167 item 2,
D-0159 section 5's lever.
Touches: `lib/core/prop/member.ml`, `lib/flatzinc/compile.ml` (`post_member` and its `hold`
comment), `test/unit/test_prop.ml` (member brute force), `test_mutation.ml` (three lanes),
`test_trace.ml` (the I-X10 comment), `test/models/member_{chase_sat,eqhole_sat,eqhole_unsat}.fzn`
and their expected outputs, `bench/member_spike/` (`fuzz_member.py` new, `meas_member.sh`,
`member_rows.py`), PROOF-FORMAT section 4, ARCHITECTURE section 1, CLAUDE.md's map. No
`Explanation` constructor, nothing in `justify.ml`, `trace.ml`, `explanation.ml`, `encoding.ml`.

### 1. The rows

Per position k, [a, b] the overlap of the DECLARED hulls of x_k and y:

    ~b_k \/ [x_k >= a]    ~b_k \/ ~[x_k >= b+1]    ~b_k \/ [y >= a]    ~b_k \/ ~[y >= b+1]
    F_k   sum_{v=a+1..b} ([x_k >= v] + ~[y >= v]) + (b - a) ~b_k >= b - a
    G_k   the same with x_k and y swapped

a constant literal folded (a clause it makes true not written), `~b_k` alone for disjoint hulls,
the big-M pair only when b > a. Under b_k the clauses put both variables in [a, b], where each is
a plus its rungs a+1..b that hold, so F_k and G_k are x_k >= y and y >= x_k; without b_k every row
is true. At most six rows per position whatever the width.

The row the task named first, over the WHOLE hulls (`x_k - y + M ~b_k >= 0`, M = hi y - lo x_k),
was built and counted before it was measured: a rung of an order-encoded variable is a literal of
any linear row over it, so that row has |hull x_k| + |hull y| literals, and over the 35 instances
the pair cost 46.7 M literals against the threshold clauses' 22.4 M. Restricted to the overlap the
pair costs 4 (b - a) + 2 literals against the clauses' ~6 (b - a). The literal mass stays
width-proportional on the order encoding (only a bits encoding could change that); the row COUNT
does not.

### 2. Soundness and the justifications

A line is still one `rup`. The rows propagate the SELECTOR (F_k's coefficient on ~b_k exceeds its
slack once the x/y part is violated) and refute two bounds that cross under b_k (`x_k <= p` and
`y >= q > p`: a bound clause when p < a or q > b, F_k otherwise), but no ladder rung: every rung has
coefficient 1 and the slack is the width left. So:

- lines that only compare bounds are RUP against the rows directly: a selector death by disjoint
  bounds, the last selector set by OR, a bound carried under a set selector, a value of y every
  live position excludes by a bound (each bound-excluded selector dies on its row);
- a line whose argument walks a HOLE needs the bound-form clause of D-0159 at the threshold where
  the bound crosses from one variable to the other. Those clauses are now LEMMAS:
  `R+(k, v) = ~b_k \/ ~[y >= v] \/ [x_k >= v]` and its mirror R-, each RUP from the rows and the
  ladders (assume b_k, [y >= v], ~[x_k >= v]: for v in a+1..b, F_k's left side is at most
  (v-1-a) + (b-v) < b - a; for v <= a or v > b a bound clause closes it).

Which lemmas: a selector death across holes walks runs of one OWNER's holes (x_k or y) on their own
lines, and needs a lemma only where the owner switches; it starts at whichever end is free (the
owner of the end value is the variable whose bound the reason cites, or the declared overlap ends
there), with one more lemma when neither is, and when both are the two walks meet at the last
switch, whose lemma is dropped. A hole carried under a set selector needs one lemma, a value of y
one live position excludes by a hole one, none at an end of the overlap.

The derivation ahead. Such a line is made under `Store.deriving_ahead`; its explanation is ONE
`Combine`: each lemma as a `Term` of its `Clause` (a `rup`) followed by the `Weaken` of all its
literals (the lemma becomes a constant), then the line's own `Clause` scaled by k = 1 + the degree
the weakening cost, divided by k. A `Combine` emits its terms left to right, so the lemmas are on
the page before the line's clause is checked; the result is exactly the line's clause (coefficients
k/k, degree k - (k-1) = 1), which is what a later citation of the entry reads. D-0159's gap shape
(two hole-excluded positions, a case split per selector) keeps its OR + lemmas divided by their
count, with the threshold lemmas weakened in front the same way. No new `Explanation` constructor.
The cost is two lines per such pruning beyond the lemmas: the line's clause is stated once inside
the derivation and once by the trace (Trace states its own line and does not consult the claim
index, M1-T59).

### 3. Tests

- Three new models, every proof VERIFIED: `member_chase_sat` (b1 dies across the holes of x1 and of
  y at level 3, b2's set selector carries y's holes onto x2, a pigeonhole fails the branch so the
  lines are on the page), `member_eqhole_sat` and `member_eqhole_unsat` (holes carried both ways
  under a set selector, at depth and at the root).
- `test_mutation.ml`, three lanes on `member_chase_sat`, a SATISFIABLE model (the rup vacuity trap):
  `chase-start`, `chase-last`, `transfer` each delete ONE lemma and the `pol` from the honest proof;
  veripb refuses at the RUP wording, at the line the lemma was written for. The three D-0159 lanes
  still pass.
- `test_prop.ml`'s brute force reads the new derivation shape (lemma/weaken pairs, the scaled line,
  the divisor) and checks every lemma true on every solution: 1 500 scenes, no violation.
- `bench/member_spike/fuzz_member.py`: 3 600 random small models (n in 2..4 over 1..7, set domains,
  constants, aliasing, side constraints, random search; 400 of them at `--bits-above 0`), answer
  against a brute-force oracle, solution against the model, veripb over every proof: 0 failures.
  On the satisfiable ones every threshold lemma was deleted in turn: 54 load-bearing, 57 redundant.
  The redundant ones rest on holes whose lines hold with no fact (declared, or punched at the root),
  which a walk from a bound clause can cross on its own; the choice above is minimal for holes the
  reason cites. Taking those into account is possible and was not done.

### 4. Measurements

Rows `post_member` writes (`member_rows.py` over the 35 flattened models, D-0159's routes):

| instance | positions | rows before (threshold clauses) | rows after | literals before | literals after |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2023 `mips_mesa.eval.gl_Map1f` | 5 210 | 3 771 621 | 15 725 | 11 308 022 | 6 851 758 |

## D-0171  M11-complexity-T16: the release build for the measured binary (`make release`); same bytes as dev, 5 to 17 % fewer instructions per node

**Context.** D-0169 found that dune's dev profile compiles every library module with `-opaque`, so
no cross-module call is inlined, and measured the release profile at about -17 % instructions per
node on codes-cp QR48. The orchestrator decided, on the user's delegation: a `make release` target,
the Challenge and bench harnesses can use its binary, gates and sessions keep dev.

**Decision.** `make release` runs
`dune build --root . --profile release --build-dir _build_release bin/main.exe` and prints the
binary's md5. A separate build directory has its own lock, so it does not fight the dev `_build/`;
dune does not scan `_build_release/` as source (a leading `_`), and it is in `.gitignore`. No
`dune-workspace` and no profile stanza: a workspace context would build everything twice on every
`dune build`, and D-0169's option (a) (release as THE profile) would change every session's build.
`dune build`, `make check` and a worktree's `--root .` are unchanged. No harness changed its
default: every one already took the binary by variable (`BAGUETTE=` for `compare_run.sh`,
`corpus_run.sh`, `bench/run_bench.sh` and the suite scripts, `BIN=`/`--bin` for the two lanes).
`scripts/README.md` §8 and `bench/challenge/README.md` say to run a series on the release binary
and to record its md5 and its profile.

The release profile does not turn warnings into errors. That hides nothing, because dev stays the
gate on the same sources: a warning dev would refuse never reaches a merge.

**Measured** on `4b6a08f` (sources as main `327141a`), fataepyc-06 at load 59 to 72, binaries dev
`bf6aa1e6`, release `6f6a12c9`. Results copied to `/cluster/arthur/baguette-results/wave55-release/`.

1. Same bytes. Every `test/models/*.fzn` (200) with `--proof`: stdout, exit code, `.opb` and `.pbp`
   of dev and release, 800 comparisons, 0 differences. The diff lane `--tier all` (`-j 8`) with
   `BIN=` each binary: 301 of 301 runs equal the reference both times. The twelve perf runs below:
   stdout, `--stats`, `.opb` and `.pbp` identical between the two.
2. Instructions per node (`perf stat -e instructions:u`, `BAGUETTE_NODE_LIMIT` at the lane's budget,
   the same node count on both sides):

| instance (nodes) | mode | dev k instr/node | release | change |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `H_qr48_bag_def` (6 001) | `--no-proof` | 1 474 | 1 250 | -15.2 % |
| | `--proof` | 2 267 | 2 012 | -11.2 % |
| `2013_rcpsp_11` (10 001) | `--no-proof` | 5 315 | 4 403 | -17.1 % |
| | `--proof` | 17 085 | 15 906 | -6.9 % |
| `2011_cyclic-rcpsp_easy_6` (2 001) | `--no-proof` | 6 545 | 5 435 | -17.0 % |
| | `--proof` | 64 865 | 61 608 | -5.0 % |

   With a proof the gain is smaller because more of the time is in proof text and the stdlib's
   buffers, which are compiled the same way under both profiles.
