## D-0173  M11-complexity-T17: the learned clauses that "cannot prune" are SATISFIED; RESTING takes them out of the wake index, same pruning, another order, so behind a flag (off)

**Status**: **DONE** as a flag, `BAGUETTE_REST_SATISFIED=on` (`Search.config.rest_satisfied`), OFF by
default. Making it the default is a **decision for the user** (section 5). Recorded 2026-11-20 by
agent-learnprop on `wave55-learnprop`. Files: `lib/core/prop/clause.ml` (`Learned_clause`),
`lib/core/engine.ml` (`rest_on`, `release_rests`, `sync_watched`), `lib/core/propagator.ml` (the constant
`rests`), `lib/core/prop/pb.ml` (`holds`), `lib/core/search.ml` and `bin/main.ml` (the knob),
`test/unit/test_engine.ml`, `bench/diff/configs.tsv` and the `rest` references. Measured on `fataepyc-06`
under load 23 to 66, instruction counts (`perf stat -e instructions:u`, minus a 1-node run of the same
binary) as the robust number. Scripts and outputs under `/scratch/arthur/wave55-learnprop-runs/`, the
scripts, counters and summaries copied to `/cluster/arthur/baguette-results/wave55-learnprop/`.

### 1. What a learned clause can still do here, the four candidates examined

- **(a) A nogood made only of negated decisions is never unit again once its subtree is closed.** Not the
  object. The clauses registered for propagation are the 1UIP clauses (`Search.register_learned`), the
  decision nogoods are proof lines only. And the claim is false for a decision nogood too. `~d1 \/ ~d3`
  learned under `d1, d2, d3` is unit at the root of `~d2`'s subtree whenever that sibling is explored
  (another conflict below `d2` named level 2), where it forces `~d3`.
- **(b) A 1UIP clause asserts at its backjump level and is unit again only after a restart or a backjump.**
  False in this DFS. It is unit at the root of every later subtree hanging below its assertion level, and
  above that level chronological backtracking un-falsifies its lower literals and later decisions can
  falsify them again. Neither a restart nor a backjump is needed.
- **(c) Two watched literals would make a non-unit clause free.** Learned clauses already have them
  (D-0104, M6-T22, D-0142). The hundreds of ids one trail entry wakes (D-0169, item 4) are exactly the
  visits of the clauses watching the literal just falsified. What MiniSat does that this engine did not is
  leave a SATISFIED clause alone (section 2).
- **(d) A per-clause activity that stops waking clauses that never prune.** Loses pruning by construction,
  and section 2 shows nothing has to be lost.

The one rule of this kind that is search-neutral by proof was measured and is worth nothing. A clause
satisfied at a level the DFS never pops again (the prefix of second branches above the current node,
without restarts) can be dropped for good. On QR48 3 fixed that covers 14 889 of 5 283 653 learned-clause
runs, about one per clause.

### 2. What the 177 runs per node are

An instrumented build (not committed) classified every learned-clause run on the two QR48 instances of
D-0169 (`dom/sym_p47_w8_basis.dzn` "3 fixed", `..._f2_...` "2 fixed", flattened with `tools/baguette.msc`).

| | runs | of a SATISFIED clause | with the true literal WATCHED | effective |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 3 fixed (29 779 nodes) | 5 283 653 | 5 283 653 (100 %) | 5 166 230 (97.8 %) | 0 |
| 2 fixed (108 699 nodes) | 42 408 976 | 42 408 976 (100 %) | 41 877 893 (98.7 %) | 0 |

So every run is a satisfied clause woken because its OTHER watch was falsified. The run walks the clause,
moves that watch to the next free literal, and the clause is woken again when that one falls. A concrete
case. A clause learned in the left branch `x_k = 1` contains `x_k <= 0`, which the right branch decides.
For the whole right subtree the clause is true, and each deeper decision that falsifies its current second
watch costs a wake, a queue slot, a walk and an index move.

A first cut skipped only the runs (the advisor declined when a watched literal is true). 3 fixed went from
1 380 k to 1 223 k instructions per node, and 2 fixed went UP, 1 911 k to 2 044 k, at three times the CPU
time. A satisfied clause that no longer moves its watch stays in the slot of a variable the search keeps
re-deciding, and is asked again at every re-descent. The asks were the cost, so the clause has to leave the
index.

### 3. The rule, why it loses no pruning, and why it is not search-neutral

**RESTING.** A learned clause whose run finds one of its two watched literals TRUE does nothing, moves
neither watch, and reports `(w, Propagator.rests)` from `inst_watched`. The engine then indexes it under
`w` alone and files it under the decision level of the bound holding that literal up (`lo x` for `x >= k`,
`hi x` for `x <= k-1`). Its advisor declines everything while it rests. At the first propagation after a
backtrack that popped that level, the engine seeds it (`release_rests`, and a released clause stays seeded
by every call until it has actually run, since a conflict can drop its run). That run finds the literal
still true and rests again, or goes back to the two watches it left.

**No pruning is lost.** A clause with a true literal cannot prune or fail, so declining is I-P7 read
literally. Once released, its two watches are good again. The second watch was non-false or falsified at
the current level when the clause began to rest, so at or above the true literal's level, and the backtrack
that pops the true literal's support pops it too. That is the argument behind MiniSat's satisfied clauses.
The one other case, a clause seeded as newborn or young, is re-seeded after any backtrack below its birth,
as before this row (rule (b) of the incremental seed, M6-T18). Filing under the level of the CURRENT support and not of the first
crossing releases early at worst, which costs one run that changes nothing. Checked by
`test_engine.ml`'s scene (rests, is not run, is released, propagates, with its control) and by 500 random
searches with and without the rule, equal domains at every fixpoint (and, there, equal trails in 500 of
500). Under `BAGUETTE_DEBUG`, whose `check_skip`, I-P7 and `check_fixpoint` re-run what was skipped or
declined, 289 of 289 debug lane runs and 200 of 200 model tests with the rule on raised nothing, and every
proof was accepted.

**But the order can change.** The old engine moved a satisfied clause's false watch, resting keeps it. After
the release the two engines watch different literals, so the clause can be woken at another trail entry.
The engine runs a woken learned clause later, at its seed slot or in the FIFO, so with an earlier wake it
can find itself unit and force its literal BEFORE another propagator woken in between, whose reason would
have been on the trail. Example, `a \/ b \/ c` with `a` true at level 3. At level 5 `b` falls, the old run
moves the watch to `c`, resting keeps `b`. Back at level 2 a run R1 falsifies `b`, then R2 falsifies `c`.
The old engine is woken by R2 and resting by R1. In the FIFO the resting clause then runs ahead of a row `Y`
that R2 wakes too, and forces `a` first, where the old engine runs `Y` first (lower id, same wake). The trace
line for `a` cites the clause instead of `Y`. Different reasons make
different 1UIP clauses, so different trees. A search-neutral version would have to reproduce the old watch
moves, which needs the old queue positions of runs that a conflict can cut, which is the cost removed.
On QR48 nothing a learned clause does is ever effective, so the order never shows there.

### 4. Measured

QR48, the same tree (binary `1fed7ed7`, the rule's logic as merged; `88275b8` only trims the default path).
Instructions per node, stdout, every `--stats` search counter and both proof files byte-identical with the
rule on and off.

| | main `bf6aa1e6` | rest on | learned propagation off (D-0169 b) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 3 fixed `--no-proof` | 1 380 k | **923 k (-33.1 %)** | 862 k (-37.6 %) |
| 3 fixed with proof | 2 718 k | **2 250 k (-17.2 %)** | 2 167 k (-20.3 %) |
| 2 fixed `--no-proof` | 1 911 k | **886 k (-53.6 %)** | 819 k (-57.1 %) |
| 2 fixed with proof | 3 157 k | **2 111 k (-33.1 %)** | 2 018 k (-36.1 %) |
| learned-clause runs per node, 3 / 2 fixed | 177.4 / 390.2 | 7.0 / 8.3 | 0 |

CPU time at load 23, 2 fixed: 50.1 s to 17.0 s without proof, 91.7 s to 40.9 s with. The rule keeps 85 to
94 % of what switching learned propagation off gains there, and keeps every pruning everywhere else.

The differential lane, rule on against the reference: **250 of 301 runs differ** (188 a SEARCH counter
first, 17 the `.pbp`, 6 stdout, 39 WORK only), and 241 of 289 in the debug pass. The differences are
small (`cls-prune` 82 against 78 on parity-learning, decisions 2513 against 2515 on QR72), the order of
section 3. Rule off, **301 of 301 equal** the reference, WORK counters included. The lane's 27 lines at
their budgets, instructions per node rule on against main (`bf6aa1e6`), the trees differing:

| | median | best | worst |
|---|---|---|---|

## D-0172  M11-complexity-T15: explanations as a DAG whose nodes carry their line; the memo table goes and every byte stays (A), and hash-consing the written nodes writes share mode's proof for less than main costs (B)

Status: DECIDED. A and B landed, B (hash-consing) ON by default and share mode removed, by the
orchestrator on the user's delegation (D-0167 item 3 had already put sharing on by default).
`BAGUETTE_HASHCONS=0` turns B off. Sections 1 to 7 are the spike as measured on `795e869`;
section 8 is what landed, its re-record and its gate.
Date: 2026-11-20
Task: M11-complexity-T15 (agent-dag, `wave55-dag`). D-0140 J1, after D-0168 (option B) and D-0158
(share mode).
Touches: `lib/core/explanation.ml` (the type: `Clause`, `Linear`, `Cut`, `Combine` and `Resolve`
become inline records with `mutable line` and `hid`; `node_line`, `set_node_line`; the
hash-consing table; T13's frame, `captures`, `nodes_under` and `keep` removed),
`lib/core/justify.ml` (the memo table, its shallow hash, D-0168's window, ghost and release of
cells, and the second forcing at a release removed; `memoized` reads the node; a thunk whose
tree answered takes that line), `lib/core/store.ml`, `engine.ml`, `trace.ml`, `search.ml` (the
producer of a build, for `BAGUETTE_MEMO_STATS` only, and patterns), `pb_analysis.ml`,
`prop/maxmin.ml`, six test files (patterns), `test/unit/test_justify.ml` (the D-0166 and D-0168
tests restated without memo cells), `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` section 4.

### 1. Where identical explanations come from

`BAGUETTE_HASHCONS=1 BAGUETTE_MEMO_STATS=1` counts every node built and whether it equals a
node whose line is on the page, by the propagator that built it (a node built inside a thunk
is counted for the propagator that made the thunk). At the budgets of section 3:

| instance | producer | `Combine` builds | identical to a written node | per node |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `2020_cable_tree_wiring_R046`, 300 nodes | `all_different_int` | 17 513 990 | 17 314 925 (98.9 %) | 57 525 |
| `2011_black-hole_9`, 40 nodes | `all_different_int` | 3 499 845 | 3 230 221 (92.3 %) | 78 786 |
| `2011_cyclic-rcpsp_easy_6`, 2 000 nodes | `all_different_int` | 2 271 912 | 2 000 001 (88.0 %) | 1 000 |
| `2013_rcpsp_11`, 10 000 nodes | `cumulative` | 4 596 500 | 543 369 (11.8 %) | 54 |

Every other producer (`bool2int`, `array_int_element`, `learned_pb`, the search and the
analyses) builds `Clause`s or a few thousand `Combine`s, and two of all those builds (on
cyclic) are identical to a written one. So the identical explanations are, all of them, the derivations a
`Needs_derivation` family writes ahead of its trace line (I-X10): all_different's Hall
derivations and cumulative's capacity derivations, rebuilt from scratch each time the
propagator finds the same Hall set or the same overloaded time point again at another level.
On cable and rcpsp_11 the count is exactly D-0158's "shared" column (17 314 925 and 543 369):
the identity at the build finds the lines share mode finds by rendering them.

### 2. The design

1. **A node carries its line.** The five constructors a line is written for are inline
   records, `Combine of { summands; divisor; mutable line : line; hid : int }` and so on. The
   `line` is D-0168's record (id, level, epoch, owner) and is live under D-0168's test
   (`wiped_at.(level) <= epoch`), so a wipe stamps its levels and visits no node.
   `Justify.memoized` reads and writes the field. What goes: the memo table of
   `justify.ml` (its chains, its shallow hash with the 48-node operand walk, `by_level`, the
   growth), D-0168's window, ghost and release of cells, and in `explanation.ml` the frame
   that recorded every build during a forcing and the second forcing at a release. They all
   existed to take a written tree's cells out of a table, and no table holds a node any more.
   This is variant A, and its memo answers exactly what main's answered (the same lookups
   and hits on the four instances, 8 971 984 and 4 366 803 on rcpsp_11).
2. **Hash-consing in the smart constructors** (variant B, `BAGUETTE_HASHCONS=1`). The key is
   the constructor, its integers and literals, and every operand by identity (`hid` for a
   node, `tid` for a thunk, the id for a `Model_row`). It is shallow because the operands are
   themselves canonical, so a lookup costs the size of the node and never descends.
3. **The table holds the written nodes and nothing else.** `Justify` enters a node when it
   writes its line, at the writer's level, and `wipe_level` takes that level's nodes out with
   the lines. A build of equal content returns the written node, whose line is then cited. A
   line deeper than the writer's current level does not answer (the claim index's condition
   2, as in share mode), and a node whose line was wiped is written again, as D-0168 does for a
   thunk. Two other scopings were measured and dropped. A weak table answers according to
   whether the collector has run, and the same run wrote a different proof with
   `BAGUETTE_MEMO_STATS` on. A table scoped by the store's level at the build never answers
   (rcpsp_11 at 300 nodes, 0 identical builds found against 67 264 with the weak table),
   because the identical rebuilds come after the level that built the first copy was undone,
   while its line, written at a shallower level, is still on the page.
4. **Thunks** keep D-0168's line. One change in both variants: a thunk whose tree answered
   with a line already on the page takes that line, its level and its epoch, instead of a new
   record at the writer's current level. Main's choice states a shorter life than the line
   has when the line is shallower (the thunk is then rewritten to the same id after its own
   level is wiped, the same bytes), and a longer one when the line is deeper, which can happen
   only inside `with_level` (PB learning at level 0), where the thunk could then be cited after
   its line was deleted. Not observed on main, and closed here.

### 3. Measured

On `fataepyc-06`, proof mode, `perf stat -e instructions:u`, peak RSS from `/usr/bin/time`,
under `systemd-run -p MemoryMax=32G`, at the budgets of D-0158 and D-0168 (`BAGUETTE_NODE_LIMIT`
10 000 for rcpsp_11, the lane's 2 000 for cyclic, 300 for cable, 40 for black-hole_9). "main" is
`d275d46` (md5 `c3b9cd1b`, gate 72's binary), "share" is main with `BAGUETTE_MEMO_SHARE=1`, A and
B are `795e869` (md5 `3f888e58`) without and with `BAGUETTE_HASHCONS=1`. Instructions in G,
RSS and `.pbp` in MB. The runs are under `/scratch/arthur/wave55-dag-runs/r/`.

| instance | main | share | A | B |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| rcpsp_11, instructions | 175.61 | 203.29 (+15.8 %) | 138.65 (-21.0 %) | 162.38 (-7.5 %) |
| rcpsp_11, RSS | 144 | 157 | 145 | 160 |
| rcpsp_11, `.pbp` | 420.7 | 374.3 | 420.7 | 374.3 |
| cyclic, instructions | 130.67 | 117.01 (-10.5 %) | 127.61 (-2.3 %) | 54.48 (-58.3 %) |
| cyclic, RSS | 99 | 95 | 101 | 105 |
| cyclic, `.pbp` | 490.0 | 86.7 | 490.0 | 86.7 |
| cable, instructions | 536.19 | 379.30 (-29.3 %) | 518.11 (-3.4 %) | 192.28 (-64.1 %) |
| cable, RSS | 4 646 | 2 069 | 4 586 | 2 068 |
| cable, `.pbp` | 1 887.2 | 114.1 | 1 887.2 | 114.1 |
| black-hole_9, instructions | 737.96 | 705.93 (-4.3 %) | 734.18 (-0.5 %) | 666.36 (-9.7 %) |
| black-hole_9, RSS | 2 230 | 1 603 | 2 173 | 1 577 |
| black-hole_9, `.pbp` | 617.1 | 316.6 | 617.1 | 316.6 |

Stdout and the `.opb` are main's on all sixteen runs, and veripb `d5644ca4` accepts all sixteen
proofs (`s VERIFIED NO CONCLUSION`). A's `.pbp` is main's byte for byte on the four. B's is
share mode's byte for byte on rcpsp_11, cyclic and cable (the same md5), and on black-hole_9 B
writes 266 907 `pol` lines where share mode writes 266 817, the same size to 0.1 MB. Share mode
on the branch writes main's share-mode bytes for less (rcpsp_11 166.08 G, cyclic 114.30,
cable 358.23, black-hole_9 701.47).

**Why B costs less than share mode for the same proof.** Share mode finds an identical line by
rendering it, so every miss emits its operands and builds and hashes the whole `Pol.t` before
it can be answered. B finds the identical node when it is built, by a shallow key, and its
emission is then one field read that skips the whole subtree.

**What B costs where little is identical** (rcpsp_11, 11.8 %): 23.7 G more than A. A profile
of both at 10 000 nodes puts the collector at 17.6 % of B's instructions against 7.7 % of A's
(about 18 G), because the table keeps every written node alive until its level is wiped, so
the nodes are promoted and marked where A drops a written tree at once; hashing and comparing
nodes is 3.9 % (about 6 G). RSS is +11 % on rcpsp_11 and +6 % on cyclic, and -56 % on cable
and -29 % on black-hole_9, where the lines B does not write are most of the live state.

- **B, the model suite** with `BAGUETTE_HASHCONS=1`: 200 of 200, every proof through veripb.

- `dune runtest --force` on the branch: 4 270 ok, 0 FAIL.

### 5. What it costs in clarity

- **`Explanation.t` changes shape, and gains mutable state.** Five constructors go from tuples
  to inline records with two more fields, `mutable line : line` and `hid : int`. A pattern now
  names the fields it reads and ends in `_` (`Combine (ss, d)` becomes
  `Combine { summands = ss; divisor = d; _ }`): 30 lines of `lib/` and about 25 of `test/`,
  mechanical. A node can no longer be built without spelling `line = No_line; hid = 0`, so the
  rule "build through the smart constructors", which was a comment, is now visible at every
  site that breaks it. The D-0026 split is untouched: `Reason.t` keeps the facts and these
  nodes stay the cutting-planes data, nothing is merged. `same_derivation` ignores the line.
- **Removed.** `justify.ml` goes from 1 977 to 1 505 lines (the table, its hashing, the window,
  the ghost, the release of cells). `explanation.ml` loses T13's frame and `captures`, and gains
  the hash-consing table and the per-producer counts (900 to 990 lines with B; A alone would be
  shorter than main).
- **What a propagator author must know.** Under A, nothing new, and one rule less: D-0168's
  "a closure hands nobody a node it built" protected the release of memo cells and has nothing
  left to protect. Under B, a node may be the same value as another propagator's identical
  derivation, so nothing may rely on the physical identity of a fresh build, nor on its line
  being unset.

### 6. The tests restated

The D-0166 and D-0168 tests counted memo cells (`Justify.memo_stats`), which no longer exist. They
now ask the property the count stood for: every node remembers its line
(`Justify.remembered`), after a wipe exactly the nodes below the wiped level answer, and a
released thunk's tree is collectable (a weak pointer to it is empty after `Gc.full_major`,
which is stronger than a cell count). Two checks went: "the forcing saw the captured node"
(nothing tracks captures) and "a thunk whose closure gives two derivations is not released"
(there is no second forcing outside `BAGUETTE_DEBUG`, which refuses such a closure as I-X6
says, and the thunk is released like any other).

### 7. The decision left to the user

| option | proof bytes | instructions against main | peak RSS | clarity |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| land A | the same | rcpsp_11 -21.0 %, cable -3.4 %, cyclic -2.3 %, black-hole_9 -0.5 % | the same (±3 %) | `Explanation.t` becomes inline records with a mutable line; 470 lines fewer in `justify.ml`; D-0168's frame and second forcing gone |
| land B on by default | share mode's: cable -94 %, cyclic -82 %, black-hole_9 -49 %, rcpsp_11 -11 %; 85 of the lane's 301 references re-recorded (their `pol` counters and `.pbp` hash) | cable -64 %, cyclic -58 %, black-hole_9 -10 %, rcpsp_11 -7.5 % | cable -56 %, black-hole_9 -29 %, rcpsp_11 +11 % | A's, plus a table of written nodes (about 150 lines) and the rule of section 5; share mode then has no use and goes |
| land A, B behind its switch | the same by default | A's | A's | A's plus the switch; share mode stays or goes |
| drop | the same | none | none | none |

Recommendation: land A now, since it changes no byte, passed the gate and removes more code
than it adds. Then replace share mode by B and turn it on by default: it writes the proof share
mode writes and costs less than main without sharing on all four instances, which leaves share
mode's switch nothing to do. That second step changes the proof's bytes and the lane's
`pol` counters on the runs where something is shared, so it is the user's call, as D-0158 left
share mode.

**Decided** (orchestrator, on the user's delegation): land A and B, with B on by default in place
of share mode, and a documented switch to turn it off.

### 8. What landed

## D-0181  M15-symmetry-T3: the chain that follows the search, and what VeriPB accepts in the middle of a proof

Status: step 1 DONE (tools and measurements, no solver code). Step 2 PROPOSED (the dynamic case, a
design; the user decides any `lib/` change and whether dejavu's library runs beside baguette)
Date: 2026-11-20
Task: M15-symmetry-T3 (agent-sym3, `wave55-sym3`)
Touches: `tools/symmetry/symchain.py` (`--order search`, `--orient`), `tools/symmetry/symmerge.py`
(negative points, the probes `--as-rup` and `--unit-probe`), new `tools/symmetry/midproof.py`,
`scripts/sym_lane.sh` (`--chain`, `--solver`, `--no-base`, a `:Wmax=K` source, the `huge` tier, the
controls pinned to a cut that is not implied), `bench/symmetry/instances.tsv` (qr32_w8, qr48_w8,
qr48_w12), new `bench/symmetry/stc_bug/` (a checker bug, §4), this record, `docs/ROADMAP.md` (T3
row), `WORKLOG.md`. Nothing in `lib/` or `bin/`. Solver binary `243d84cd` (main `b1bb157`), dejavu
`f984485` as distributed (`bb1759d0`), checker `~/.cargo/bin/veripb` 3.0.2 (`d5644ca4`). Runs in
`/scratch/arthur/wave55-sym3-runs/`, copied (without proofs) to
`/cluster/arthur/baguette-results/wave55-sym3/`.

### 1. The static case: the chain takes the search's own order

`symchain.py --order search` takes as the point of each level the FIRST break variable in search
order whose orbit under the current stabilizer is nontrivial (T2's `first` score), and orients the
cut by the value choice. The point becomes a literal p, the value the search tries first. It is
p = x for `indomain_max` (the cut x_c v ~x_b, T2's) and p = ~x for `indomain_min`, `indomain`,
`indomain_split` and SPEC 3.4's default (the cut ~x_c v x_b). `--orient max|min` forces one
orientation, for the controls below. Without `--order search` everything is T2's, byte for byte.

Why it agrees with the search. Every break variable before c_i in search order is fixed by G_{i-1},
because it is an earlier point or its orbit is trivial (symchain checks it and writes
`prefix_fixed` per level, true on every level measured here). Let s* be the lex-first solution in
search order under the value choice. If s* violated a cut p_i v ~b, an element g of G_{i-1} with
g(p_i) = b would give the solution s* o g, equal to s* before c_i and with the preferred value at
c_i, so lex-smaller than s*. Hence s* satisfies every cut. A depth-first search with a static
order and value choice finds s* first, with learning and backjumping too (a learned constraint is
satisfied by s*, so the trail up to the first decision that leaves s* always agrees with s*). The
broken search therefore reaches the same first solution, and on a satisfiable model the breaking
cannot cut the branch the search was heading to. This guarantees that the breaking loses nothing.
It does not make the search faster.

The proof needs nothing new. A literal permutation commutes with negation, so the orbit of ~x is
the negation of the orbit of x with the same words, a swap of x and y swaps ~x and ~y, and the
`dom` order is the lex order of the points' negations (`load_order symlexN ~p_1 .. ~p_N`).

### 2. Step 1 measured: T2's static chain against the chain that follows the search

`make sym` with `--chain "--order search"` against the default, depth 3, the annotation's search
(`bool_search(x, input_order, indomain_max)` on the codes, SPEC 3.4's first-fail with the min value
on the test models, which have no annotation). One run each on fataepyc-06 under a load of about
60, wall seconds. Every merged proof is `s VERIFIED` against the original `.opb` with the expected
answer. In the points, x_k is the k-th coordinate or model variable, and ~ marks a point pushed to 0.

The QR48 rows are codes-cp's qr48orb instances (its 17 296 words of weight 12 as the checks, no
fixed coordinate), from `dom/sym_p47_w8_nofix.dzn` with `Wmax` set to 4, 8 or 12 (the row order may
differ from codes-cp's benchmark file, the code and the group do not). QR48 runs with `SYM_TL=3600`.

On every code the two chains are the SAME chain, with the same points and cuts, `.fzn` files that
differ only in MiniZinc's comment line, and the same node counts. The codes are searched in input order with the
value 1 first and their groups are transitive (2-transitive for QR, 5-transitive for Golay), so T2's
largest-orbit rule already takes x1, x2, x3 in search order, and T2's cut x_c v ~x_b already pushes
the point to the value tried first. On the three satisfiable codes the broken search visits exactly
the nodes of the unbroken one (24, 122, 1 108), which is §1's guarantee at work.

On the test models the search-order chain is WORSE (php_unsat 9 -> 53 nodes, php_escape_sat 20 ->
67), and on all 15 instances it stays at or below the "without" column, as §1 predicts. Two causes,
which the other two cells of the 2 x 2 (`--orient`) separate:

| instance | largest orbits, point to 1 (T2) | largest orbits, point to 0 | search order, point to 0 (`--order search`) | search order, point to 1 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `php_unsat` (UNSAT) | **9** | 47 | 53 | 37 |
| `php_wide_unsat` (UNSAT) | **17** | 63 | 77 | 61 |
| `restart_pigeons54` (UNSAT) | **7** | 23 | 17 | 13 |
| `colour_unsat` (UNSAT) | **11** | 25 | 15 | 17 |
| `php_escape_sat` (SAT) | **20** | 62 | 67 | 51 |
| `restart_queens6` (SAT) | 23 | 24 | 24 | **6** |

- The orientation matters most. When solutions are sparse (one hole per pigeon, a few coordinates of
  a code word), "the point is 1 unless its whole orbit is 0" keeps one solution in |orbit| and puts
  the point in the support. "The point is 0 unless its whole orbit is 1" is almost always true
  already (x1 = 0 follows by propagation) and removes little. Agreeing with `indomain_min` picks the
  weak one.
- The points matter next. The search order walks one pigeon's row (x1, x2, x3), whose orbits shrink
  at once (30, 4, 3), where the largest-orbit rule takes a diagonal (30, 20, 12). At full depth
  (`--depth 40`, until the group is trivial) the gap stays (`php_unsat` 9 against 25 nodes,
  `php_wide_unsat` 11 against 53). On the codes the full chains are again identical (Golay has 7
  levels, w <= 4 goes 21 -> 9 nodes and w <= 8 24 -> 12).

The fighting control on the codes (search-order points pushed to 0 by `--orient min`, against the
search's 1 first) confirms the orientation from the other side. UNSAT gets much worse (Hamming
w <= 2 5 -> 9, Golay w <= 4 21 -> 83, QR32 w <= 4 21 -> 129, QR48 w <= 4 45 -> 6 859 nodes and
2.1 -> 139.8 s, QR48 w <= 8 1 273 -> 10 269 nodes and 42 -> 570 s). SAT moves either way (Hamming
w <= 4 4 -> 8, Golay w <= 8 24 -> 21, QR32 w <= 8 122 -> 86, QR48 w <= 12 1 108 -> 803 nodes and
57.4 -> 41.8 s).

### 3. Where the static chain hurts: qr48orb_w12, and the dynamic search

codes-cp measured the harm on qr48orb_w12 with other solvers (HiGHS 4.3 -> 25 s, CP-SAT 176 ->
332 s) and, for baguette, 71.8 -> 73.8 s with the annotation and 37.8 -> 45.8 s with
`baguette-act` (`--search activity --restarts luby --phase-saving --reuse-trail`, tiered
retention). Here with our binary, one run each, the same flags passed to both runs
(`--solver`):

| instance | search | without | T2's chain (the search-order chain on the codes) | the chain pushed to 0 (`--orient min`) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| QR48, w <= 12 (SAT) | annotation | 1 108 nodes, 57.4 s | 1 108, 58.7 s | 803, 41.8 s |
| QR48, w <= 12 (SAT) | activity | 401, 31.0 s | 441, 35.1 s | 146, 17.7 s |
| QR48, w <= 8 (UNSAT) | activity | 8 596, 608.7 s | 702, 38.0 s | 4 912, 307.5 s |
| QR48, w <= 4 (UNSAT) | activity | 9 597, 195.6 s | 45, 2.1 s | 5 311, 100.6 s |
| QR32, w <= 8 (SAT) | activity | 115, 0.24 s | 115, 0.23 s | 16, 0.06 s |

Every merged proof is `s VERIFIED` against the original `.opb`. The chain pushed to 0 makes the
QR48 w <= 8 proofs 3.7 GB (0.8 GB for T2's chain under the activity search), checked in 2 586 s with the annotation
(10 269 nodes, 8.6 GB of checker memory) and 1 276 s with the activity search (4 912 nodes).

- With the annotation there is no harm to remove. The static chain is the search-order chain and
  the broken search visits the same 1 108 nodes. codes-cp's 71.8 -> 73.8 s is what the 115 extra
  rows cost on the same tree.
- The activity search cannot be followed by a chain chosen before it starts, and there the chain
  costs 10 % on the satisfiable QR48 (401 -> 441 nodes), the same sign as codes-cp's 37.8 -> 45.8 s.
  The chain pushed to 0 finds the solution 2.7 times faster (146 nodes) and costs about 100 times
  more on the two unsatisfiable QR48 (45 -> 5 311, 702 -> 4 912). Pushing three coordinates to 0 is
  close to fixing them at 0, because x1 = 1 forces its whole orbit to 1, over the weight bound. It
  gives a smaller space that still holds weight-12 words, and almost no breaking.
- So the orientation that pays depends on the answer more than on the search. On the unsatisfiable
  codes, where breaking pays at all (QR48 w <= 8 15 945 -> 1 273 nodes with the annotation, 8 596
  -> 702 with the activity search), T2's chain is already the right one under both searches. The
  harm codes-cp saw with HiGHS and CP-SAT comes from their own searches, which no chain written into
  the model can follow.

### 4. The dynamic case: what VeriPB 3.0.2 accepts in the middle of a proof (measured)

With a dynamic order the next decision is known only during the search, so a cut that follows it
must enter the proof where it is used, after baguette's learned constraints. `midproof.py` takes a
T2 merged proof of a SATISFIABLE model (so no `red` is judged over a contradictory database,
D-0053) and inserts, after some of baguette's learned `rup` lines, the cuts of another `symchain`
run, each a `red` with its swap. `golay_w8` (3 938 learned lines in all):

| inserted | default mode | `strengthening_to_core on`, explicit subproofs |
|---|---|---|
| the chain EXTENDED (level 3 of the same chain, 20 cuts, witnesses fixing x1 x2 x3) | after 80 learned: VERIFIED. After 1 974: refused at the first cut, proofgoal 5143, a learned constraint | VERIFIED after 80 and after 1 974 |
| the chain RE-BASED (level 0 of a chain rooted at x6, 23 cuts) | refused at the first cut, proofgoal 3846 (a cut of the first chain), after 80 and after 1 974 | refused, proofgoal 3847 (a cut of the first chain), after 80 and after 1 974 |
| the orientation FLIPPED (~x1 v x_b on top of x1 v ~x_b, 23 cuts) | refused at the third cut, proofgoal 3846 | refused at the third cut, proofgoal 3847 |
| control: the extended or re-based cuts as bare `rup` | refused, so they are not implied where they stand and the acceptances above are judgements | |

`php_escape_sat` (216 learned lines, insertion after 103) agrees. Extended (5 cuts of level 3)
VERIFIED in the default mode, and accepted in the strengthening mode up to baguette's `sol` line,
which then falsifies one of the new cuts, because the run that wrote the proof did not have them (a
solver that installs the cuts finds a solution that satisfies them). Re-based (at x20) and flipped
are refused at the first cut in both modes, proofgoals 25 to 28, the first chain's cuts.

Read from the checker's source and then measured:

- In the default mode `red` has a goal for every derived constraint its witness touches
  (`red_strengthening.rs`, `add_derived_goals = !is_strengthening_to_core`). The image of a learned
  constraint under a symmetry is implied by the model but is not RUP in general, so a cut introduced
  after learning is refused once its witness touches enough learned constraints.
- In `strengthening_to_core` mode `red` checks the core only, and a chain can be extended at any
  point of the proof, because the new witnesses fix the earlier points and the earlier cuts map onto
  cuts. Re-basing or flipping is refused. Cuts from two bases are not closed under each other's
  witnesses, as the ROADMAP row expected.
- **A checker bug.** In that mode a `red` WITHOUT an explicit subproof puts its constraint in the
  DERIVED set (`RedStrengtheningRule` keeps the default `add_constraints_to_core = false`,
  `veripb-checker/src/rules.rs:107`, which `DomStrengtheningRule` overrides), and later `red` lines
  skip the derived set, so they are checked against no earlier cut at all. Measured, the re-based
  and flipped insertions above are ACCEPTED without subproofs, and
  `bench/symmetry/stc_bug/false_unsat.pbp` gets `s VERIFIED UNSATISFIABLE` for x1 + x2 = 1 (two
  variables, satisfiable) on both 3.0.2 builds (`d5644ca4`, `78db9573`). The same proof without the
  mode is refused at line 12 (`default_mode.pbp`), and with an empty `: subproof` .. `qed ;` on each
  `red` it is refused at line 15 (`with_subproof.pbp`). baguette never writes
  `strengthening_to_core`, so no proof it emits is affected. Any design below that uses the mode
  must give every `red` an explicit subproof until the checker is fixed. To report upstream.
- In that mode a core cut cannot be deleted unless it is implied (checked deletion is a proof by
  contradiction, `deletion.rs:161`, measured on a three-variable proof). And `load_order` moves every
  derived constraint into the core (`load_order.rs:42`), so a `dom` cut (the cuts with no swap, QR
  levels 2 and 3) cannot be added after learning without making every learned constraint a goal.

### 5. The dynamic case: the options (PROPOSED)

From §4, a cut is accepted where it is used only if every core cut maps, under its witness, onto a
constraint that is present or implied there. A witness from the stabilizer of the points already
used does that for the earlier cuts. Nothing does it for the cuts of another base, nor for learned
constraints in the default mode.

| | (a1) one global chain, extended lazily | (a2) branch-local chains | (b) a family of chains, switched at restarts | (c) orbital / orbitopal fixing as propagation |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| what it is | each new point is the variable the search decides when the chain is extended (the first descent, or at a restart the unfixed variable of highest activity in a nontrivial orbit of the current stabilizer). Points never change, cuts are never removed | at a node with decisions D, the next decided variable c gets its orbit under the pointwise stabilizer of D's variables, and the cuts ~D v c v ~b | k chains computed in advance (other bases or orientations), one active per restart window | orbital fixing (Margot; Ostrowski et al.): at a node, x_b := 0 when b is in the orbit, under the stabilizer of the variables branched to 1, of a variable branched to 0. Orbitopal fixing (Anders, Codel, Heule, TACAS 2026): units at the root for a row-interchangeable matrix |
| proof (VeriPB 3.0.2) | `red` with a swap where the cut is introduced, `strengthening_to_core on` at the head and an explicit subproof on every `red`. Measured, §4. Cuts without a swap are lost: `dom` needs `load_order`, which moves every learned constraint to the core | `red` with a witness in the stabilizer of D. It closes while every other branch's cut is falsified by D on a fixed variable, i.e. under chronological backtracking. After a backjump or a restart an old cut whose condition still holds is mapped off the database and refused (§4, re-based), and keeping it is unsound in general. It cannot be deleted either: a core cut in that mode is undeletable, and in the default mode every touched learned constraint is a goal | a second base or a flipped orientation is refused (§4, both modes, after 80 and 1 974 learned constraints). A switch must delete the old cuts AND every learned constraint, which may encode the old chain: a restart without learning | orbital fixing: each fixing is a conditional cut ~D v ~x_b, the proof problem of (a2). Orbitopal fixing: static units, one `red` each at the head (D-0177 measured one accepted) |
| sound with learning and restarts | yes: global, permanent, one base | no, unless learning is switched off under the cuts | only by forgetting all learning at each switch | orbital: as (a2). Orbitopal: yes, it is static |
| cost | one stabilizer per new point, at most n in a run: `set_base` + `sift_random` in dejavu's library (backend B), no graph search. Not measured | one stabilizer query per decision | k chains up front (47 to 151 s per chain on QR48 with backend A, growing with Wmax) | an orbit computation per node |
| needs in `lib/` | a hook in `search.ml` at a decision or a restart; the cuts as permanent clauses (`learned.ml`, pinned in `retention.ml`); `writer.ml` writing the mode and the subproofs, and no `del range` over a cut's id; a client for a symmetry server. `Explanation.t` unchanged: a cut is a clause whose propagation is RUP | all of (a1), a cut store per level deleted on backtrack, and chronological backtracking under the cuts | (a1)'s writer and installation, and a restart that forgets everything | a propagator over the group with (a2)'s proof |
| agrees with the search | with the first descent (under an annotation, exactly §1's chain), then with the activity order at each extension, never re-based | at every node | within a window | it reads the branching by construction |

### 6. Recommendation, and what is left to decide

The static case needs nothing more. `--order search` exists, and on the codes it is T2's chain. It
should not become the default, because on the test models it loses to T2's chain (§2), since the
orientation that agrees with a min-value search is the weak one for sparse solutions.

For the dynamic case the recommendation is (a1), one global chain, extended lazily and never
re-based. It is the only option that stays sound under learning and restarts and that VeriPB 3.0.2
accepts as it is (§4, with the explicit-subproof workaround). Its new points would be the search's
choice of variable (at the first descent, then at restarts the unfixed variable of highest activity
in a nontrivial orbit) with T2's orientation (the point pushed to 1 on sparse 0/1 models). It is not
worth building yet, for three measured reasons.

1. Where breaking pays (the unsatisfiable codes), T2's static chain already gives the large gain
   under both searches (QR48 w <= 8: 8 596 -> 702 nodes with the activity search), and the full
   chain of PSL(2, 47) has 3 levels, so a lazy chain could only choose which three points.
2. Where the static chain hurts (qr48orb_w12 under the activity search, 401 -> 441 nodes), the lever
   measured is the orientation, and the right one depends on the answer. A dynamic choice of points
   does not reach it.
3. A cut introduced after learning can only be a `red` with a swap, so the 68 `dom` cuts of QR48
   (levels 2 and 3) would be lost, and §8 shows that no other chain has swaps there.

If the user wants it anyway, it needs, in `lib/` (a decision, and a claim on `lib/core/search.ml`,
`learned.ml`, `retention.ml` and `lib/proof/writer.ml`), the four items of §5's (a1) column, and,
beside baguette, a symmetry server, that is a C++ process over dejavu's header-only library (`set_base`,
`sift_random`, `get_transversal_element`, D-0177's backend B), with dejavu unchanged and outside
baguette, as the user's rule requires. Whether to run that server is the user's decision too.

To do in any case, report the strengthening-to-core bug to VeriPB with `bench/symmetry/stc_bug/`.
The checker is the sole oracle (D-0046), and a design that uses that mode is unsound on 3.0.2
without the workaround.

### 7. The lane and its controls

- `scripts/sym_lane.sh` gains `--chain ARGS` (to symchain), `--solver ARGS` (to both baguette runs),
  `--no-base`, a source `mzn:FILE:Wmax=K`, and the tier `huge` (run only when named: qr48_w8,
  qr48_w12). `make sym` without options is T2's lane, and its results are unchanged.
- The controls are now pinned to a cut that is NOT implied by the lines before it. A probe
  (`symmerge --as-rup K`) writes cut K as a bare `rup`, and if VeriPB accepts it every mutation of
  it is accepted for that reason alone. Under `--order search` on `php_escape_sat` every cut after
  the first of a level is RUP (the pigeon's exactly-one row), and all four controls on T2's choice
  (the second cut of level 1) were accepted, so the lane takes the next level-1 cut, then the first.
- A second probe (`--unit-probe K`, the point alone as a unit with the cut's witness) marks the
  bad-cut control VACUOUS when the unit is derivable, since c v X is then a weakening of a derivable
  line. On `php_escape_sat` with its points pushed to 0 (`--order search`, or `--orient min`) the
  unit ~x2 is derivable (with x2 = 1 the pigeon's row makes the swapped image ~x3 hold), so the lane
  reports "refused 2/2 (cut 29), vacuous: auto/bad-cut dom/bad-cut", the bad witnesses refused at
  full wording. When every level-1
  cut is implied (search-order points pushed to 1 on `php_escape_sat`), the lane says VACUOUS for
  that instance. Every other control run (hamming_w4, golay_w8, qr32_w8, under every chain) is
  refused 4/4.
- `tools/symmetry/midproof.py` is §4's probe, kept for the T4 to T7 rows and for checking a fixed
  checker.
- The default lane after these changes (`final-static`) gives T2's rows unchanged (nodes, verdicts,
  controls 4/4). `make check` on the branch (`DUNE_JOBS=4`): `check: ok`.

### 8. D-0179's last question: does another chain find swaps on QR?

No chain can. A swap of c and b is an element g of the level's group with g(c) = b and g(b) = c, so
g^2 fixes c. If the group has odd order, the order k of g is odd, and g = g^(k+1) = (g^2)^((k+1)/2)
fixes c too, against g(c) = b. So a group of odd order has no swap. The level groups of QR48 after the first point are the stabilizer of one
point, of order 51 888 / 48 = 1 081 = 23 x 47, and of two points, of order 23. Both are odd, and
PSL(2, 47) is 2-transitive, so every choice of the first two points gives conjugate groups of the
same orders. QR32 is the same (PSL(2, 31): 14 880 / 32 = 465, then 15). So on QR every cut of
levels 2 and 3 is a `dom` under any base, any order and any orientation. This also caps (a1) on QR: a level
added after learning would be lost entirely.
## D-0183  M13-codes-leads-T1: the root LP relaxation of baguette's own `.opb`, measured before any code. Nothing on the codes, a bound on a third of the Challenge sample, fixings on two instances

Status: STUDY (no solver code, a recommendation for the user)
Date: 2026-11-20
Task: M13-codes-leads-T1 (agent-lp, `wave55-lp`)
Touches: `tools/lp/opb2lp.py` (new), `bench/lp/` (new, `gen_codes.sh`, `gen_challenge.sh`,
`run_lp.sh`, `table.py`, `check_cert.sh`, `minweight_opt.mzn`). Runs in
`fataepyc-06:/scratch/arthur/wave55-lp-runs/`. The tables, the per-instance results, the
certificates and the checker logs are copied to `/cluster/arthur/baguette-results/wave55-lp/`.

### 1. The question, and the tool chain

The ROADMAP row, after the user's direction of 2026-11-19, asks to solve the LP relaxation of the
model's linear rows at the root and to use its bound and its reduced-cost fixings, each consequence
being one `pol` (a nonnegative combination of rows, then a division). This study measures first what
the root LP alone would give, on the codes and on Challenge instances.

- The LP solver is HiGHS 1.16.0 (git `f3f113d`) through `highspy` 1.16.0 from PyPI, in a venv at
  `/scratch/arthur/wave55-lp-runs/venv`, one thread. It is the HiGHS version of codes-cp's benchmark.
  Nothing is installed into baguette.
- The model is baguette's own `.opb`, written by the release binary (`make release`, md5 `7c880bce`)
  at `--time-limit 0`. The LP is therefore over exactly the rows a `pol` could cite, which are every
  model row, the ladder rows and the objective's `min:` line (its constant included, a maximisation
  negated, PROOF-FORMAT §3). Every Boolean is relaxed to `0 <= x <= 1`, and `~x` is `1 - x`.
- `tools/lp/opb2lp.py` reports, per instance:
  - `prop`, bounds propagation of the same rows at the integer level, which stands in for the
    solver's root. The literals `X_ge_v` are read back into intervals, and a row's terms on `X` are
    the step function `sum of c_v over v <= x`. Literal-level PB propagation is useless on these
    rows because every literal of an order-encoded linear row has the same coefficient, so it never
    fires. The first version of the script did exactly that and reported a root bound of 0 on
    rcpsp_13, whose critical path is 69.
  - `LP0`, the pure relaxation, and `LP1`, the relaxation with the propagated bounds fixed. The gap
    closed is `(LP1 - prop) / (UB - prop)`, with UB baguette's incumbent from the M7-T26 tables
    (`/scratch/arthur/m7t26/<YEAR>/results.tsv`, 1 200 s runs). `gap closed 2` is the same against
    the best known value (Chuffed's, when it is better).
  - What the cutoff `obj <= UB - 1` adds. Bounds propagation runs first, because the solver gets
    that once it holds an incumbent, and only fixings beyond it are counted. The LP over those bounds
    proves UB optimal if it is infeasible or if `z > UB - 1`. Otherwise a free literal at its lower
    bound with reduced cost `d_j > (UB - 1) - z` cannot be 1 in an improving solution (symmetrically
    at its upper bound), and bounds propagation runs again to count what these fixings imply.
  - For comparison only, HiGHS's own root (`mip_max_nodes = 1`, 60 s), which adds its presolve,
    cuts and heuristics but no branching.

### 2. The codes. The root LP gives nothing, and cannot

`bench/lp/gen_codes.sh` builds Golay (`qr23`), QR48 (`qr47`) and the random [80,40] codes of phase 1
(seeds 1 to 3, distances 9, 10 and 10 from codes-cp's `results/phase1-p1`) with codes-cp's
`gen/p1.py` and `writers/write.py`. They are flattened through `models/minweight_chk.mzn` with
`ENC=2`, the parity checks written as sums `= 2y`. That gives 12 decision instances, UNSAT at `d-4`
(QR) or `d-1` (random) and SAT at `d`, with 0 or 3 fixed coordinates. The optimisation face
(minimise the weight) goes through `bench/lp/minweight_opt.mzn`, 5 instances.

| | instances | root LP | gap closed | RC fixings | UNSAT at the root |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| decision (12) | golay24 w4/w8, qr48 w8/w12 f0/f3, rand80s1..3 at d-1 and d | feasible on all 12, 0.01 s | n/a | n/a | **none** |
| optimisation (5) | golay24, qr48, rand80s1..3 (d = 8, 12, 9, 10, 10) | bound **1** on all 5, the trivial `x != 0` | **0** | **0** | n/a |

This is structural and not a matter of tolerance. The problem is homogeneous, because any fractional
point scaled down to weight 1 still satisfies every parity row `sum x = 2y` with `y` continuous. No
relaxation of these rows can therefore bound the weight above 1, with or without the odd-set cuts
that make each single parity row integral. HiGHS's own root confirms it, its bound after presolve
and cuts being still **1** on all five. What HiGHS does get at the root is a **solution**. Its
heuristics found a word of weight `d` on golay24 and qr48 (and 13, 12, 13 on the random codes against
9, 10, 10), and a codeword on the three SAT decision instances golay24_w8 and qr48_w12 f0/f3, each in
under 0.1 s. The MILP solvers' lead on the codes' SAT and optimisation questions (the M13 evidence,
Gurobi 73 of 83 P1 instances with every clear win a SAT or optimisation question) comes from primal
heuristics and node speed, **not from the LP bound**. A root LP in baguette would not move a single
codes instance.

### 3. The Challenge sample, 42 instances in 15 families with linear rows

`bench/lp/gen_challenge.sh` re-flattens each instance with the current `tools/baguette.msc` and
writes the `.opb` at `--time-limit 0`. The selection takes up to three instances per family among
those where baguette had an incumbent, unsolved ones (TIMEOUT) before OPT and the smallest flattened
model first. 39 of the 42 finished. The three team-assignment instances (33 to 52 MB of `.opb`, 0.1
million literals) did not finish in 900 s. Their parse takes 1 s, so the time goes to the script's
Python propagation or to the LP, which this run does not separate. HiGHS's own root stays at the
trivial bound (-1 000) on the one where it did not crash.

| family (n) | prop -> LP1 bound (UB) | gap closed (vs baguette / vs best) | RC fixings with baguette's UB | with the best known | HiGHS root (cuts) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| radiation (2) | 114 -> 708.7 (711), 51 -> 854.8 (856) | **0.996, 0.999** | **154 (+38 by propagation), 207 (+1 344)** | same UB | 710, 856 |
| rcpsp-wet (3) | 0 -> 80 (127), 0 -> 89 (224), 7 -> 332 (929) | **0.63, 0.40, 0.35** / 0.95, 0.92, 0.41 | 0 | **238 (+227)** on j30_27_5 | 84, 97, 332 |
| cyclic-rcpsp (3) | medium_2 42 -> 203 (516), hard_5 52 -> 316 (799), easy_5 85 -> 353 (881) | **0.34, 0.35, 0.34** | 0 | 0 | 204, 316, - |
| stack-cuttingstock (1) | 0 -> 10 (16) | **0.63** | 0 | n/a | 10 |
| rcpsp (3) | 45 -> 51.2, 16 -> 23.0, 69 -> 69 | 0.19, 0.31, 0 | 0 | rcpsp_12, **the LP proves 38 optimal** (after the cutoff's propagation) | 56, 25, 69 |
| mrcpsp (3) | 31 -> 34.7, 25 and 30 unchanged | 0.14, 0, 0 | 0 (j30_17_10, propagation alone proves 26) | 0 | - |
| lot-sizing (3) | 0 -> 60, 50, 40 (1 237..1 869) | 0.05, 0.03, 0.02 | 0 | 0 | 152, 147, 80 |
| depot-placement (3) | 0 -> 0.2, 0.4, 2.9 | 0.002 | 0 | 0 | 13, 31, - |
| bacp, fast-food, fjsp, openshop, stochastic-fjsp, project-planning, concert-hall-cap (2+3+2+2+3+3+3 = 18) | LP1 = prop on every one | **0** | 0 | 0 (fjsp_easy02, propagation alone proves 11) | bacp-9 38, s-fjsp 242 and 328 (all optimal) |

A `-` in the last column is a root that did not finish in 60 s or crashed. Over the 39:

- The LP closes more than 10 % of the gap beyond propagation on **12** instances (radiation 2,
  rcpsp-wet 3, cyclic-rcpsp 3, stack-cuttingstock, rcpsp 2, mrcpsp 1), a trace (0.2 % to 5 %) on 6,
  and **nothing on 21**.
- Reduced-cost fixings against baguette's own incumbent exist on **2 instances**, the two radiation
  ones (154 and 207 literals, from which propagation draws 38 and 1 344 more). Against the best known
  value there is one more (rcpsp-wet j30_27_5, 238 + 227). The LP proves the incumbent optimal on
  **one** instance and only against the best known value (rcpsp_12, 38, where baguette held 39).
- **No LP was infeasible**, on the codes or here, so nothing is UNSAT at the root. Every Challenge
  instance had an incumbent, so none could be.
- LP1 takes under 6 s on 27 of the 39 (one thread), and 17 to 213 s on the other 12 (fast-food,
  fjsp, openshop, mrcpsp, cyclic-rcpsp easy_5, depot ulysses22), whose `.opb` has 0.1 to 0.5 million
  literals and 0.6 to 31 million nonzeros because of the order encoding's horizons. On those the LP
  costs 1 % to 18 % of a 1 200 s run before it gives anything, and it closed a gap on two of them
  (0.34 on cyclic-rcpsp easy_5, 0.14 on mrcpsp j30_37_4). HiGHS's MIP root crashed (SIGSEGV, HiGHS
  1.16.0) on 5 instances where its LP did not, so `run_lp.sh` runs it in a process of its own and a
  crash costs only that column.
- **HiGHS's root with cuts is far stronger than the plain LP.** It reaches the optimum on bacp-9
  (LP 31, root 38), on both stochastic-fjsp (230 -> 242, 300 -> 328), on rcpsp-wet j30_27_5 and
  j30_44_8 (80 -> 84, 89 -> 97) and on radiation m07 (856), and it reaches 80 to 152 against 40 to 60
  on lot-sizing. The bound the MILP solvers enjoy comes from presolve and cutting planes, and much
  less from the relaxation of these rows.

`prop` is bounds propagation of the PB rows. baguette's real root may be stronger where a global
propagates more than its rows (cumulative's time-table, alldiff), so on those families the gap
closed is an upper estimate. On the instances where the LP helps most (radiation, rcpsp-wet,
lot-sizing) the objective is a weighted sum that bounds propagation does not bound at all.

### 4. The proof shape, checked by veripb 3.0.2 on real instances

`bench/lp/check_cert.sh` takes a real baguette proof, cuts it before `output` and `conclusion`,
appends the LP's lines and concludes NONE. It then builds, once per claim, the same proof with that
one claim made one unit stronger, which veripb must reject **at that claim's line and in its own
wording**.

- How the duals are made exact. HiGHS's row duals are floats. Each `y_i > 0` is rationalised with
  `Fraction.limit_denominator(10^6)`, and the multipliers are the numerators over the lcm `D`. They
  are nonnegative integers by construction, so the combination is valid whatever the rounding did,
  and only its strength depends on it. The combination `sum m_i row_i` is computed in exact
  integers. Every coefficient that differs from the target (`D*c_j` for the bound, zero for every
  variable but `x_j` for a fixing) is brought there with a literal axiom (`x` or `~x` times the
  difference), which only weakens the right-hand side. The line ends with `D d` for the bound, or
  `|a_j| d` for a fixing. The script checks in integers that the result still implies the claim
  before it writes anything, and the checker recomputes the arithmetic. An `ia <claim> : @id` after
  each `pol` pins what the `pol` derived. `ia` is a syntactic check, so it is not vacuous over a
  contradictory database the way `rup` and `red` are (D-0053, D-0066).
- rcpsp_13, on baguette's own prefix (a 5 s run, its last `soli` as the cutoff). The bound
  `objective >= 69` (the critical path, where triv is 0) is one `pol` of **5 rows** with `D = 1`,
  because the duals of a chain of precedences are integral, and 947 tokens. Accepted
  (`s VERIFIED NO CONCLUSION`, 6.2 s, 169 MB, on an 84 MB prefix). Its control is rejected at the
  claim with *"Expected constraint is not syntactically implied by the constraint at the hint."*
- radiation m07_07_20, the bound and two reduced-cost fixings. baguette found no incumbent in 30 s,
  so the incumbent is HiGHS's optimal point (856, found in 42 s), logged into baguette's
  `--time-limit 0` prefix as `@lpsol soli <all 68 065 literals>`, which veripb re-checks against
  every row. The bound `obj >= 853` (LP0 852.43) is one `pol` of **57 rows** with `D = 7`, and each
  of the two fixings is one `pol` of the same 57 rows plus the cutoff, 5 995 tokens. All three are
  accepted (0.15 s), and the **three** controls are rejected, each at its own line (5, 7 and 9) with
  the wording above.
- rcpsp_12. The LP0 bound `obj >= 24` (LP 23.03, `D = 186`, 56 rows, 2 585 tokens) is accepted. The
  optimality of 38 is **not** certified by this script, because the LP proves it only over the
  bounds that propagation draws from the cutoff, and the script's certificates cite model rows and
  literal axioms only. In baguette those bounds are root facts that already have ids, so the `pol`
  would cite them in place of axioms. That was not built here.

One consequence costs one `pol` whose length is the dual's support (5 to 57 rows here) plus one
axiom term per variable it touches (hundreds to thousands). The axioms are the dominant part, and
`w` would write them shorter.

### 5. Recommendation

| option | what it buys, measured | what it costs |
|---|---|---|
| **A. Do not build it now** (recommended) | nothing is lost on the codes, the reason M13 was opened, since the root LP is provably 1 there and HiGHS's root with cuts is 1 too | none |
| B. A root LP bound, opt-in, for objectives that propagation cannot bound | the bound on about a third of this sample, fixings on 2 of 39 against baguette's own incumbent, one `pol` each (5 to 57 rows, D <= 186), the shape verified | an LP solver inside an OCaml solver (C bindings to HiGHS, or an exact simplex of our own). The bound alone shortens no search unless it is re-solved at nodes, a far larger change |
| C. Cutting planes at the root (CG and {0,1/2} cuts, each a `pol` with a division) | where the MILP root's strength actually is, the optimum at the root on 6 of these instances | a separation loop and its tuning, a study of its own |

A is recommended because on the question M13 was opened for the measurement is unambiguous. All 17
codes instances get zero gap closed, zero fixings and no root UNSAT, and that is structural. The
MILP solvers' advantage on the codes' SAT questions is their primal heuristics and their node rate
(D-0169 measured the node rate). If the Challenge side is wanted later, C should be studied before
B, because the plain relaxation of order-encoded rows is weak exactly where HiGHS's cuts close the
gap.

## D-0184  M4-T6: in-proof tabulation over the order encoding. It transfers, at about five lines per pair of operand values, and two removals in three did not need it

Status: SPIKE (no solver code, no default changed, a recommendation)
Date: 2026-11-20
Task: M4-T6 (agent-tab, `wave55-tab`)
Touches: `bench/tabulation_spike/` (new: `tabulate.py`, `run_spike.sh`, `no_table.py`, four models).
Runs in `fataepyc-06:/scratch/arthur/wave55-tab-runs/`, the summary and the scaling models copied to
`/cluster/arthur/baguette-results/wave55-tab/`. Binary `main.exe` md5 `0c1ff1e5` (branch base
`b321667`), veripb 3.0.2.

### 1. The question

The ROADMAP row asked whether the GCS route to GAC arithmetic (derive a table of the relation inside
the proof, then justify every pruning by support reasoning over it, with no `.opb` change) carries
over to baguette's ORDER encoding, where `x = v` is not a literal but the pair
`x_ge_v /\ ~x_ge_(v+1)`. It was answered on `int_times(x, y, z)` with a generator
(`tabulate.py`) that reads the `.opb` the solver writes, so the formula is the solver's byte for
byte, and writes a `.pbp` of its own. No module was added under `lib/`, see section 6.

### 2. The proof shape (all of it checked by veripb 3.0.2)

Per pair `(a, b)` of declared values of x and y with `c = a*b` inside z's declared box, one fresh
selector `s_ab` and two `red` lines, the literals `l_1..l_k` being those of `x = a`, `y = b`,
`z = c` with constants dropped (`k <= 6`):

```
red +k ~s +1 l_1 ... +1 l_k >= k : s -> 0 ;        DEF1   s -> every literal
red +1 s +1 ~l_1 ... +1 ~l_k >= 1 : s -> 1 ;       DEF2   every literal -> s
```

That is the shape the bits encoding already uses for its order atoms (PROOF-FORMAT §3,
`Encoding.ensure_atom`), and both are accepted for a fresh selector. Then the at-least-one row
(ALO) `sum s >= 1` is derived from D-0060's guarded rows, by `rup` only, in three layers:

| line | per | shape | why it is needed |
|---|---|---|---|
| ZLO, ZHI | pair | `x <> a \/ y <> b \/ z_ge_c`, and `... \/ ~z_ge_(c+1)` | with x and y fixed the guarded rows are cardinality rows over z's ladder, which propagate only once a z literal is assumed |
| CAB | pair | `x <> a \/ y <> b \/ s_ab` | DEF2 closes it once ZLO and ZHI fix z |
| DEAD | pair with `c` outside z's box | `x <> a \/ y <> b` | the pair has no selector |
| PERA | value of x | `sum_b s_ab \/ x <> a` | assuming `x = a` and every `s_ab` false, the CABs walk y's ladder to a conflict |
| ALO | once | `sum s >= 1` | the PERA lines walk x's ladder |

The lemmas are then deleted. What stays is DEF1, DEF2 and ALO, that is `2|T| + 1` constraints.

Every GAC removal is then ONE line, `rup [w <> u] \/ ~F >= 1`, where `F` names, for each tuple
supporting `w = u`, why it is dead. A tuple dead by a BOUND contributes that bound literal (DEF1
then falsifies its selector by unit propagation), and one dead by an interior HOLE contributes the
hole line's own facts through a KILL line `rup ~s_t \/ ~F_hole >= 1` written first. At the root
every fact is a level-0 consequence and `F` is empty. A failed node writes the nogood over its left
decisions, and a solution is logged with `sol` over the model's literals, the selectors following by
propagation.

**So the tabulation transfers to the order encoding.** The equality literal is never needed as a
variable. It lives inside DEF1 and DEF2 as its two order literals, and a removal's claim is the
two-literal clause every hole already uses (D-0086's one hole currency).

### 3. The cost

Lines at the root, measured: about `5 |Dx| |Dy| + |Dx| + 1`, that is 2 `red` + ZLO + ZHI + CAB per
live pair. The ROADMAP's "about ten lines per constraint" is GCS's figure and does not hold here,
where it is quadratic in the operands' declared widths. Scaling on
`x in 0..k, y in -k..k, z in -k^2..k^2, z <= -1, z <> -2`:

| k | pairs in the table | tabulation + search lines | `.pbp` bytes | `.opb` bytes (unchanged) | check time |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 3 | 28 | 166 | 13 212 | 7 591 | 0.01 s |
| 5 | 66 | 376 | 32 482 | 24 239 | 0.01 s |
| 7 | 120 | 674 | 60 150 | 55 666 | 0.02 s |
| 9 | 190 | 1 060 | 96 254 | 106 504 | 0.05 s |

The tabulation costs about as many bytes as the `.opb` rows D-0060 already writes for the same
constraint, and checking it is negligible at these widths. Per search node the cost is one line per
removed value plus at most one KILL line per tuple killed by a hole.

### 4. Verified models and mutation controls (`run_spike.sh`, exit 0)

| model | answer | solver (D-0060, bounds) nodes / `.pbp` lines / bytes | tabulation nodes / lines / bytes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `tab_times_sat` | SAT | 2 / 7 / 511 | 3 / 211 / 17 572 |
| `tab_times_holes_sat` | SAT | 4 / 9 / 529 | 3 / 225 / 18 149 |
| `tab_times_holes_unsat` | UNSAT | 3 / 65 / 3 276 | 1 / 209 / 17 235 |
| `tab_times_gap_unsat` | UNSAT | 5 / 62 / 2 125 | 1 / 62 / 3 651 |

Every tabulation proof is `s VERIFIED` with the same answer as the solver's, checked in 0.01 s.
On the two SAT models each control is refused at the line it targets, asserted by the line's shape
and by the checker's full sentence:

| mutation | refused at | wording |
|---|---|---|
| wrong selector definition (z = c+1 for a tuple of a solution; both `red`s still pass, a fresh definition is always sound) | that tuple's CAB | "The constraint is not implied by reverse unit propagation (RUP) from core and derived database." |
| DEF2 with the witness `s -> 0` | that `red` | "Proofgoal #1 could not be autoproven. Please add an explicit subproof for proofgoal #1." |
| removal of a supported value | that line | RUP sentence |
| ALO with no lemma | ALO | RUP sentence |
| CAB without ZLO/ZHI | the first CAB | RUP sentence |
| no KILL lines | `z <> 2` in `tab_times_holes_sat` (supports `(1,2)` and `(2,1)`, killed by the holes `x <> 1`, `y <> 1`) | RUP sentence |

Two of these are measurements of the shape rather than soundness controls. ALO is NOT `rup` from
D-0060's rows (the case split on two operands is not unit propagation), and neither is CAB without
the z lemmas.

**The vacuity trap was met once and is recorded.** The first draft corrupted the tuple `(0,-3,0)`
under `z <= -5`. Both corrupted proofs were ACCEPTED, because the model refutes that tuple anyway,
so its CAB and its `red` goal close on the refutation and never read the definition. The controls now
corrupt a tuple that belongs to a solution, the D-0053 rule applied to one tuple instead of to the
whole database. Likewise the first holes model put the holes in z under a fixed x, where D-0060's
rows refute by unit propagation alone and the KILL lines were not needed. The present model was
chosen by a search over random disequality sets on the same box, 60 satisfiable models, whose
60 honest tabulation proofs all verified and 29 of which needed the KILL lines.

### 5. Where GAC cuts search, and how much of it needed the table

Nodes, bounds (the solver) against GAC (the generator's search), on the gap family `x, y in 2..k`
with every product removed from `z in 5..k^2-1`, UNSAT:

| k | 4 | 5 | 6 | 7 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| solver nodes | 5 | 7 | 9 | 11 |
| GAC nodes | 1 | 1 | 1 | 1 |

GAC refutes at the root what bounds consistency must search, and the gap is `2k - 3` nodes here.
That is linear, and on a larger model clause learning would learn such a root-refutable fact once.
None of the four spike models needs more than three nodes either way.

The control `no_table.py` asks, for each GAC removal, whether it is `rup` against the `.opb` alone
(every earlier line given as an axiom). 23 of 37 are (10/12, 11/18, 2/4, 0/3 on the four models).
D-0060's guarded rows already justify a removal by unit propagation whenever assuming the value
leaves a linear relation that bounds reasoning across the holes refutes, which is the case for most
values of x and y. The table is needed for the other 14, which are values of z with no factorisation
in the box (z = -7) and values whose supports die on holes of both operands.

### 6. Why no prototype module

The search half is cheap (the GAC filter over a table is a few dozen lines). The proof half is what
a build would be, and it needs three things the solver does not have for a propagator today. It
needs `red` definitions of proof-only selectors at the root, which only the bits atoms have
(`Encoding.ensure_atom`). It needs a root-lemma hook to write the ZLO/ZHI/CAB/PERA lines and delete
them (the regular family has one, `Encoding.start_proof`). And it needs the KILL line in the trace,
with the hole's facts as its tail. Writing that unwired would have been a build without its
decision, so it was left for the follow-up row.

### 7. Recommendation

| option | buys | costs |
|---|---|---|
| A. Do not build it now (recommended) | nothing lost on the measured models. Two removals in three are already `rup` against D-0060's rows | the `Bounds` level of `int_times`/`int_div` stays, and with it the extra nodes of section 5 |
| B. A `Domain` int_times that writes plain `rup` where that suffices and tabulates LAZILY (on its first removal that needs the table), under a cap on `|Dx| |Dy|` | GAC on small operands, the table paid only by constraints that use it | the three proof-side pieces of section 6, and about `5 |Dx| |Dy|` lines for each constraint that tabulates |
| C. Tabulate every small-domain arithmetic constraint at the root | the simplest code | the full quadratic line count on every such constraint, used or not, including on SAT runs whose proof today is one `sol` line |

A is recommended because the search gain measured here is small and linear, and the one fact that
would change that, the node count GAC saves on real instances with small-domain `int_times`/`int_div`,
has not been measured. The follow-up row measures it first, with this generator's GAC as the oracle.
If the gain is real, B is the shape to build, since the spike shows every piece of it checking.
Reverting this record means deleting `bench/tabulation_spike/`. Nothing else depends on it.
## D-0182  M14-e2e-verification-T8: objectives in the end-to-end chain, and the first measurement of `cake_pb_cp` on baguette's search proofs (Challenge)

Status: DONE (tooling, a lane and a measurement, no solver code)
Date: 2026-11-20
Task: M14-e2e-verification-T8 (agent-e2e8, `wave55-e2e8`)
Touches: `tools/e2e/fzn2scp.py`, `tools/e2e/bridge.py`, `tools/e2e/chain.sh`, `tools/e2e/mutate.py`,
`tools/e2e/scpsem.py`, `tools/e2e/fzn_solutions.py`, `tools/e2e/validate.py`, new `tools/e2e/measure.sh` and
`tools/e2e/prefix.sh`, new `bench/e2e_spike/series.sh` and `summarise.py`, `scripts/e2e_lane.sh`,
`scripts/README.md` §9. Runs: `fataepyc-06:/scratch/arthur/wave55-e2e8-runs/` (`lane6/`, `series3/`, `screen/`,
`fzn/`); tables, logs and the flattened instances copied to `/cluster/arthur/baguette-results/wave55-e2e8/`.

### 1. Objectives: what cake writes, what baguette writes, and the bridge

cake_pb_cp's `.scp` takes `(prob_type (minimize X))` or `(maximize X)` (`cp_parseScript.sml`,
`sexp_prob_type`), X a variable name. It writes `min: B_X` for minimize and `min: -B_X` for maximize, over
X's two's-complement bits with no constant (measured). baguette writes `min: k*S_x + k*l` over x's ladder
(`compile.ml`, M5-T1: the objective variable's own order encoding with its constant, k = 1 or -1). Both
are the same function of x, so every objective value VeriPB computes, every `soli` bound and the numbers of
`conclusion BOUNDS` agree, and nothing in baguette's proof needs renumbering. The translator maps `solve
minimize|maximize x` to the prob_type, x resolved through aliases (a constant objective is refused,
since cake's prob_type names a variable).

What differs is the constraint each `soli` adds. Checked against cake's `.opb`, VeriPB adds `k*B <= v - 1`
over cake's bits, where baguette's later lines (rup steps, the bits arm's `pol @soli @B1`, the
lower-bound hint of the conclusion) expect `k*S + k*l <= v - 1` over its ladder. The bridge renames
each `@cK soli ...` to `@O[cK] soli ...` and derives `@cK` from it by the substitution every model
row already gets: `@cK pol @O[cK] @E1 k * +` for minimize, `@E2` for maximize (B >= l + S, resp. B <= l + S).
The bridge checks first that cake's objective is exactly one variable's bit sum times k and that
baguette's is k times the same variable's ladder with constant k*l, and refuses otherwise.

**cake's verdict.** For minimize it prints `s VERIFIED BOUNDS v <= OBJ <= v` with v in the model's
numbers, for maximize the same in the model's numbers (cake converts back; baguette's `conclusion
BOUNDS` is in negated numbers, so the chain negates), and a negative number SML-style (`~6`). An
infeasible optimisation problem prints `s VERIFIED BOUNDS -INF <= OBJ <= +INF` for both directions. That
print is cake's `OBounds NONE NONE`, and under `cp_sem_concl` (`cpScript.sml`) the bound that is NONE on
the side the direction makes universal (`cp_is_lb` for Minimize, `cp_is_ub` for Maximize) means
`cp_unsatisfiable`. So that line is cake's UNSAT for an objective, and the chain requires it when
baguette says `=====UNSATISFIABLE=====`. Measured on both directions (`opt_unsat` and a maximize copy).
A partial conclusion prints the missing side as INF (`BOUNDS 2 : id INF` gives `2 <= OBJ <= +INF`), so
`OPT=v` is accepted only on the exact two-sided line.

### 2. The lane

Binary md5 `4e41e8c1` (dev, the lane's default; solver code unchanged by this task), veripb 3.0.2
`d5644ca4`, `cake_pb_cp` sha256 `ca92491e`. `make e2e`, last run `lane6` on `99b3c98`:

| | before (D-0180) | after |
|---|---|---|
| VERIFIED | 179 (100 SAT, 79 UNSAT) | **188** (100 SAT, 80 UNSAT, **8 OPT**) |
| SKIPPED | 28 | 19 |
| FAIL | 0 | 0 |
| controls | 23 of 23 | **31 of 31** |
| validation | 178 AGREE, 1 UNCHECKED | 187 AGREE, 1 UNCHECKED, 0 DIFFER |

The nine new: `opt_min_sat` (OPT=2), `opt_max_sat` (5), `opt_floor_sat` (0), `opt_ne_sat` (0),
`opt_global_settles_hole_sat` (0), `bits_opt_min_sat` (6), `bits_maxmin_opt_sat` (7),
`restart_queens6_opt` (2) and `opt_unsat` (UNSAT). The one optimisation model still skipped is
`regular_opt` (`baguette_regular`, T6). Skipped now: `baguette_regular` 4 (one with an objective),
`var int` with no domain 4, `int_times` 3, `int_div` 3, `baguette_cumulative` 3, `int_abs` 2.

**Eight new controls, a wrong claimed optimum**, every one refused at the conclusion line with the
checker's whole sentence:

| control | models | refused by, wording |
|---|---|---|
| `opt-better`: baguette's `conclusion BOUNDS` one better than its optimum | `opt_min_sat`, `opt_max_sat` | veripb: "Unable to verify 'conclusion BOUNDS'. The claimed upper bound of N mismatches the best recorded upper bound of N+1." |
| `opt-worse`: one worse | `opt_min_sat`, `restart_queens6_opt` | veripb: "The lower bound claimed for \`conclusion BOUNDS\` is larger than the best logged objective value." |
| `core-better`: the ELABORATED core's conclusion one better, after veripb accepted | `opt_min_sat`, `restart_queens6_opt` | cake_pb_cp: "conclusion BOUNDS check failed: [lb <= dbound] T [upper bound check] F [lower bound check] T" |
| `core-worse`: the core's one worse | `opt_max_sat`, `bits_maxmin_opt_sat` | cake_pb_cp: "... [lb <= dbound] F [upper bound check] T ..." |

The `core-*` pair is the one that matters for the trust argument: veripb is an untrusted elaborator in
this chain, and these show the verified checker itself refusing a wrong optimum. A wrong optimum is a
false claim on every model, so no control here can be vacuous (D-0053 is about `red`/`rup` over a
contradictory database, not about conclusions).

**Validation of the objective.** The references enumerate the model as `solve satisfy` (`-a` on an
optimisation model would print only the improving solutions), and `validate.py` then requires the
.scp's prob_type to name the same direction and variable as the .fzn's solve item, and baguette's last
solution to reach the optimum of the solution set under it. All nine AGREE with their `opt=`. Teeth:
the direction swapped in the .scp gives DIFFER on `opt_min_sat` and `bits_opt_min_sat`, the variable
swapped gives DIFFER on `bits_opt_min_sat`. The solution set alone could not see either.

### 3. The Challenge measurement: which instances

Every instance of the sixteen editions that baguette completed (OPT, UNSAT, or SAT of a satisfaction
problem) in at most 300 s in wave43 (`baguette-results/wave43run/<YEAR>/results.tsv`, 1 200 s budget):
**201**. Re-flattened with this clone's `tools/baguette.msc` (`pair.tsv`'s model and data, 300 s): 200
flatten (`2024_monitor-placement-1id_hop_counting_based_caida_139203` timed out). The translator covers
**166** of them. The other 34: `int_times` 19, `baguette_cumulative` 6, `baguette_regular` 5, `int_abs` 4,
all T6.

Each through `tools/e2e/measure.sh`: translate, encode (`cake_pb_cp`), solve (release binary md5
`53d5f37a`, `--proof`, 300 s, `ulimit -v 4000000`), `veripb` alone on baguette's own files (the
baseline), bridge, `veripb --elaborate` on cake's `.opb` and the bridged proof, `cake_pb_cp` on the core,
each stage timed with peak RSS (`/usr/bin/time`), under `systemd-run --user --scope -p MemoryMax=32G`,
7200 s per checking stage, at most 8 at a time (`bench/e2e_spike/series.sh`, `series3`). `cake_pb_cp`
ran with `--CML_HEAP_SIZE=24576` (24 GB; its default 4 GB is the CakeML default, D-0176), and its RSS
column is what it touched of that heap.

Release binary md5 `53d5f37a` (`make release` of `843a13b`'s solver code), veripb 3.0.2 `d5644ca4`,
`cake_pb_cp` sha256 `ca92491e`, tools at `99b3c98`. Load average 40 to 70 on the shared node.

### 4. The Challenge measurement: results

**Not complete when this record was written.** The series (`series3`) runs cheapest first (wave43's proof
size), and at 15:01 UTC **100 of the 166** had finished; the 66 left are the largest proofs. It keeps
running detached (`series3/series.pid`), and its `results.tsv` is the table of record; `summarise.py`
reads it. The numbers below are those 100.

| VERIFIED by `cake_pb_cp` | **96** (64 OPT, 25 SAT, 7 UNSAT) |
| `cake_pb_cp` heap exhausted at 24 GB ("CakeML heap space exhausted.") | 4: `2016_zephyrus_12__8__6__3`, `2019_zephyrus_12__8__6__3`, `2019_zephyrus_12__6__6__3`, `2015_gfd-schedule_n120f5d50m50k20` |
| refused (veripb or cake disagreeing) | **0** |

On the four, `veripb --elaborate` accepted (`s VERIFIED`), and cake ran out of its heap on cores of 0.4 to
3.3 GB. That is a resource limit, not a refusal: a larger heap would need more than the 32 GB the node's
rule allows a run, so it was not tried. Every baguette answer that reached a verdict was certified,
optimum included.

**Cost, over the 96 VERIFIED** (`veripb` alone on baguette's own files against `veripb --elaborate` +
`cake_pb_cp` on the bridged proof):

10 instances under x5, 52 from x5 to x20, 30 from x20 to x100, 4 above. `cake_pb_cp` takes a median 1.8
times `veripb --elaborate`'s time. Peak RSS: solve 0.41 GB, `veripb` alone 1.08 GB, the bridge 6.3 GB
(`2013_l2p_l2p12`), `veripb --elaborate` 3.0 GB (`2013_black-hole_6`), `cake_pb_cp` 24.0 GB, which is
its whole heap. Proofs: baguette's 1.58 GB in all, bridged 3.76 GB, cores 6.10 GB (largest 0.54 GB); the
bridged proof is a median 2.85 times baguette's.

**Where the cost is: the prefix, not the search.** `tools/e2e/prefix.sh` checks the bridge's prefix
alone (baguette's `.opb` re-derived from cake's, then `conclusion NONE`). On the worst ratio,
`2011_black-hole_17` (UNSAT, 154 variables, widths up to 415, 102 `element`), the whole chain took 1 607
s of elaboration and 58 s of cake; **the prefix alone takes 1 606 s and 54 s**. Its 60 MB hold 137 724
substituted cake rows and **93 043 `rup` pins** (element's direct-encoding clauses, which close by
unit propagation over cake's `eq` atoms, D-0180 §7), against 35 MB of search proof that costs next to
nothing on top. On `2026_saeling` (x175) likewise, 10.6 + 5.1 s for the prefix against 10.5 + 5.3 s
for the whole. So a search proof does not make the chain expensive; baguette's own encoding re-derived
from cake's does, and that is T3's work (the solver writing the prefix from what it knows, `ia` instead
of `rup` for the derived clauses) and T7's (bits, where widths are large).

**The bridge itself** took 3 459 s in all, worst 1 272 s (`2015_p1f_13`, 294 385 `.opb` rows; its matcher
is Python and close to quadratic in a model's rows over one variable). It is untrusted and replaceable,
and T3 removes it; it is reported apart and not in the ratio. The encoder took 55 s in all.
