## D-0194  [AUTONOME] M4-T6b: GAC arithmetic measured before it is built. On the Challenge and codes instances it saves no nodes worth a build, so D-0184's option B is not built

Status: DONE (a measurement and a recommendation, no solver code, no default changed)
Date: 2026-11-21
Task: M4-T6b (agent-gac, `wave56-gac`)
Touches: `bench/gac_measure/` (new: `census.py`, `gac_rewrite.py`, `gecode_pair.sh`, `bag_twin.py`,
`bag_pair.sh`, `summarise.py`, `series.sh`). Runs in `fataepyc-06:/scratch/arthur/wave56-gac-runs/`, the
tables copied to `/cluster/arthur/baguette-results/wave56-gac/`. Binary `main.exe` md5 `bb916498` (release,
branch base `42262b3`), Gecode 6.4.0 through MiniZinc 2.10.1, veripb 3.0.2.

### 1. The question

D-0184 showed that GAC `int_times` can be proved over the order encoding and recommended not building it
until one number was known, the node count a domain-consistent filter saves on real instances with
small-operand arithmetic. D-0060's arithmetic is bounds consistent. This record measures what GAC would
add, three ways, from the cheapest to the most faithful.

`int_mod` never reaches the solver. `mznlib/redefinitions.mzn` rewrites it as `int_div`, `int_times` and
a linear row, so it is counted through those two.

### 2. Census and root probe (`census.py`, every flattened Challenge instance)

1 575 flattened instances (`/scratch/arthur/m8t4/flat/`, the sixteen editions). 426 instances of 53
families post the builtins: 10 029 572 `int_times`, 5 593 `int_div`, 19 353 `int_abs`. A constraint is
`small` when every operand has at most 64 declared values and none is a constant.

| | constraints | share |
|---|---|---|
| an operand is a constant (linear already) | 1 217 065 | 12 % |
| an operand wider than 64 values | 229 098 | 2 % |
| small | 8 608 355 (224 instances, 32 families) | 86 % |
| small with a two-valued operand (a 0..1 indicator times an integer) | 8 593 451 | 99.8 % of small |

So small-operand arithmetic on the Challenge is almost entirely `b * x = z` with `b` in 0..1, posted by
the flattening of conditional sums (code-generator 3.1 M, yumi-dynamic 2.3 M, nside 0.96 M, smelt, fjsp,
gfd-schedule, test-scheduling). The only genuine two-variable products over small domains are in
harmony and vaccine (`int_div` and `int_abs`), stripboard, cable and on-call-rostering (`int_abs`), and
the codes models' squares (section 5).

On each small constraint, from the declared domains alone, the probe compares GAC with the fixpoint of
bounds(Z) consistency over the hulls, which is an UPPER bound on what D-0060's rows do, so its gap is
a lower bound on GAC's root gain. **GAC removes an operand value that bounds(Z) keeps on 0 of the
8 608 355 constraints.** It removes values of the RESULT on 366 688 constraints (42.3 M values, 225 389 of
them in carpet-cutting, 125 219 in mrcpsp): those are the holes of a product, which matter only if
another constraint reads the interior of z.

### 3. Gecode, bounds against GAC under one search (`gecode_pair.sh`)

Up to four instances per family with small arithmetic (the smallest `.fzn`), 118 of them, and the three
codes instances of section 5. Each is flattened with Gecode's library, and its twin replaces every small
`int_times`/`int_div`/`int_mod`/`int_abs` by `gecode_table_int` over the relation's tuples, which Gecode
propagates domain consistently. The model's own search annotations are kept, and each arm gets 150 s.

| | instances |
|---|---|
| flattening failed | 8 |
| nothing to tabulate (Gecode's library posts the indicator products differently) | 49 |
| run | 64 |
| both arms closed (optimum, UNSAT or a first solution) | 14 |
| both at the limit, same best objective | 48 |
| both at the limit, GAC worse (stack-cuttingstock d7, 35 against 38: GAC explored half the nodes) | 1 |
| GAC closed where bounds did not, or found a better objective | **0** |

On the 14 closed instances, nodes GAC / bounds: ATSP 0.913 (69 against 63), atsp 0.955 (155 against
148), stable-goods 0.982, still-life-wastage 0.999 and 1.000. The nine others (compression, nside,
ship-schedule x4, stack-cuttingstock, stripboard) give 1.000. The largest saving measured is 9 % of a
69-node tree.

### 4. Inside baguette (`bag_twin.py`, `bag_pair.sh`)

Gecode has no learning and flattens differently, so the same 121 instances were also run in baguette,
on the `.fzn` the Challenge series ran. The twin replaces every small `int_times`/`int_div`/`int_abs`
by the same relation as a DFA through `baguette_regular` (`state 1 --x=a--> A_a --y=b--> C_(ab)
--z=ab--> accept`, over `[x, z]` when the operands are aliased), which `lib/core/prop/regular.ml`
propagates domain consistently, learning and proof included. It is a measuring device, not option B,
because its rows are a DFA and not D-0184's tabulation. Two twins were run with their proofs and checked:
gfd-schedule n25 (1 579 nodes in both arms, both VERIFIED BOUNDS) and fjsp easy01 (118 nodes against 113,
both VERIFIED BOUNDS). The other runs used `--no-proof`, which does not move the search. Each arm got
240 s.

| | instances |
|---|---|
| no twin (DFA table over the 400 000-cell cap: gbac, cyclic-rcpsp hard_5, routing-flexible) | 9 |
| twin over 3 M state flags (nside, yumi-dynamic) | 7 |
| an arm died (the twin out of its 32G scope on ATSP, atsp, code-generator, ihtc; two Stack overflow crashes, see section 7) | 9 |
| compared | 96 |
| both closed | 26 |
| both at the limit, same best objective | 53 |
| GAC better objective at the limit / closed by GAC only | 4 / 1 |
| GAC worse objective at the limit / closed by bounds only | 9 / 3 |

On the 26 closed instances, nodes GAC / bounds have a geometric mean of **1.096**, a minimum of 0.958
(fjsp) and a maximum of 2.028 (ship-schedule). None is below 0.95. Learning makes the twin's trees
different, and they are not smaller. The five changes in GAC's favour are not node savings. In each, the
GAC arm explored MORE nodes than bounds in the same time: still-life-wastage_09 closed at 217 s after
24 730 nodes where bounds had done 22 201 in 240 s, opd 277 199 against 94 374, maximum-dag 72 677
against 67 800, stable-goods s-d16 6 407 against 5 011, still-life-wastage_12 17 562 against 14 349. That is the DFA device's cost per node, which
is lower than D-0060's rows on those models, and option B would not have that cost.

### 5. The codes models

`codes-cp/models/shortvec.mzn` posts `int_times(x, x, sq)`, x in `-W..W`, which are the only small
two-variable products of the codes models (`minweight` posts none, `code.mzn` avoids `mod` on purpose).
On leech_m2, p48q_m4_b0L and p48q_m4_b1:

| | leech_m2 (UNSAT) | p48q b0L, b1 |
|---|---|---|
| Gecode, model's default (dynamic) branching | 42 757 against 308 831 nodes | both at the limit, no answer |
| Gecode, static input-order search | **221 193 against 221 193** | both at the limit, no answer |
| baguette | 9 583 against 9 577 nodes, **46.9 s against 12.4 s** | both at the limit, no answer |

Under a static search GAC on the squares prunes nothing more. The difference under Gecode's default
branching is the branching heuristic reading different failure counts. The twin solves leech_m2 3.8 times
faster in baguette with the same nodes, so D-0060's case split on `x * x` costs more per node than a
40-state DFA does. That is a lead on the COST of the square rows, not on GAC (section 7).

### 6. Decision

| option | buys, measured | costs |
|---|---|---|
| A. Do not build GAC arithmetic (chosen) | nothing lost: no instance in sections 3 to 5 saves more than 9 % of its nodes, and none changes an answer within the limits through pruning | `int_times`/`int_div` stay `Bounds` |
| B. D-0184's option B (plain `rup` where D-0060's rows suffice, lazy tabulation under a cap) | GAC on 8.6 M small constraints, 99.8 % of which are indicator products where it adds no operand pruning at the root and no measurable node saving in search | the three proof-side pieces of D-0184 section 6 and about `5 \|Dx\| \|Dy\|` lines per tabulating constraint |

**A is chosen.** The bound on an answer within 1 200 s follows from the same numbers. Where both arms
close, GAC saves at most 9 % of the nodes. Where neither closes, the best objective is the same in 101
of the 115 limit pairs (48 of 49 in Gecode, 53 of 66 in baguette). Of the 14 that differ, 4 favour GAC
and 10 favour bounds, and each of the 4 explored more nodes than its bounds arm, not fewer. A 9 %
saving cannot move an instance across the 1 200 s line unless it already sits within 9 % of it. This record is reverted by a family whose
small arithmetic is a genuine two-variable product over holed domains (not an indicator, not a square)
and on which a twin, with both arms closed, saves a large share of the nodes. `bench/gac_measure/`
measures that in one command (`series.sh bag RUN LIST BIN`). Nothing else depends on this record.

### 7. Two findings on the way, not acted on here

- **Stack overflow.** `main.exe 2021_ATSP_instance10_0p25.baguette.fzn --no-proof -s -t 240000` (and
  `2025_atsp_instance4_0p15`) prints its solutions and then dies with `Fatal error: exception Stack
  overflow` before the `%%%mzn-stat` block, in both arms. The Challenge series ran those two with a
  proof and was stopped by the proof cap (CAPPED, REFUSED) before reaching that point.
- **The square rows are expensive.** On codes leech_m2 a DFA over `[x, x*x]` replaces D-0060's case
  split for 3.8 times less time at equal nodes (section 5). A cheaper encoding of `int_times(x, x, z)`
  (one guarded row per value of x is what D-0060 writes, and that is the cost) belongs to the M16
  per-node cost work, not to GAC.

## D-0193  M16-file-review-T5: the front end and the setup read file by file. Under `--no-proof` the objective's `.opb` line was built for nothing, and on 79 of the 150 large instances measured it was nearly the whole setup. The lexer called three closures per byte and allocated a position per token, and the name tables were polymorphic. Seven byte-identical levers, and what is left is `Encoding`'s and `Engine.create`'s

**Status**: DONE, recorded 2026-11-21 (agent-review5, resumed by agent-review5b, `wave55-review5`,
autonomous mode).
**Task**: M16-file-review-T5, `lib/flatzinc/lexer.ml`, `parser.ml`, `builder.ml`, `compile.ml`,
`output.ml` (the cost before node 1, after D-0143).
**Files changed**: `lib/flatzinc/lexer.ml`, `parser.ml`, `builder.ml`, `compile.ml`, `model.ml` (the
`Names` table), `output.ml` (its header only), `test/unit/test_flatzinc.ml` and `test_compile.ml`.
**Runs**: `fataepyc-06:/scratch/arthur/wave55-review5-runs/` (`setup1.sh` one setup-only run, `job5b.sh`
and `s5.sh` the sweep, `lev5.sh` and `lev5slot.sh` the per-lever runs, `models.sh`/`modelsnp.sh` and
`cmpmodels.sh` the byte identity, `tools/s5cmp.py`, `tools/levtab5.py`, `tools/setupattr.py`,

### 1. Method

The setup is everything before node 1, so it is measured by `--time-limit 0` (the run stops at node 1)
with `--stats --time`, under `perf stat -e instructions:u` and `/usr/bin/time`, once with `--no-proof`
(np) and once with `--proof` (pf), the `.opb` and `.pbp` md5 kept. The instances are the 150 Challenge
`.fzn` agent-review5 chose (`top150.list`) after its sweep of the setup over all 1 574 flattened
instances (`setup/sw.np.tsv`). It did not record its rule, and the list holds both the costliest
setups without the proof and seven `train_instance` files whose `.opb` is 90 GB. To these come smelt_11, nonogram_non_med_3 and gt-sort_n9,
whose setup is most the front end's, and D-0143's openshop_gp10-4. The binaries are release builds of main
`95b4406` (`68ed1cf0`) and of the branch before main's merge, `be6f0f2` (`d54edb28`), and one per lever
commit for section 3. The profiles are main's release build under `baguette-fp` (`perf record -e
cycles:u --call-graph fp`, np), attributed by `tools/setupattr.py` to the nearest front-end frame. The
node ran at load 45 to 65 on 192 cores (two Challenge series and the M8-T4 runs), so instruction
counts are the measure and wall times only a check.

Byte identity was checked on the dev builds (`7b967430` main, `d8077c1a` branch) over the 207
`test/models` with `--proof --stats` (stdout, exit code, `.opb`, `.pbp`, `--stats` without timings) and
again with `--no-proof --stats` (stdout, exit code, `--stats`), with 0 differences. On the sweep, stdout
and `--stats` are equal on all 150 np pairs, and stdout, `--stats`, `.opb` and `.pbp` on every pf pair
that finished.

## D-0197  [AUTONOME] hotfix: the "Stack overflow" on the ATSP instances (D-0194 §7) was `Learned.make` recursing once per term on a 32-million-term PB row. Constant-stack walks there and on five more sites, same answers

Agent-stack, branch `wave56-stack`, 2026-11-21. Claim `hotfix`, no ROADMAP row.

### 1. The cause

`main.exe 2021_ATSP_instance10_0p25.baguette.fzn --no-proof -s -t 240000` (binary `dca706be`) prints
two solutions and dies with `Fatal error: exception Stack overflow`, rc 2. With `OCAMLRUNPARAM=b` the
backtrace is 1 022 frames of `Learned.make.merge` (`lib/core/learned.ml:247` at `15a10e0`) under
`Lit.equal` (`lib/proof/lit.ml:183`). A probe build that printed the call stack of every `make` over
more than a million terms found the caller: `Pb_analysis.analyse` (`pb_analysis.ml:1118`,
`Learned.of_pb_row` of the conflict row) from `Search.pb_at_conflict`, on a row of **32 168 204 terms**,
the conflict row over the ladder of `X_INTRODUCED_317_`, a variable 22 072 740 values wide. The merge was
`{ coeff = a1; lit = l1 } :: merge rest`, one frame per term, and 32 million of them pass OCaml 5's
1 GiB stack limit. `2025_atsp_instance4_0p15` gives the same backtrace.

So the crash was in the SEARCH, at the first PB conflict analysis over that row, and not on the exit
path. The `stats:` lines printed before it are the encoding cost, which `bin/main.ml` prints before
search starts. The run "ended rc 0 at -t 30000" because the 63 s setup outlasts 30 s: that run took
no decision.

With `--proof` the old binary does not reach the crash point. After 6.5 minutes it was still writing
the `.opb` (33 GB on disk, 30 GB resident, no search yet), which is why the Challenge series saw
CAPPED or REFUSED rather than the crash.

### 2. The fix

- `lib/core/learned.ml`: `merge_equal_lits`, the merge shared by `make` and `make_reference`. It
  accumulates in reverse and reverses once. `sort_by_lit` no longer calls `List.merge`, which is
  one frame per element in OCaml 5.1.1's stdlib (unlike `List.map` and `@`, which are
  `tail_mod_cons` there), and calls a tail-recursive stable merge instead, earlier run first on a tie.
  `ladder_form`'s per-variable `group` is accumulated too.
- `lib/proof/writer.ml`: `Pol.write_with` walks a `pol`'s left spine with a loop. `Pol.sum` and
  `Pol.lin_comb` build one `Add` per operand, so the recursion was one frame per operand of the line
  being written, which is the same width again on the `--proof` path. `Pol.tokens` (the `--stats`
  shape count) is tail-recursive down the same spine.
- `lib/core/store.ml`: `drop_page_only_lemmas` (a walk over a `Combine`'s summands) is accumulated.

Each module header has one paragraph saying so. None of these changes an answer. The lists come out
in the same order, ties go the same way, and the bytes are written in the same order.

### 3. Sites looked at and left

Checked: every `let rec` in `lib/` and `bin/` whose recursive call is under a `::`, an `@` or a `+`,
and every call of the stdlib functions that are not tail-recursive in 5.1.1 (`List.merge`,
`List.combine`, `List.split`, `List.concat`/`flatten`, `List.fold_right`, `List.remove_assoc`).

- Left because they are bounded by the MODEL's size, not by width or by the run: `List.combine` on
  FlatZinc arrays (`builder.ml:358`, `compile.ml:838`, `e2e.ml`), `pairs` (`compile.ml`,
  `encoding.ml`), `take` (`builder.ml`), `decompose` (`compile.ml`), the `List.concat` of one block
  per variable of a row (`linear.ml:255`, `encoding.ml:2246`), and `Occurs.merge` and `note_held_back`
  (a few entries each).
- Left because they only run in the mutation harness, on the test models: `Writer.rewrite_first`
  and `Writer.cited_ids`. The writer's header says so.
- Not measured: `cumulative.ml`'s ladder walk builds explanations nested as deep as the window it
  crosses (`step prev k`). A recursive emission over that nesting would be one frame per value. No
  instance has been seen to overflow there, and it is a tree to walk, not a list to rewrite. It is
  left for whoever finds one.

### 4. The test

`test/unit/test_learned.ml`, `test_d0197_long_rows_small_stack`. The walks run inside a fresh effect
fiber after `Gc.stack_limit` is lowered to 64 Ki words (512 KiB). A fiber started after that starts
small, while the main stack may already have grown and does not shrink. 200 000 terms is then about
ten times what one frame per term can hold. A probe check asserts that a one-frame-per-element
recursion over 200 000 does overflow there, so the test cannot pass because the limit failed to apply.
The checks drive `make` on two overlapping runs (the stable merge, then the summing), `make_reference`,
`combine` against `combine_reference`, a 200 000-operand `Pol.sum` written and counted, and
`drop_page_only_lemmas`. On the old code the probe passes and the five checks FAIL. With the fix they
pass in well under a second.

A model run under a reduced stack was not chosen. The overflow needs a row tens of millions of terms
long, which only a declared width in the millions produces, and CLAUDE.md forbids wide domains in the
suite. A unit test that shrinks the stack instead of growing the input finds the same defect at width
200 000 with no solver run.

### 5. Measured

Gate on a fresh clone of `wave56-stack` at `99cf6b0` (binary `b8c71132`) against gate 84's
`dca706be`: `make check` rc 0 (4 463 ok, 0 FAIL, which is gate 84's 4 457 plus the six above), 207 x 4
artefacts equal, lane 324/324, debug 311/311, scaling ok. The two ATSP instances, `--no-proof -s -t
240000`, under `MemoryMax=32G`:

| instance | before (`dca706be`) | after (`b8c71132`) |
|---|---|---|
| 2021_ATSP_instance10_0p25 | 2 solutions, Stack overflow, rc 2 | the same 2 solutions, rc 0. Stop fired at **373.5 s** wall, 709 nodes, peak 32 GB plus 5.8 GB swap |
| 2025_atsp_instance4_0p15 | 2 solutions, Stack overflow, rc 2 | those 2 and a third improving one, rc 0. Stop at 240.7 s, 824 nodes, peak 27.7 GB |

### 6. A finding left open

The fix removes the crash and exposes the next limit on instance10. The PB analysis of that one
32-million-term row takes RSS from 11.8 GB to the 32 GB cap in about 2.5 minutes. The profile is
`Store.member_support`, `Hashtbl.find_opt` and `Pb_analysis.falsified_at_with` per term, then the
kernel's swap paths. The analysis polls the stop only between its steps, so the 240 s limit landed
133 s late. A bound on PB analysis by row length, giving the conflict back to the clause path past
some number of terms, would change what is learned on wide instances. That is a default-behaviour
decision for the user, so it is not taken here.


## D-0196  [AUTONOME] M14-e2e-verification-T7: the bits arm in the end-to-end chain. The prefix DERIVES baguette's unsigned offset bits from cake's two's-complement bits by a ripple-carry adder whose every relation is one linear row

Status: DECIDED in autonomous mode on 2026-11-21, before the work that depends on it. Section 6 is
the result.
Date: 2026-11-21
Task: M14-e2e-verification-T7 (agent-e2e7, `wave56-e2e7`)
Touches: this record, `tools/e2e/` (bridge, chain, mutations, models), `scripts/e2e_lane.sh`,
`lib/proof/e2e.ml`, `lib/proof/encoding.ml` (additive), `lib/flatzinc/compile.ml` (the e2e hooks
only), `docs/PROOF-FORMAT.md` §3b.

### 1. Context

Under `--bits-above W` a variable wider than W whose scope allows it (D-0130 §3.4) is encoded on
`x_bit_i`, the bits of `x - l`, unsigned, `n = bit_length(u - l)` of them, with two bound rows and no
ladder (D-0130, D-0132, PROOF-FORMAT §3). cake_pb_cp encodes every integer by its two's-complement
bits `i[X][b<j>]`, weight `2^j`, `j < h`, and `i[X][sign]`, weight `-2^h`, when `l < 0` (§3b). Neither
end-to-end path covered a bits variable: the bridge assumed a ladder, `--e2e` refused (D-0187 §3).

Found while deciding, measured on `bits_ne_sat` at `--bits-above 0` with a scratch bridge: once the
bits are defined, every substituted cake row is over baguette's bits, and baguette's linear rows are
`ia` against them unchanged. What does not follow by `ia` is any row with a guard (a disequality
selector, a reifier, a choice selector, an arith guard): cake's big-M is over the BIT range of the
terms (`bits_imply`), baguette's over the declared bounds, and on a bits variable the two differ
(`x + 17 ~b >= 2` against `x + 11 ~s >= 17` in literal form, for `var 0..9`). On the ladder they
coincide after saturation, which is why the order arm never met it.

### 2. The options

| | what | gains | costs |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) baguette writes cake's representation under `--e2e` | its bits arm declares two's-complement bits and posts its rows over them | the bits are cake's, no definition | a second bits encoding in the solver: every `pol` the bits arm writes (D-0130 §5, D-0132) cites rows whose coefficients change, the minted atoms' pairs too; a large change to lib/core's justifications for one flag |
| (b) the prefix DERIVES baguette's bits from cake's | per digit a linear relation of an adder, each fresh variable defined by a red pair | the solver's proof after the prefix is byte for byte its own (as for the order arm); O(bits) lines per variable where the order arm writes O(width) | the definitions are a new device to get right (checked, so a mistake is a refused line) |
| (c) identity only (`l = 0`, no sign: `x_bit_i` is `i[X][b<i>]`), refuse the rest | trivial | every negative or offset domain refused |
| (d) define `x_bit_(n-1)` down to `x_bit_0` greedily, each by a red pair reifying `x - l - (higher bits) >= 2^i` | no carries | the halves of `B = l + S` then need the big-M of each reification tightened, the same problem as the guards, n times per variable |

**(b).** Over cake's digits `u_j` (`b_j` for `j < h`, `~sign` at `j = h`), `U = B + 2^h [sign]` is
unsigned and `x - l = U - L'` with `L' = l + 2^h [sign] >= 0`. The digits of `x - l` are those of
`U + c`, `c = (2^m - L') mod 2^m`, through a ripple-carry adder, and its relation at digit i is ONE
linear row, `d_i + 2 k_(i+1) = u_i + c_i + k_i` (`k_0 = 0`). While the carry is a constant, the next
one is `0`, `u_i` or `1`; once it is a literal, the next is a fresh variable defined by a red pair
whose two goals are tautologies. `d_i` (`x_bit_i` for `i < n`, a fresh high digit above, which is zero)
is defined by the relation's two halves, a red pair whose goals are the carry's own rows. Summed with
weights `2^i` the relations telescope, so the halves of `B = l + S` (the order arm's `@E1`/`@E2`, now
with `S = sum 2^i x_bit_i`) follow by one `pol` each, after a unit on the final carry and one per high
digit (`rup` against one row each). Everything downstream of the halves, the substitution of cake's
rows (D-0187), is unchanged. With `l = 0` and no sign, every carry is 0 and each bit is a renaming.

**The guards, by contradiction.** A row whose guard's big-M is baguette's own and that cake's
candidate implies only up to that coefficient is derived by `pbc` (D-0195 §2.3's device): the
negation plus the candidate, saturated, forces the guard; the negation plus each negated bits
variable's ub row (`-S >= -(u - l)`, baguette's own, pinned in the prefix) leaves it no room; unit
propagation closes. No new rule, and only where `ia` fails.

**Two definitions the order arm did not need.** (i) A choice-group selector `_mxN` (D-0134) is set
by `sol` to the FIRST operand attaining m and no other, where cake's array_max flag `x[N][<i>]` is
`x_i >= m` both ways: at a tie two flags hold. So `_mx_i` is defined as `F_i /\ ~F_0 /\ .. /\
~F_(i-1)` (a red pair over the conjunction), not as `F_i`; the binary max/min, whose flags have one
direction only, keep the renaming. (ii) An int_abs sign guard over a bits variable is defined as
cake's atom `i[X][ge0]` itself (its order atom `x_ge_0` is minted by the solver's proof, later, and
two definitions of one name would collide).

### 3. How to revert

Revert the commits prefixed `M14-e2e-verification-T7:` on branch `wave56-e2e7` (or their merge).
Nothing outside `tools/e2e/`, `scripts/e2e_lane.sh` and the `--e2e` path changes, and every default
byte stays (the gate compares the 207 models' four artefacts with main's).

### 4. What this does not decide

Whether `--e2e` becomes a default, whether the bridge is retired (D-0187 §5), and whether a wide
domain should go to the bits arm by default (D-0130's threshold stays `none`).

### 5. (reserved)

### 6. Result

**What was built.** In `tools/e2e/bridge.py`: [bits_prefix] (the adder, the halves, `@BL`/`@BU`),
[tight] (a guarded row by contradiction against the ub rows, tried after every candidate failed
strictly), the choice selectors' conjunction (`@C1`/`@C2`) and the abs guard over bits; and a fix
found on the way: the swap cache was keyed on a selector's name alone, so a selector tried as F

## D-0198  [AUTONOME] M6-T2 re-scoped: the trail and the domains are 0.5 to 4.5 % of the words allocated, so no `Bigarray`/`Bytes` move. The lever was the minor heap's size, 256 k words by default, and one sort that forced a minor collection per call

Agent-gc, branch `wave56-gc`, 2026-11-21. ROADMAP M6-T2 asked to find the allocating site with a
profiler before spending the `Bigarray`/`Bytes` change. This record is written before the code it
decides (CLAUDE.md, "Mode autonome"), and §4 adds the measurements after it.

### 1. What the run allocates and what the GC costs, at `0518dc2`

Release binary `9956c047`, on the 21 fast instances of `bench/diff/corpus.tsv` at their lane budget
and on the codes instances `f3` and `f2` (D-0169's, run to the end), with and without `--proof`.
`OCAMLRUNPARAM=v=0x400` for the totals, `perf record --call-graph fp` on the same source built in the
`baguette-fp` switch for the shares. Scripts and outputs in `/scratch/arthur/wave56-gc-runs/`.

- **The allocation rate is the same everywhere**: 14 to 23 words per thousand instructions on all
  46 runs. What varies is the share of it that survives a minor collection: 3 to 13 % on most
  runs, 19 to 25 % on lot-sizing and fox-geese.
- **The GC's share of the cycles**: median 13.3 % without the proof (5.3 % on f2, 42.5 % on
  fox-geese) and 16.6 % with it (9.2 % on f2, 40.3 % on fox-geese). About 60 % of that is the
  minor collector and 35 % the major one. The runtime allocation functions (`caml_make_vect` and
  the like) take 0.2 to 1.5 %.
- **No site dominates.** A GC sample charged to the first non-`Stdlib` OCaml frame above the
  runtime (the site whose allocation crossed the minor-heap limit, or that called the runtime to
  allocate) gives, averaged over the 23 instances, at most 0.72 % of the cycles to one site without
  the proof (`Engine.watchers_of_new_entries`) and 0.65 % with it (`Trace.emit_to_page_inner`).
  The large single sites are on one instance each. `Pb_analysis.lits_array` and `Learned.make`
  take 10.7 % and 8.3 % on fox-geese, already D-0191's subject. `Gcc` takes 6.8 % on lot-sizing.
  `Justify.sort_pairs` takes 10 % on soccer with the proof, see §3.
- **The trail and the domains are not among them.** `Store.apply` is 0.19 % on average (at most
  0.71 %). A probe build that counted the `Changed` arm of `Store.apply` puts the trail's
  allocation, about 20 words a push (the 14-word entry, the 4-word `Domain.t`, the `Changed`
  box), at 4.4 % of the words on f3, 3.3 % on chessboard, 3.2 % on QR48 and 0.5 % on fox-geese.
  Moving the trail and the domains into `Bigarray`/`Bytes` would remove at most that share of the
  allocation. The entry would still point at its `Reason.t`, which is boxed. At a GC share of
  15 %, that is under 1 % of the cycles for a rewrite of `Store`'s central structure. M6-T2's
  premise does not hold, and the row is closed without that change.
  `Store.first_mark_above` allocates a closure per call (0.21 % on average, 1.2 % on fox-geese).
  That is too small to act on here.

### 2. The minor heap: 256 k words by default, 4 M words from here on

OCaml 5.1's minor heap is 256 k words (2 MB). With `OCAMLRUNPARAM=s=...` on the base binary, two
runs each on eight of the instances above (cycles, at load ~50 on a 192-core node, noise about 5 %):

| instance | 256 k | 2 M | 4 M | 8 M |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| f3 `--proof` | 34.6 / 31.1 G | 28.9 / 27.7 | 25.5 / 26.8 | 26.8 / 27.6 |
| f3 no proof | 16.7 / 17.1 | 16.1 / 16.5 | 16.1 / 16.7 | 15.7 / 15.9 |
| lot-sizing no proof | 10.7 / 10.6 | 8.9 / 8.7 | 8.1 / 8.1 | 7.8 / 7.8 |
| rcpsp_12 `--proof` | 7.0 / 7.3 | 6.3 / 6.6 | 6.0 / 6.2 | 5.8 / 5.8 |
| chessboard `--proof` | 9.8 / 8.8 | 8.1 / 8.0 | 7.9 / 8.4 | 8.1 / 7.6 |
| fox-geese no proof | 5.5 / 5.6 | 5.2 / 5.0 | 5.2 / 5.0 | 5.0 / 5.0 |
| QR48 no proof | 3.3 / 3.5 | 3.2 / 3.4 | 3.3 / 3.1 | 3.3 / 3.1 |
| soccer `--proof` | 3.9 / 3.9 | 4.3 / 4.1 | 3.8 / 4.0 | 3.9 / 4.2 |

A larger nursery lets more of the short-lived data (trail entries of a branch that is undone, a
conflict's analysis, a proof line's terms) die young instead of being promoted. Promoted words fall
by 2 to 9 times (f3 with the proof 106 M to 18 M at 4 M words), and the major collector follows.
Soccer does not move: its minor collections are forced, see §3.

| option | consequence |
|---|---|
| keep 256 k | nothing changes; 10 to 25 % of the cycles stay on the table on most proof runs |
| `OCAMLRUNPARAM=s=4M` in the scripts | the lanes and Challenge scripts gain, a user running `main.exe` by hand does not, and every script must carry it |
| **`Gc.set` at the top of `bin/main.ml`, 4 M words, unless `OCAMLRUNPARAM`/`CAMLRUNPARAM` sets `s`** | every run gains; an explicit `s=` still wins; +32 MB resident per process (the nursery is touched in full after the first cycle); and, found by the gate below, 4 GiB of reserved address space |
| the same at 8 M words | a little more gain on lot-sizing and rcpsp, inside the noise elsewhere, +64 MB per process |

**Choice: 4 M words in `bin/main.ml`, cut under a tight address-space limit (below).** It is the knee of the table. 32 MB is the size of one
EPYC L3 slice, and the extra memory is small beside a 92-run campaign's budget or the laptop's 15 GB.
The setting changes only when memory is reclaimed, never a value the solver computes. Nothing in
`lib/` depends on addresses (the one ephemeron, `Search.staged_orders`, is keyed by a live object),
so stdout, proofs and `--stats` must stay byte-identical, and the gate checks that. The test
binaries do not link `bin/main.ml`, so the suites keep the default nursery. The model tests run
`main.exe` and get the new one.

**Corrected by the gate: the address space.** The first gate failed at `make check`'s
determinism self-test with `Fatal error: Not enough heap memory to reserve minor heaps`. OCaml 5.1
reserves the minor heaps of all 128 possible domains in one mapping, so a 4 M-word nursery reserves
4 GiB of address space that is never touched, and every suite and lane here runs under
`ulimit -v 4000000`. So the size now depends on the soft address-space limit read from
`/proc/self/limits`: the largest size up to 4 M words whose reservation is at most an eighth of that
limit, and never below the runtime's 256 k. That is about 490 k words under the lanes' 4 GB cap, the
full 4 M under the corpus scripts' 32 GB cap, under `systemd-run -p MemoryMax` (a cgroup, not an
address-space limit) or with no limit. No `/proc` reads as no limit. Across the lane, against
`0518dc2`, in instructions (median over the 23 instances, the `sort_pairs` change included):

| nursery | no proof | `--proof` |
|---|---|---|
| 512 k (about the lanes' 490 k, under 4 GB) | -3.4 % | -4.1 % |
| 1 M | -5.1 % | -7.7 % |
| 2 M | -6.3 % | -9.8 % |
| 4 M (no limit, 32 GB) | -7.1 % | -11.7 % |

A fixed 1 M words would have been simpler and safe everywhere, but it gives up a third of the gain
on exactly the runs that matter (the Challenge and codes runs, which have no tight limit). The
eighth is the second try. A quarter (1 M words under 4 GB) passed `make check`, the 207 artefacts,
the debug lane and the scaling lane, and lost one lane run: lot-sizing under `activity`, whose major
heap alone peaks at 405 M words (3.2 GB) of its 4 GB cap, ended in `Out_of_memory`. At 488 k words
the same run passes, its peak RSS 3 189 MB against 3 269 MB at 256 k, because the larger nursery
promotes less. That run sits at the edge of its cap with any binary, and the eighth keeps the margin
it had. It leaves 28 GB of the corpus scripts' 32 GB, where `--max-heap-mb=auto` already stops the
solver at half.

**To revert**: the commits `M6-T2: the minor heap at 4 M words` and `M6-T2: the nursery keeps its
reservation within a quarter...` and the one that made it an eighth touch only `bin/main.ml`'s startup. Revert both, or run with
`OCAMLRUNPARAM=s=256k` to get the old behaviour from the new binary.

### 3. `Justify.sort_pairs` forced one minor collection per long claim key

`sort_pairs` sorted a claim key of more than 24 pairs by building an array of tuples with
`Array.init` and handing it to `Array.stable_sort`. Past 256 elements, `Array.make` with a young
initial value (the first tuple) runs a minor collection before it allocates, and the merge sort's
scratch array does the same. On soccer with the proof that is 1 300 of its 1 635 minor collections,
6.5 % of its cycles in the collections alone and 10 % with the sort. D-0191's L4 fixed the same
pattern in `Pb_analysis.lits_array`.

The fix sorts an `int array` of pair indices with the same comparison and then writes the pairs
back from a copy. No tuple is allocated and no array holds a pointer, so nothing forces a
collection. The result is the same bytes: two pairs that compare equal are equal pairs, so the
order among them cannot show. The change is in `justify.ml` only.

### 4. Measured after, and the gate

Release binary at `5bbe225` (4 M words, since no limit applies under `systemd-run -p MemoryMax`)
against `0518dc2`'s `9956c047`, on the same 46 runs as §1:

- **Byte-identical**: stdout, the `.pbp`/`.opb` md5 and every `--stats` line other than the times,
  on all 46 runs.
- **Instructions** (deterministic): median -7.1 % without the proof and -11.7 % with it. Every run
  gains. The smallest gains are rcpsp_12 without the proof (-3.5 %) and perfect_square with it
  (-6.2 %). The largest is lot-sizing without the proof (-27.4 %), and soccer with the proof gains
  -17.5 %, `sort_pairs` included.
- **Cycles** (load 45 to 60, so noisy): median -7.0 % and -11.4 % in one campaign, -5.2 % and -7.3 %
  in a second one with a gate running beside it. f2, the longest run, gains -18 to -25 %.
- **The GC's share of the cycles** (perf): median 13.3 % to 8.7 % without the proof, 16.6 % to
  8.8 % with it. Promoted words fall 1.4 to 5.9 times. fox-geese stays at 35 %, which is the
  long PB rows of D-0191 and not the nursery.
- **Peak RSS**: +8 to +20 MB on the small runs (QR48 38 to 58 MB, rcpsp_12 with the proof 49 to
  68 MB). f3 with the proof goes from 174 to 132 MB, because less is promoted.
- **Under the lanes' 4 GB cap** the nursery is about 490 k words, worth -3.4 % and -4.1 % in
  instructions (§2's table).

Left as they are: allocation stays diffuse, and no other site reaches 1 % of the cycles on average.
`Store.first_mark_above`'s closure is about 0.2 %. The long-row allocation in `Pb_analysis` and
`Learned` on fox-geese belongs to D-0191's line.

**Gate** (fresh clone of `wave56-gc` at `8cf4345`, binary `16f96560`, against gate 86's `ba895ce2`):
`make check` rc 0 (207 models passed), 207 x 4 artefacts equal, lane 324/324, debug lane 311/311,
scaling ok. The first gate, at a quarter of the limit, had the same results except lane 323/324
(§2).

### 6. The answer

**`W = 0` is not at least as good everywhere.** It is better in total by a wide margin: +42 verified
complete answers, +119 incumbents, 146 fewer proof caps, 43 fewer refusals, a better rank in 6
editions and a worse one in none, +729 points. But the order encoding answers 14 instances that `W = 0`
does not, and keeps 10 incumbents that `W = 0` loses. So removing it outside the tests would lose
those answers today.

What favours order, as the input for a middle `W`:

- **one family carries most of it.** `nfc` gives 10 of the 14 lost complete answers. Its widest
  variables are 421 to 1 849 wide, which is the middle of the distribution, and it runs at a fifth of
  the nodes per second with 4.5 times the memory on bits. A middle `W` saves `nfc` only if `W` is
  above its widths (around 2 000). That gives back most of what the wide families gain in the 1 000 to
  10 000 band.
- **narrow variables.** Below width 100, bits costs about 6 % per node (median 0.94 in both bands),
  and `fox-geese-corn` (52) and `java-auto-gen` (65) lose an answer there. That band is cheap to put
  back on order with a small `W` (say 64 or 100), and it is where the ladder is short anyway.
- **memory on a few families.** `road-cons` (79x), `largescheduling` (8.5x), `nfc`, `network_50_cstr`,
  `fjsp` and `test-scheduling` grow their RSS on bits. In 2024 the heap guard then throws away a better
  incumbent (`harmony`, `community-detection`), which is all of that edition's loss.
- **`mapping` and `is`** are mixed. `mapping` runs 5 times more nodes per second on bits and still
  loses two complete answers and three incumbents, so its loss is not the per-node cost. It is what the
  search finds (the encodings give different propagation, and so a different tree).

The options for the default, which the user decides:

| option | consequence |
|---|---|
| (a) default `W = 0`, keep the order code | +729 points and +42 complete answers on this measurement. `nfc` and the other 4 instances are lost by default and come back with `--bits-above none`. Both paths stay in the code |
| (b) a middle `W` (64 or 100, a second run) | likely keeps (a)'s gains and gives back the narrow losses (`fox-geese-corn`, `java-auto-gen`). It does not give back `nfc`, `mapping` or `is` |
| (c) remove the order encoding outside the tests | the simplest code (Ciaran's point), and (a)'s numbers, with the 14 answers and 10 incumbents lost for good, and no switch to get them back |

**Recommendation**: (a) now, with `nfc` investigated as its own task before (c) is considered. One
family gives 10 of the 14 lost answers, and a per-family cause there may be a bug in the bits path
rather than a property of the encoding. A middle `W` is (b), not part of this task.

### 7. What this record does not show

- 93 pairs have no bits variable in `w0` (D-0130 §12). On them the two arms are the same solver, and
  their ratios (1.01 and 1.00) are this run's noise.
- The scores count a REFUSED as UNK, incumbent or not (182 such rows in `none`, 148 in `w0`). That
  harness rule penalises whichever arm hits the heap guard after finding a solution.
- veripb ran out of memory under the same 16 GiB cap on 12 proofs and ran past 3 600 s on 36 (both arms
  together). So 26 printed OPT or UNSAT in `none` and 12 in `w0` are not in the complete column, as in
  D-0133.
- The nodes per second include the encoding time in the wall. An arm that encodes faster looks faster
  per node on short runs.

## D-0200  [AUTONOME] hotfix: the M7-T8 heap budget was read only at the end of a major cycle, so a growing heap could reach the address-space limit between two readings. It is now also polled ten times a second of CPU against the last reading plus the major words allocated since, and confirmed by one forced cycle

Agent-heapguard, branch `wave56-heapguard`, 2026-11-21. Claim `hotfix`, no ROADMAP row. Runs and
scripts in `/scratch/arthur/wave56-heapguard-runs/`.

### 1. The cause

Under the Challenge harness (`--max-heap-mb 8192`, `ulimit -v` 16 GiB, MemoryMax 32G), four runs
died on `Fatal error: allocation failure during minor GC` or `Fatal error: exception Out of memory`
at 14.4 to 14.7 GB RSS instead of the M7-T8 refusal. Reproduced with main `f365c1e` (binary
`7c475a45`, the gate-88 binary) on 2013 proteindesign12 1HZ5, same flags and limits: rc 134 after
63 s, 14.5 GB RSS.

The guard read `Gc.quick_stat ().heap_words`, which on OCaml 5.1 is a snapshot taken at the end of
the last major cycle (the header of `check_heap_at` had already measured that it is 0 before the
first one). Both halves read it, the `Gc` alarm at each cycle end and the synchronous check at each
declaration. A cycle lasts longer the larger the heap is. A probe build that printed the snapshot
and `/proc/self/statm` at each alarm showed it on 1HZ5:

| CPU s | heap at the cycle end | RSS |
|---|---|---|
| 16.0 | 2 924 MB | 3.2 GB |
| 27.3 | 6 574 MB | 7.0 GB |
| 63 | (no cycle ended) | 14.5 GB, abort |

The heap grew by about 2 GB every 7 s and the next cycle had not ended when the address space ran
out. RSS tracks the heap figure at every alarm on 1HZ5, on 2017 groupsplitter u6g3pref0 and on 2015
is HgSWGJHxY5, so nothing outside the OCaml heap is involved. D-0198's larger minor heap is not the
cause either. The m10t5 series binary predates it and failed the same way, and main with
`OCAMLRUNPARAM=s=256k` aborts the same way on 1HZ5 (74 s, 16.3 GB RSS, the smaller minor heaps
reserving less of the address space).

### 2. The fix

- **An estimate between two cycle ends** (`Encoding.heap_estimate`). The heap cannot gain more
  words since the snapshot than were allocated into it since, by promotion or directly.
  `Gc.counters`'s third component counts exactly those and is live. So the snapshot plus the major
  words allocated since is an upper bound on the heap now, and it is tight while the heap grows (on
  1HZ5 between the two alarms above, the heap gained 3.65 GB and the major words 3.8 GB). The base
  pair is taken by the alarm at each cycle end.
- **The estimate only decides when to look** (`Encoding.heap_overrun`). Past the budget, it forces
  the current cycle to its end with `Gc.major` and the fresh snapshot decides. A run is refused on a
  cycle-end figure, which is the rule the alarm already had. The declaration check uses it too.
- **A CPU-time ticker** calls it (`bin/main.ml`, `SIGVTALRM` every 0.1 s of user time, handler
  `Encoding.poll_heap`), installed only under `--max-heap-mb`. It ends the run the way the alarm
  does, message and exit 5, wherever it lands.
- **`Out_of_memory` at the top level** (parse and solve) prints a resource message and exits 5. It
  is the one allocation failure that can be caught, a single large allocation the runtime could not
  map, which no reading of the heap sees coming.

### 3. The choices, and the two designs that were measured and dropped

| option | measured consequence |
|---|---|
| poll from the search's `stop` closure (node entry, every 128 runs, the trace) | 2017 groupsplitter u6g3pref0 `--no-proof`: the root propagation completed 127 runs in 42 s and grew the heap from 4.4 to 9.9 GB, one run short of the poll. The alarm refused at 9 876 MB, 10 939 MB with `s=256k`. No count of runs or nodes bounds the allocation between two polls |
| **poll on a CPU-time ticker** (kept) | 16 of 16 runs refused between 8 196 and 8 703 MB, see §4 |
| confirm with `Gc.full_major` before refusing (never stricter than the alarm) | 1HZ5 `--no-proof` sat at 8.8 GB RSS for 680 s, forcing a cycle every `limit / 16` words, 143 nodes in 683 s, never refused and never ending. Killed by its PID |
| **confirm with one `Gc.major`** (kept) | the alarm's rule. The same run is refused at 30 s |

Two parameters, both round rather than calibrated. The ticker period is 0.1 s, so the heap can
pass the budget by what the mutator allocates in a tenth of a second (a few hundred MB on these
runs, 6 % at most in §4). After a forced cycle finds the heap under the budget, the next one waits
for `limit / 16` more major words. Without that floor a run hovering under its budget would force a
cycle every few MB of promotion. With it, such a run can be caught up to a sixteenth past.

The poll ends the run from a signal handler, at an arbitrary point, as the alarm always has, with the
same partial proof that the refusal message already declares. Raising instead would have to unwind
through code that never agreed to handle it, the proof writer included (the alarm's own comment).

To revert, revert the `hotfix (D-0200)` commits of `wave56-heapguard`. No default changes, since
everything here is behind `--max-heap-mb`, except the `Out_of_memory` arm, which turns an rc 2
abort into an rc 5 message.

### 4. Measurements

Binary `34db2c68` (`3465a33`) unless stated, harness flags and limits, `--proof` and `--no-proof`,
default minor heap and `OCAMLRUNPARAM=s=256k`. Before is the m8t4b and m10t5 run directories.

| instance | before | after, 4 runs each |
|---|---|---|
| 2013 proteindesign12 1HZ5 | allocation failure, 14.5 GB | exit 5 at 8 203 to 8 678 MB, 30 to 51 s, RSS at most 8.9 GB |
| 2018 proteindesign12 2PCY | Out of memory, 14.4 GB | exit 5 at 8 210 to 8 703 MB, 32 to 56 s, RSS at most 9.1 GB |
| 2015 is HgSWGJHxY5 | allocation failure, 14.6 GB | exit 5 at 8 196 to 8 646 MB, 26 to 48 s, RSS at most 9.0 GB |
| 2017 groupsplitter u6g3pref0 | allocation failure (m10t5), 14.7 GB without the proof | exit 5 at 8 589 to 8 687 MB, 48 to 67 s, RSS at most 9.0 GB |

2PCY without any budget: main `7c475a45` dies on `Fatal error: exception Out of memory`, rc 2, and
this branch exits 5 with the `Out_of_memory` message (both at 14.4 GB RSS).

Cost (`perf stat -e instructions:u`, binary `c181478d`, which differs from `34db2c68` only on the
paths that fire and in a message), the 21 fast lane instances at their node budget with `--proof`.
Without `--max-heap-mb` the code executed is the old one (no timer, no handler, the declaration
check still matches `None` first), and the instructions move by at most 0.08 % (fox-geese, 0.014 %
when rerun with one proof path for both). With `--max-heap-mb 100000`, which never fires, the new
binary runs 0.01 to 0.39 % FEWER instructions than the old one, because the declaration check now
reads `Gc.counters` where it read `Gc.quick_stat`, which aggregates every domain's statistics
into a freshly allocated record. Against its own run without the budget, the new binary costs at most 0.19 %
(fox-geese) and 0.016 % elsewhere.

### 5. The tests

- `test_proof`: the estimate both ways at a budget 16 MB above the live heap. 32 MB kept alive is an
  overrun, and 48 MB that died before the last collection, which the estimate counts past the
  budget, is not one. Plus the `Out_of_memory` message's wording.
- `test_endtoend`: the CLI, a 10-into-9 pigeonhole over clauses (Boolean cells, 0.3 s) under
  `OCAMLRUNPARAM=s=256k,o=100000`, a pacing that makes major cycles rare, at `--max-heap-mb 8`.
  Asserts exit 5, the wording, a heap of 8 to 12 MB and no runtime abort. Main `7c475a45` exits 5
  at 16 MB there (and 0 without `s=`, the budget never enforced), this branch at 9 MB on 30 runs of
  30.

### 6. What this does not cover

- A single allocation larger than what is left of the address space. It surfaces as
  `Out_of_memory` and §2's arm, or, inside a minor collection, as the uncatchable abort.
- Phases that allocate faster than a few GB per second of CPU, where a tenth of a second is more
  than the headroom. The harness's budget at half of `ulimit -v` leaves 8 GB on these runs.

### 3. What a middle `W` changes, instance by instance

**Won back from `w0` (64 and 100 alike)**: `2016_java-auto-gen_plusexample_6`,
`2024_fox-geese-corn_foxgeesecorn_61`, `2018_mapping_full2x2_mp3`, `2018_mapping_mesh3x3_mp3_2` (OPT
VERIFIED in `none`, `w64`, `w100`, TIMEOUT in `w0`), and `2018_mapping_ring_mp3` (OPT in `w64` and
`w100` only). `w100` also keeps `2019_hrc_exp2-1-5145`. Their widest variables are under 100 (or the
variables bits would take are), which is D-0175 §6's narrow band.

**Not won back**: all 10 `nfc` (OPT VERIFIED in `none`, TIMEOUT with the same or a worse objective in
the three bits arms). At `W = 100` each still puts 13 to 39 variables on bits, its widths being 421
to 1 849. Also the `mapping` mesh instances of 2015, 2016 and 2021, the `is`, `nside` and
`proteindesign12` incumbents (REFUSED by the heap guard in all three bits arms), and `2016_mapping_ring_1`.

**Lost against `w0`**: of the 15 complete answers `w0` gives on the sample, `w64` and `w100` lose 4.
`2017_steelmillslab_bench_14_1`, `_16_10` and `2019_steelmillslab_bench_20_8` (OPT 0 in `w0` within 360
to 943 s, TIMEOUT or REFUSED at 16 to 44 in the three others. Half of steelmillslab's 223 bits variables
are 64 wide or narrower, and they are the ones that help), and `2013_radiation_i7-15` (OPT in `w0`, no
solution at all in `none`, `w64` and `w100`). The fifth difference, `2022_gfd-schedule`, is OPT in all
four arms and only the check differs. `nside` loses its one `w0`-only complete answer
(`2019_nside_EASY_200_50`) too.

So on complete answers a middle `W` nets +4 (`w64`) or +5 (`w100`) on the 110 family instances (5 or 6
won back, `nside_EASY` lost) against -4 on 40 of the 170 sampled instances. Scaled to the pool, that
-4 is -17 if the sample is taken as uniform, and about -8 if steelmillslab, which was drawn whole, is
counted once (3, plus 1 in 37 over the other 167). So the net is -3 to -13 complete answers. The
Challenge score moves the same way: +23 for a middle `W` on the families, -10.6 on the sample, which is
about -45 over the pool, so about -20 net in `w0`'s favour (rough, the per-family clustering is not
modelled). Both estimates carry the sample's noise, and neither reaches
a sign that a middle `W` is better.

`w64` and `w100` differ on one instance (`hrc_exp2-1-5145`, a check that ran out of veripb's memory).

### 4. A finding on the way: 24 ERROR rows where D-0175 had REFUSED

On 6 instances per arm (`proteindesign12`, `is`), the solver dies with `Fatal error: allocation failure
during minor GC` at a peak RSS of 14.2 to 14.7 GB. That is under the 16 GiB `ulimit -v`, and
`--max-heap-mb 8192` should have stopped the run first. In D-0175 (binary `492638b9`) the same instances
ended REFUSED by the heap guard (exit 5). The guard's Gc alarm runs at the end of a major cycle. With
D-0198's larger minor heap, it seems the RSS can outrun the alarm. This changes no score (REFUSED and
ERROR are both UNK), but the heap guard no longer bounds the RSS it promises. It belongs to D-0198's
owner, as a task.

### 5. The decision

| option | consequence on this measurement |
|---|---|
| keep `none` (today) | the 10 `nfc` and 4 narrow answers kept; D-0175's -42 complete answers, -119 incumbents, +146 proof caps and -729 points stay |
| **`W = 0`** | D-0175's gains whole. Loses `nfc` (10) and the 4 narrow answers, which `--bits-above none` gives back. One representation for every eligible variable, the step toward Ciaran's all-bits code |
| `W = 64` | gives back `java-auto-gen`, `fox-geese-corn` and 3 `mapping` instances, and not `nfc`. Loses 4 of the 15 sampled `w0` complete answers (`steelmillslab` 3, `radiation`), about 10 or more over the pool. Two representations stay in the default path |
| `W = 100` | as `W = 64`, plus one `hrc` check. The best score on this order-biased set (345.6 against 332.3), but behind `W = 0` once the sample is weighted to its pool |

**Recommendation: `W = 0`** (D-0175's option (a)), with the order encoding kept behind `--bits-above none`
and in the tests. No `W` gets back what order wins most, `nfc`, because its widths (421 to 1 849) sit
where bits pays elsewhere (D-0175 §4). A middle `W` that saved `nfc` (about 2 000) would give back most
of the gain in the 1 000 to 10 000 band. A small middle `W` gets back 5 narrow answers and pays for them
with 8 to 17 on `w0`'s side (`steelmillslab` shows that the band under 64 is not
uniformly order's). It also keeps two representations in the default path, against the simplicity
asked for. The next lever is `nfc` itself: why bits runs it at a fifth of the nodes per second with
4.5 times the memory (D-0175 §4) is a task, and a per-family cause there may be a bug in the bits path.

### 2. `make check` at the new default, and what the tests needed

The first `make check` after A had 63 failing checks. 62 of them were in eight unit suites
(`test_flatzinc`, `test_ladder`, `test_compile`, `test_prop`, `test_learn`, `test_endtoend`, `test_trace`,
`test_mutation`), and one was the self-test of `check_unlimited.sh`. Each one names something only the
order encoding has. Examples are the `x_ge_v` rungs of a hand-written `rup` line (I-X10's accept-side
control, `trace_settle_*`), the ladder rows a PB row is lifted onto (`test_ladder` b/d), the consistency
clause that comes first in `bool2int`'s rows, an order-width cap that a bits variable does not reach
(`--max-order-width`, `test_flatzinc`'s width cap), and the conflict counts of `test_learn`'s scenes. In
each of them the break lane's target exists only on the ladder. Each suite now sets
`Encoding.bits_above := None` before any test runs, `check_unlimited.sh` exports `BAGUETTE_BITS_ABOVE=none`,
and no assertion changed. A bits test still sets its own `W` and restores the pin.

**Model tests**: 207 of 207 print the same stdout and exit code at `W = 0` as at `W = none`, so
`test/expected/` is unchanged and no solution needed an independent check. The proofs differ (§6).
`run_model_tests.sh`'s second pass ran the `bits_*` models at `--bits-above 0`, which is now the main
pass. It now runs every model at `--bits-above none` instead. The proof is verified, the verdict is the
default run's, and the `--no-proof` identity is checked (207 of 207). Without this pass the order
encoding would have left the model lane, against D-0199's "order kept in the tests".

### 7. How to revert

- One run: `--bits-above none` (or `BAGUETTE_BITS_ABOVE=none`). §3 and §6 show that this is the solver before D-0201, byte for byte.
- The default: `git revert` A, C and D together. A alone would leave C's references and D's baseline
  recorded at `W = 0`, so the lane would fail and parity-learning's growth would be OVER. B and E are
  correct at either default, because they pin the order encoding where a test needs it. They can stay,
  or be reverted too (`git revert 3e1d67e 29d2c08 d53ce76 5f0dc7a 18d4841`).

### 8. What it leaves

D-0199 §5's open lever is `nfc`: it is OPT under the order encoding and TIMEOUT under bits, at a fifth
of the nodes per second with 4.5 times the memory. `--bits-above none` gives it back per run. The eight pinned
unit suites keep testing what they tested before, which is the order encoding plus their explicit
bits tests. The model lane, the differential lane and the e2e chain test both encodings.

### 5. [AUTONOME] Does the default stay fixed (D-0154)?

**It stays.** The brief's criterion was "unless B wins nearly everywhere". By edition score B
wins 15 of 16. By instance it wins 489 and loses 336, and by family 139 against 90. So it wins on
aggregate and is far from winning everywhere. D-0154's reason was never performance. The default
follows the model's annotation, as the fixed category and a MiniZinc user expect, and `-f` is one
flag away. Nothing in the solver changes here.

**Proposal for the user** (no change made):

| option | consequence |
|---|---|
| keep fixed by default (recommended) | the annotation is followed, the Challenge's fixed category is what a plain run does, and users who want the stronger aggregate pass `-f`, which the README documents |
| make `-f` the default | +28 % summed score in fixed-category scoring and +39 verified answers on this binary, but 336 instances get worse, 64 more instances reach the heap budget, and the fixed-category entry needs a flag to turn it off |
| keep fixed, and let `minizinc -f` choose free search | already the case: `-f` is in `stdFlags` of `tools/baguette.msc`, so MiniZinc passes it through |

To revert this decision there is nothing to revert, because no code changed. To take the second
option, change the default in `bin/main.ml` in its own commit and re-record the lanes.

**Reading.**

1. **No proof was rejected, none hit a checker memory failure or a timeout**: all 30 proofs are
   `s VERIFIED` (partial proofs of stopped runs included), the largest check 270 s.
2. **`-f` against default.** QR48 2.1x the time (23 367 to 50 325 nodes), QR72 def 1.9x (222 s
   against 117 s) and QR72 u1 3.5x (209 s against 59 s), the nodes doubling.
   o7k2 def, a timeout for default in 600 s (151 440 nodes), is refuted in 27 s (14 869 nodes, 30
   restarts); with proof 37 s, 229 MB. o7k2 u1 is the annotation and unchanged (2 s, 0 restarts). This is
   D-0137's finding on the new default encoding, and the Challenge's: the free search wins where
   the fixed search is wrong and loses 2x where it is right.
3. **`tiered` alone is a wash.** Node counts equal default (QR48 identical, QR72 within 6 of 100 685).
   QR72 def is faster (70 s against 117 s, 103 s against 156 s with proof), QR72 u1 12 % faster, QR48
   equal. o7k2 def still times out (more nodes per second, 234 k against 151 k). Proofs are the same
   size where nothing is evicted. It does not change an answer.
4. **`-f` + `tiered` is worse than `-f`.** QR48 doubles again (44 s against 21 s, 82 k nodes
   against 50 k, 126 restarts against 88) and QR72 times out in both (511 k nodes, 566 restarts),
   where `-f` alone finishes in 210 to 270 s. o7k2 def is the same as `-f` (26 s). The restarts
   re-enter the nodes `tiered` has evicted lemmas for. D-0139's finding that `tiered` costs
   more conflicts (+116 % on `opd`) shows here once a restart repeats work.
5. **`--bits-above none` against default** (D-0201's pair, this binary): node counts equal on all
   five instances that finish, times 1 to 4 % apart (QR72 def 115 s against 117 s), so the
   codes set is insensitive to the encoding. o7k2 def times out on both (104 k and 151 k nodes).
   Against D-0137's `base` rows (QR48 23 367 nodes, QR72 100 685 and 101 435, o7k2 u1 158)
   the node counts are identical; times are 2.5x to 4x lower (release build, D-0171, and a less
   loaded node), o7k2 u1 172 nodes against 158 (the D-0201 default, and 157 under `-f`).

**Proposal (not applied).** Keep the fixed search as default (D-0154, D-0185 section 5) and keep
`keep_all`. The codes set confirms D-0185: `-f` is the free-category setting, 2x on the instances
the fixed search already solves, and the only arm that refutes o7k2 def. `tiered` gains nothing here
and breaks `-f`, so it stays off, and `-f` should not be combined with it. Nothing to revert.

## D-0204  The user's decisions of 2026-11-23: past decisions are reopened by measurement, the 16 GB proof cap goes, and the roadmap turns to coverage, configuration and speed

**Status**: DECIDED by the user (2026-11-23), recorded by the orchestrator.

**Context.** The Challenge series of D-0185 ranks baguette last or next to last in most editions,
with or without proof. The user's words: decisions taken in the past may no longer fit the present
situation, and if staying on the fixed search is bad, it has to go. MiniZinc has no certified track
yet, so the Challenge's conventions do not bind a solver that logs proofs.

**Decisions.**
1. A default is chosen by measurement on the M17 series, not by the Challenge convention. D-0154
   (the default search stays fixed) is reopened, and M19-config-T1 decides it from the numbers.
2. The 16 GB proof cap of the harness (`PROOF_CAP_KB`, D-0133's settings) is removed from our
   series. The time limit (1 200 s) stays, so scores stay comparable with the official entrants.
   CAPPED disappears as an outcome. The series of D-0203 was told to restart without it.
3. The roadmap gains three milestones, in this order of priority: M18-coverage (the globals that
   reach baguette decomposed, and the third of the Challenge that is refused before search),
   M19-config (the ideas of other solvers, each behind a flag and measured, to find the best
   configuration), M20-pernode (code speed, after M16).

**Revert.** Point 2 is a harness setting (`bench/series/`, `scripts/compare_run.sh`), not solver
code. Point 1 changes nothing until M19-config-T1 measures.

## D-0205  [AUTONOME] M19-config-T0: the tuning set, 200 Challenge instances drawn by a rule, and the protocol for comparing an idea

**Status**: DECISION on a measurement tool, recorded 2026-11-23 (agent-tuning, branch `wave59-tuning`).
No campaign was run, the set is computed from D-0185's rows (binary `7c880bce`, 1 200 s, three arms).

**Context.** M19-config rows each need an on/off table, and a full series costs two days. Options:
(a) the full 1 574 instances at 300 s, about 12 h per arm pair at 87 processes, no choice to make;
(b) a random 200, cheap but most draws are all-timeout or trivial, so it cannot separate ideas;
(c) a stratified draw weighted toward instances where configuration matters. Chosen: (c), because
D-0185 shows 749 of 1 574 instances tie between A and B.

**Rule** (code `bench/tuning/draw_set.py`, details `bench/tuning/README.md`): candidate = in all
three arms, no FLATTEN-FAIL, not refused by all, not complete within 10 s in every arm. Tier 1
contested, 2 hard with an incumbent, 3 solved by all over 10 s, 4 nothing to compare. Round r gives
each family (problem name) its r-th best instance by (tier, md5 of id). Result: 1 222 candidates,
183 families, 200 instances, tiers 164/15/6/15, 17 families have two instances and the rest one.
Re-draw: the command in the README; the same inputs give the same list. A re-draw is a new
D-record, because it changes what past tuning rows were measured on.

**Protocol**: 300 s, with and without proof, a flag against the default of the day, score and
complete/incumbent counts by `agreement.py`, status changes listed, per-family reading in aggregate.
The subset proposes, the full series decides, and their verdicts must agree in sign.

**Validation against D-0185** (`agreement.py`): subset and full set both rank C > B > A on the 1 200 s
rows (shares 0.391/0.367/0.242 vs 0.403/0.337/0.260); B over A is 94+/56- (subset) against 489+/336-
(full). The subset narrows C against B (gap 0.024 vs 0.066). On the same rows cut at 300 s (an
optimistic cut) the subset ranks B and C level (0.372 vs 0.369, order B > C) where the full set has
C ahead (0.395 vs 0.339). The set separates A from B and from C, and does not separate B from C at
300 s, so a gap under about 0.03 of the share between two arms is noise.
**Limits**: tier 4 takes 15 slots to keep every attempted family, which costs resolution; the
set is validated on D-0185's configurations, not on future ideas (restarts, new phases), where the
agreement is unknown until the first full series (M17) repeats a row.

**Revert**: delete `bench/tuning/`; nothing else depends on it.

## D-0207  M20-pernode-T1: where the factor per node goes, on five families and the same tree. Without learning baguette is 6 to 55 times Gecode per node, and learning that never backjumps multiplies that by 1.4 to 60. Five ranked levers for T2 to T5

**Status**: DONE (measurement only, no `lib/` or `bin/` change on the branch), recorded 2026-11-23 by
agent-pernode2 (`wave59-pernode2`). Measured on `fataepyc-06` while the Challenge series of
2026-11-23 ran at 87 processes (load 2.5 to 89, given per run in `out/*.load`). Every comparison is
in instructions (`perf stat -e instructions:u`) and in `perf` sample shares, never in wall time.
Runs, scripts and tables in `/cluster/arthur/baguette-results/pernode2/`.

### 1. Method

**Binaries.** Main `3dc1a81`, `make release` (D-0171): `f244c35a` (column B). A MEASUREMENT binary,
`a49b56ea` (column NL), is the same source plus three lines in `bin/main.ml` (`nolearn.patch`,
never committed) that read `BAGUETTE_LEARN=off` into `Search.config.learn = false` and `pb = false`,
the `Search.no_learning` configuration the unit tests already use. Its proofs are checked
(`rcpsp11_60` without learning, 33 945 nodes, `s VERIFIED UNSATISFIABLE`). Without it no comparison
on the same tree exists, because baguette always learns and Gecode never does. Profiles use the same
two sources built release on the `baguette-fp` switch (D-0145): `e9d6889e` and `a2bad1e4`.
Gecode 6.4.0 and Chuffed 0.14.0 from the MiniZinc 2.10.1 bundle, each on its own flattening.

**Same tree.** Every model has a complete search annotation and no restart (Chuffed `--restart
none`). An optimisation model becomes a satisfaction model with the objective bounded below its
optimum, so the tree is a refutation. Where the tree is too large it is cut at the same node count
(Gecode `-node L`, baguette `BAGUETTE_NODE_LIMIT=L`), and the failure count at the cut is the check
that the prefix is the same. Chuffed `--lazy off` is Chuffed without explanations or learning (0
backjumps on every family), Chuffed LCG is its default with `--restart none`. Chuffed has no node
limit, so it runs to a time limit and its own count is used. Chuffed LCG counts decisions as nodes
(the right side of a refuted left branch is an implied literal), so its node figure below is nodes
+ failures, which equals Gecode's on QR48 where both trees agree.

**Per node.** (I - I_base) / (N - N_base), the base being the same command stopped at one node
(Gecode `-node 1`, baguette `BAGUETTE_NODE_LIMIT=1`) or at 1 ms (Chuffed `-t 1`, whose own node count
is subtracted). Parsing, compiling and the `.opb` are out.

**Layers.** `perf record -F 499 --call-graph fp`, each sample to the first layer whose frames match,
in this order (`tools/layers.py`): kernel, GC, setup (no `Search` frame, removed and the rest
renormalised), proof (`Baguette_proof.*`, `Justify`, `Trace`), conflict analysis and learning
(`Learn`, `Analysis`, `Pb_analysis`, `Reduce`, `Retention`, `Learned`, `Ladder`, the `Search` learning
entry points, and the branch nogood `Search.combine_nogoods` without learning), learned-constraint
propagation (`Clause.propagate` and the learned watches, plus `Pb` on the two families whose `Pb` runs
can only be learned PB rows), explanation construction (`Explanation`, `Order_reason`, the `Store`
support queries), model propagation by the first propagator module on the stack (so a `Domain` or
`Store` write made by a propagator is that propagator's, and so is a reason it builds inline), backtrack,
engine (queue, wake walk, dispatch, `Store.run_as`), search. Layer x instructions per node is the
attribution, as in D-0169.

### 2. The five families

| family | instance | baguette's flattening | tree (G = Gecode, CN = Chuffed --lazy off, NL, B) |
|---|---|---|---|
| clauses | codes-cp QR48, 3 fixed (D-0169's `f3.fzn`, `g_f3.fzn`) | 1 134 `bool_clause`, 48 `bool2int`, 2 `int_lin_le` | full, UNSAT: 29 779 nodes in all four, 14 890 failures |
| alldiff | 2011 costas-array, n = 14 | 14 `all_different_int`, 157 `int_lin_eq`, 1 `int_lin_le` | to the first solution: G and CN 21 509, NL 21 425 (-0.4 %), B 21 129 (-1.8 %) |
| linear | 2014 multi-knapsack `mknap2-1` (60 x 0/1, 30 rows, objective `= z`) | 30 `int_lin_le`, 1 `int_lin_eq` (the objective) | cut at 20 000 nodes: G 9 994 failures, NL and B 9 994 |
| element | 2013 javarouting `trip_6_3`, objective <= 66 (optimum 67) | 97 `array_int_element`, reified comparisons, 1 `all_different` | cut at 20 000 nodes: G 9 999 failures, NL and B 9 998 |
| cumulative | 2013 rcpsp `11`, makespan <= 60 (optimum 77) | 4 `cumulative`, 329 `int_lin_le_reif` + 329 `bool_clause` (the disjunctions), 82 `int_lin_le` | full, UNSAT: CN and NL 33 945 nodes. Gecode 17 (its `cumulative` adds edge-finding), B 71 (learning backjumps, 4 skipped) |

The fifth family has no same tree with Gecode, so its same-tree reference is Chuffed `--lazy off`,
and Gecode's figure is its own tree at makespan <= 66 (1 665 999 nodes, full). B is measured on that
bound too (2 010 nodes, 73 backjumps) against Chuffed LCG (2 483 node-equivalents), two learning trees
that are close but not equal.

On the first four families the default solver **never backjumps** (`skipped 0`) and its tree is the
no-learning tree, to 1.8 % on costas. Learning buys no node there.

### 3. Instructions per node

Thousands of instructions per node. The factor is against Gecode on the same tree (rcpsp: against
Chuffed `--lazy off` on the same tree, Gecode's own tree in brackets). `--bits-above none` changed no
figure by more than 0.02 % (QR48 and mknap have no wide variable, costas's differences and the
others' are small), so it is one column here and the per-run values are in `summary.tsv`.

| family | Gecode | Chuffed --lazy off | Chuffed LCG | NL --no-proof | NL proof | B --no-proof | B proof (shipped) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| QR48 | 28.0 | 15.9 | 31.9 | 437 (16x) | 1 212 (43x) | 1 044 (37x) | 1 841 (66x) |
| costas 14 | 108 | 154 | 276 | 5 871 (55x) | 15 188 (141x) | 44 736 (416x) | 54 119 (503x) |
| mknap2-1 | 69.4 | 32.2 | 62.8 | 667 (9.6x) | 1 205 (17x) | 40 298 (581x) | 41 080 (592x) |
| javarouting | 213 | 143 | 257 | 8 253 (39x) | 18 586 (87x) | 12 586 (59x) | 24 548 (115x) |
| rcpsp 11 | (149) | 92.7 | 150 (bound 66) | 885 (9.5x) | 7 331 (79x) | 2 636 (bound 66) | 10 201 (bound 66) |

Read across a row, the factor has three parts that multiply. The propagation core without learning
or proof is 6 to 55 times Gecode. The proof multiplies it by 1.8 to 8.3 (NL proof over NL
--no-proof). Learning, on trees where it never backjumps, multiplies it by 1.5 (javarouting), 2.4
(QR48), 7.6 (costas) and 60 (mknap). For comparison Chuffed's learning costs it 1.8 to 2.0 per node
(LCG over `--lazy off`, on its own trees except QR48).

|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| model propagation | 168 | 157 | 172 | 5 243 | 5 150 | 4 012 | 472 | 362 | 6 360 | 5 619 | 6 104 | 641 | 549 | 1 405 |
| engine (queue, wake, dispatch) | 196 | 361 | 394 | 381 | 345 | 11 483 | 102 | 16 323 | 1 086 | 1 021 | 1 943 | 175 | 191 | 533 |
| learned-constraint propagation | 0 | 264 | 222 | 0 | 0 | 26 161 | 0 | 21 358 | 0 | 0 | 967 | 0 | 0 | 315 |
| conflict analysis + learning | 30 | 170 | 200 | 23 | 31 | 1 735 | 58 | 1 068 | 44 | 52 | 2 085 | 15 | 19 | 421 |

| proof (justify, trace, writer) | 1 | 8 | 683 | 32 | 7 582 | 196 | 2 | 116 | 15 | 8 854 | 9 278 | 2 | 4 575 | 5 404 |
